Then we found ourselves behind again.

When Becks scored, I thought we still had to win the game.

So I ran and got the ball while everybody else was over in the corner celebrating as if we’d won the match.

I was running back to the halfway line with the ball under my arm shouting, ‘Come on, come on, we need another goal!’



But someone had obviously passed word on to the pitch that we only needed a draw to qualify.

We ended up drawing the match and Becks got acclaimed for an absolute worldie of a free-kick and rightly so.

I said to Becks at the time, ‘You’ve had five free-kicks already today. You’ve hit the wall, you’ve hit Row Z, you scuttled one along the floor. I’ll have it if you don’t want it’.

That was more what I was saying to him and his response to me was, ‘You can’t even reach from here, Ted, so leave it to me’.

I knew he was the kingpin. I could do that every now and again but he could do that seven or eight times out of ten.



But you never know, it might have just focused his mind to put me in my place.

He practised them day in, day out and more often than not, he put the ball exactly where he wanted it.

That’s what he did at the right time — and got us out of a bit of trouble again.



MATT BELL (England fan)

ON the drive home from Munich after England’s memorable 5-1 win over Germany back in September 2001, I said to my pals: “I bet we cock-up now against Albania or Greece.”

The then 35 years of hurt instilled that pessimism.

But I still didn’t really expect that, just a month later, we’d be relying on a last-gasp David Beckham free-kick to seal the point we needed against the Greeks for World Cup qualification.

It’s just one of those standout moments in my years of following England that I’ll never forget.

Stood behind the goal, aware the clock was ticking, I then turned to my mates and said: “If anyone can do this now, it’s Beckham.”



That day at Old Trafford he was immense. I’d go as far as to say he produced one of the best individual performances I’ve witnessed from an England player — particularly while being surrounded by a number of poor performances from team-mates.

At one stage, Becks even felt the need to tackle one of our own defenders, just to get the ball and move it quickly up the pitch.

So as he stood over the ball for THAT free-kick, I just felt certain that he would score.

But it didn’t dilute my celebrations after the ball hit the net — sending me wildly jumping up and down, losing my mobile phone and ending up several rows forward from where I had been stood.

I’m pleased to say that I did manage to retrieve my phone but I wouldn’t have cared in all the euphoria.



And, ever since, I’ve always had an instinct to defend Beckham from any criticism of his ability.

NIKOS DABIZAS (Greek defender)

WE HAD a new manager [Otto Rehhagel] so we wanted to perform well to impress him.

We hadn’t had the best result when we played Finland away, we lost and got battered [5-1] then you had this difficult game against England.



It was a difficult and strange evening because England had to win or draw and they were depending on another result, but we didn’t think anything of that. We just wanted to go out and represent our country, and that was the most important mission that we had.

When we scored again to go 2-1 ahead you obviously think, ‘Okay, now it’s maybe it’s the day that we can create a shock.’ England had a very good team, a lot of young, good players. So it felt like a spark that maybe something was going to happen.

It went well, we held on, and then obviously that free kick came and changed everything.

I guess it was one of those decisions that always goes with the home side.

The referee basically took the whole nation out of jail. Don’t take anything away from the free-kick — but the actual decision was shocking.



You couldn’t believe it but the free-kick was quality. The decision-making to place it in that specific corner . . . it was genius.

David did that throughout his career. But what makes that goal so special is it was the moment — the exact second — that England qualified.

The Three Lions would have been eliminated. So that’s what makes the kick, the moment, the goal, so special.

You couldn’t say that it was going in from that split-second he kicked it but when it was in the later stages, you could understand it was going in.

You have to hold your hands up and accept it as it was a pure masterclass in terms of hitting and getting the direction of the ball with that end product.



When you see it hit the back of the net, it was just a huge disappointment. It was the last stage of the game.

You don’t have anything to prevent or change that moment, change the direction of the ball. You can’t do anything about it.

You know you are just witnessing that moment — and it’s pure disappointment.

Obviously, it gave pure joy to England but it was a disappointing feeling for us as we didn’t have the chance to create that shock.

Yet, looking back now, sometimes you have to hold your hands up and say, ‘Listen, this was a masterclass of hitting the ball, placing it in that corner with the right angle and specification’. Everything was perfect.



You just had to hold your hands up and accept it.

MARTIN TYLER (Commentator)

DAVID BECKHAM had taken FIVE free-kicks already in this game.

And, while 25 years may have slightly clouded my memory, I do recall thinking that each time it felt like they were getting closer!



But, for football’s most famous player at that time to produce a performance and a goal under those circumstances was truly extraordinary.

It was even more prophetic for him as it was at Old Trafford — where he was adored — and if anyone knew the dimensions of his home pitch to convert a free-kick like that it would be him.

Beforehand everyone fully expected Germany to beat Finland and England to win against Greece in these last group games.

That would have seen Three Lions safely through to the World Cup finals the following summer on goal difference.

Yet neither happened as Finland surprisingly got a 0-0 draw in Gelsenkirchen.



What we didn’t know then but we found out three years later was that Greece would win the Euros — shocking everyone by beating hosts Portugal in the final.

Both England’s goals that day were from set-pieces and, as Greece proved in summer 2004, they gave very little away.

A key asset in TV commentary is a touchline reporter feeding us information of what is happening in the technical areas and giving us a heads-up on changes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Yet, by the time I had been told Teddy Sheringham would be replacing Robbie Fowler in the 67th minute, he was on and had nodded home the equaliser — ten seconds after coming on. But Greece were ahead again just two minutes later through Demis Nikolaidis.

With the minutes slipping away and the idea that England were set to end up in the nail-biting play-offs, up stepped Becks and a perfect free-kick to write his own narrative that even 25 years ago is a wonderful moment to talk about.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte appears to makes subtle pitch for Man Utd job as pressure mounts on Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

ANTONIO CONTE declared that he wants to join a club that has “lost sight of its history” amid Manchester United links.

Red Devils boss Michael Carrick is already under fire following an underwhelming start to the season.



United entered the extended international break 12th in the table after drawing 1-1 at winless Fulham.

Carrick’s men have also looked poor in games against Hull, Manchester City and Brighton so far this term.



Conte, 57, is out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer.

The Italian won the Premier League with Chelsea in the 2016-17 campaign, in addition to being the only manager since Mauricio Pochettino to guide Tottenham into the top four.



Speaking to The Athletic, Conte outlined his burning desire to win – as well as revealing what he’s looking for in his next project.

He said: “If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself — a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories — you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back — if it isn’t there today — to fight for those goals.

“I know full well that only one team can win every year, but I must carry in my heart — and instil in the hearts of the fans, my players and my directors — that spark, that hope that makes you say, ‘F***, we can win’.

“Even that one per cent — but it must be a one per cent that can become 70, 80 or even 100 per cent. It depends on how you convey it.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“The manager is important, because he conveys that message, day in, day out.

“He has daily interactions with everyone: with his staff, the masseur, the kit man, the physiotherapist, the groundsman — all people who need to be involved and feel part of the drive to make history, and you only make history by winning.

“There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I’d like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.

“Clubs where there’s pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you’re not going there just to take part, but to compete.”

Man Utd have won a joint-record 20 league titles, but are on a 13-year drought since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure in 2013.



In that period alone, Conte has won leagues with Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli.

Carrick, 45, took over as United’s interim boss in January following Ruben Amorim‘s departure and guided his team to a third place finish.

This led to him landing the job on a permanent basis.

United return to action this Saturday as they host another of Conte’s former clubs Spurs.

On his time with the North Londoners, Conte added: “I remember we weren’t winning or we’d drawn a game and I sent Daniel Levy a message.

Sports.title: White's Dorking have new co-owners - and ambitions to become 'the world's local club'
Sports.content:
Football needs charismatic characters - and Marc White is certainly one of those.

It is more than likely you will have seen one of his rants go viral on social media. In that respect, he is one of a kind.

But he also has no equal in the way that he set up Dorking Wanderers with a group of friends in 1999 - and is still there, 27 years on. The chairman, the manager, the face of the club.

After a recent FA Cup second qualifying round win over Southall FC, he posted from the club's X account: "Thanks for tonight to all of our loyal supporters & never forget we were in Crawley & District Division 5. Step 17."

It has been a long, long journey. One that has cost millions and taken in an incredible 12 promotions.

Dorking finished 16th in the National League in 2022/23 - their best ever finish and the closest they have come to the EFL, which is the stated goal. At this point, why would it not be?

Currently, they are back in the National League South - but now White has significant additional backing.

US entrepreneur Frank Villares had first become involved in Dorking in 2024, through the 'Rise With Us' campaign, which allowed the public to buy shares in the club to help them achieve their goals. A £180,013 target was set, with £333,180 the actual figure raised by 746 investors.

In the summer, he and his wife Debra Tucker were announced as co-owners and growth investors.

"Frank and Debra are massive English football fans and there's this huge enthusiasm for the English pyramid in the US as that's the one thing the US money can't buy," says White, speaking to Sky Sports in a room overlooking the club's Meadowbank home.

"They were actually looking around for a bigger interest in a club. They wanted to be more involved and I was actually helping them with that, telling them what to watch out for.

"They'd gone to four or five clubs and a deal fell through last minute so I just said: 'Don't forget, there's always Dorking Wanderers!' It just felt like everything had gone wrong for a positive reason. Then they were like, 'You know what, we've already said to ourselves we love Dorking, why are we even doing this?!'

Image: White (centre) with co-owners and growth investors Frank Villares and Debra Tucker

"They are both 40 plus VAT and they're in a position now in life where they want to really enjoy and have a project and they want to win - Frank has even put a picture of the team at Wembley, an AI job, on his vision board!

"They're perfect because they trust us to run it, but they want to be involved as well. This is just the beginning."

In addition to Villares and Tucker, a consortium led by former professional ice hockey player James Sixsmith acquired a shareholding in the summer.

"We want to surround this club with people that want to succeed and want to win and James is very similar," adds White.

"We're really lucky. James and Daryl [Cumberland] from his consortium are part of that mechanism behind it all. As we go up the divisions and as we find more success, their involvement will become greater and greater.

"I want to say to the people involved: 'Listen, here's the thing. If we put in another X million, we could actually get to the Championship or we can build a stadium and we can do X, Y and Z. We've got big players in our setup that are going to enable us, not just financially, but also in terms of decision-making and having the right mindset towards growth.

"The legacy of Dorking Wanderers is to find a way to progress. What people love about the club is the underdog story of coming from nowhere to somewhere. We have to find a way for that to continue."

Image: Dorking have climbed from step 17 of the non-League pyramid to step 2 (Image: Dorking Wanderers)

What does that look like in practice?

"The investment has made things easier. But in football, everything you do, whether it's on or off the field, costs a lot of money. We're by no means set for life, not in a million years. We're just in a position where we can add some things, largely off the field.

"But that kind of off-field investment can generate more income, which we can invest on the field, hopefully. That's where the success cycle comes; win more games, more fans, promotion, more fans.

"There's not one football club in the world that really profits. You might get the odd one but, in general, someone somewhere is putting time, effort and money into a football club. Off the field is the largest part of the football club.

"You're in the entertainment business and you've only got one show a week normally. The rest is all hard work."

Speaking of, White is, naturally, one of the central figures on the YouTube channel Bunch of Amateurs, which documents all the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Dorking.

The channel currently has more than 200,000 subscribers and a global audience.

"We had half a billion unique views last year of the club. Half a billion. Ten times the average Premier League club. My thing is to part capitalise on that, but part deliver. Imagine what happens to that with more promotions?

"As a result, every single match there's someone from Australia, New Zealand or America. They'd be the three top places every game.

"I went down to Costa one morning to get a coffee. It opened at 7am and I looked like I'd just been f*****g dug up. Two people came in with these Dorking Wanderers shirts on. They were American and had just got off a flight and they couldn't believe they'd seen me.

"It's a bit surreal like that, but it's all positive. I like the recognition I get. I don't really get any bad words about me from anyone that knows the game. I quite like the recognition of the hard work that's gone into it because it would be easy just to think I just swear at refs. Obviously, there's a lot more to me!"

Throughout the interview, White keeps coming back to V2 - the next version of the club.

"V1 took us from the park fields to where we are today," he says. "Everything is teeing up this club to have a V2. We're better equipped now.

"I think we need to get promoted again really soon. Next year or two minimum. We then need to try and do a bit of a double and then try and break into the Football League.

"I think breaking into the Football League genuinely will make us one of the world's greatest sporting successes. As big as that sounds. I don't know f*****g any others!"

One potential obstacle is that, while White has been so successful at Dorking, he does not hold the coaching badges necessary to manage in the EFL.

"We'll take care of that, that's fine," he says. "The dream really is to be in there. I'd love it."

Image: Dorking's finished 16th in the National League 2022/23 - their highest finish to date (Image: Dorking Wanderers)

But the ambitions extend far beyond the EFL.

"I feel like we really want to be the whole world's local club," White says.

"We believe we're the pioneers of like real, relatable content with a local football team. It's given us this global stage and that trying to capitalise on that and people feeling like they belong to a local community, even if they live in Mississippi.

"Frank tells me he can't believe how many times he gets stopped in America - even in Texas, someone said to him 'I love Dorking!'.

"We want to just like continue to put the club on a global reach - and we identify with the fact that winning will be a part of that. So we have to find a way to win."

As for this season, Dorking are currently eighth in the National League South, three points behind leaders Maidstone United. A trip to Dover Athletic - a point and a place above them - beckons on Saturday.

"Standard stuff, really. Stressful. We've done alright. Loads of injuries, all that s**t. Standard modern football," says White as he picks up his bag, ready to dart to a podcast record.

"Dorking are always in the mix, so we'll be there again."

There is no time for sentimentality - only the next challenge.

Sports.title: Lifeline for LIV Golf with potential $300m investment
Sports.content:
LIV Golf has secured a potential $300m windfall from BC Partners Credit as it looks to continue into 2027.

The league lost its multi-billion-dollar funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) following the end of the 2026 campaign and filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States.

LIV hopes a court-supervised "restructuring process" can be completed early next year.

Current participants, who are owed millions of pounds, reportedly have no obligation to sign on for LIV 2.0 should it materialise.

Image: LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil says BC Partner Credit's investment can help the league become 'truly global'

Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, said in a statement: "Our goal is to facilitate LIV Golf's emergence from the restructuring process on sound financial footing and with renewed momentum heading into the 2027 season."

BC Partners Credit will support the next stage of LIV, under which players would become equity owners of the league and its teams.

Major winners Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Dustin Johnson are among the players who signed on with LIV following its creation in 2021 having been lured over from the PGA Tour.

Those golfers are some of the creditors listed with unsecured claims - Rahm heads that with 7.5m (£5.5m).

Image: Jon Rahm is one of the plyers owed millions of pounds

England's Tyrrell Hatton (£2.5m) is among the creditors as is five-time major winner Brooks Koepka (£1.25m), who quit LIV to re-join the PGA Tour earlier this year.

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil said: "This investment is an important ‌step forward for LIV Golf, and I want to thank Ted Goldthorpe and the entire BC Partners team for their conviction in what we're building.

"We believe ‌deeply in the future of this league and in the opportunity to build something distinctive alongside our players.

"We're delivering on our major milestones, and while there is still work ahead, today marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league that complements the wider game and creates new opportunities for players, fans, partners, and the next generation of golfers."

Sports.title: 'Painful as hell' - Norris uncertain McLaren can fix issue for Singapore
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has admitted he is unsure whether McLaren will be able to fix an issue with his car that is causing a loss of straight-line speed ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

The reigning world champion was in fine form as he claimed three pole positions and two victories in four races spread either side of the summer break, but he has since been off the pace in Azerbaijan and Malaysia.

Norris only qualified fifth at both events, was taken out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in a crash and could only manage ninth in an error-strewn display as Malaysia hosted the Bahrain Grand Prix.

McLaren are yet to discover the cause of the issue, which made Norris slower than his team-mate Oscar Piastri in certain parts of the Sepang International Circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Asked whether the team can fix it for the upcoming Sprint weekend in Singapore, Norris told Sky Sports F1: "I have no idea.

"The team are trying but I'm losing almost two tenths a lap. Two tenths a lap over 55 laps is just painful as hell. It's making my life pretty damn difficult.

"There are also other things. In Malaysia I could have done better. I can't just have that. That's not just an excuse.

"There are things I can do better and the team as well."

Stella: Rivals may have developed car with bigger steps

McLaren boss Andrea Stella admitted that some of the team's rivals may have "developed their car with bigger steps" after successive underwhelming showings.

The reigning constructors' champions appeared to be back in the mix for victories when their upgrade package at the Hungarian Grand Prix before the summer break helped Norris deliver the team's first grand prix pole and victory of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

However, despite McLaren having added more upgrades to their car, Mercedes' George Russell claimed a dominant win in Azerbaijan before Max Verstappen exhibited Red Bull's progress by triumphing in Malaysia.

Stella said: "We see a scenario in Formula 1 which seems to be changing pretty rapidly.

"In Hungary, we took some upgrades, and we were in condition to have a pole position in Hungary and Zandvoort and then we were in condition to do pole position and pretty much victory in Madrid without the Virtual Safety Car.

"Then very rapidly and interestingly, as we took upgrades as well, the picture changes.

"I think we have to take a look at our own development. We don't see any anomaly in our data, but we have to acknowledge that potentially some competitors have developed their car with bigger steps than we did."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Lando Norris took the Spanish Grand Prix pole with this sensational final lap.

The extremely high temperatures and rough track surface in Malaysia created a potential outlier in terms of conditions, which has left Stella with some hope that McLaren could return to form in Singapore.

"There are very specific conditions in Malaysia, so I think we should give ourselves more time," he added.

"I'm sure this is the same kind of review that we'll have next door at Mercedes. It's a very special condition in Malaysia, so I think we have to understand better the behaviour of the cars.

"I think we need to give ourselves some more time. I'm personally not in condition to say if Singapore will be now more suitable or not, because from a track layout point of view, we thought that Sepang would be a decent circuit for us.

"This is because of the uncertainty caused by the new scenario from a competitiveness point of view, but also because we might have to understand a bit better the upgrades that we took ourselves, and Singapore will give us a better answer."

Sports.title: India's World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet steps down
Sports.content:
India's World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from the role across all three formats.

The batter, 37, led India to their first-ever global women's title at the 2025 50-over World Cup on home soil.

Harmanpreet is only the third Indian captain, after men's players Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni, to guide a team to victory in that event.

Her last act in charge was steering her country to a second straight Asian Games gold last month, with India thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final.

Image: Harmanpreet led India in 211 matches across the formats

Overall, Harmanpreet - who is likely to be succeeded by Smriti Mandhana - captained in five Tests, 51 one-day internationals and 155 T20 internationals.

'I have given everything I had to this team'

Writing on Instagram, Harmanpreet said: "This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.

"I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women's cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions.

"There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.

"As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost.

Image: India beat South Africa in the 2025 World Cup final

"But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this team better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.

"I leave the captaincy with a heart full of emotions but also with peace. Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of.

"I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women's cricket."

'Captaincy ends, the journey continues'

Harmanpreet's final Test as captain was the 270-run drubbing of England at Lord's in July, the first women's Test to be held at the ground.

She became T20 captain in 2016 and added the Test and ODI roles when Mithali Raj retired in 2022.

Image: Harmanpreet is now ready to 'play for the love of the game again'

Harmanpreet added: "Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.

"Blood. Sweat. Sacrifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues."

India will host Zimbabwe for three T20 internationals and as many ODIs from October 16 before a tour of South Africa in December that is live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: NFL suspends official for swearing at player
Sports.content:
The NFL has suspended a line judge for two games for swearing at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride.

Jeff Seeman was caught on camera cursing at McBride during the Cardinals' loss to the New York Giants on Sunday.

"Obviously, you hate to see it, for obvious reasons," Arizona coach Mike LaFleur said. "I do want to give the man a little bit of grace, too. I know Jeff. He's a good man. It's unfortunate it happened. It can't happen, obviously, and I'll leave it at that."

The incident drew the ire of union leader JC Tretter, a retired offensive lineman who played eight seasons.

"This kind of behaviour from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter, the NFL Players Association's executive director, said on social media along with a video clip of the incident.

"Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Sports.title: Jude awakening: how a more fluid England are ‘unlocking’ Bellingham’s full potential
Sports.content:
Anthony Barry knows the hunt is on. The England assistant coach has been through the debriefs. He has mulled over the minutiae with Thomas Tuchel to such an extent he is allowed to make a joke at the boss’s expense. “He’s doing my head in,” Barry says with a smile. What is the missing piece of the puzzle? After all the emotion of England’s semi-final finish at the World Cup, how can they take the decisive step to glory?

It is early days in the Nations League campaign, which everybody at the Football Association wants to use as a slingshot into Euro 2028 when England will co-host, but Barry can see the genesis of an answer. It comes down to liberation, enabling England’s top players to fully express themselves, and there is a reason why he finds himself talking about Jude Bellingham.

The Real Madrid player was sensational in Saturday’s 7-0 win over Croatia in Rijeka, just as he was in the 3-2 defeat against Spain at Wembley on the Saturday before that. Playing in the No 10 role but with greater licence to drift, to overload on either side, there were times when Bellingham seemed to be playing with his own ball.

The story about why he wore the No 22 shirt at his first club, Birmingham, is well told. Because he was a No 4, a No 8 and a No 10 rolled into one. Tuchel appears to have reached a conclusion, the basis of which was formed at the World Cup when Bellingham excelled: when a talent like him can play in so many positions, perhaps it is better not to give him one at all.

“The structure [now in the Nations League] allows Jude to play more from his intuition,” Barry says, “and less from being locked down or caged in a certain position. It allows him to roam and operate in spaces in which he thinks he can be dangerous and so far it’s brought out the best in him.

“It is a challenge because Jude can play in any of those positions comfortably and on a high level. So the challenge is to give him a space where he can do it all at once inside of one game. Right now, in a short sample, it seems like we found a solution to unlock all of the potential that Jude has. But we have to continue.”

The point is that it is not just about Bellingham, even if he has drawn the eye almost inexorably so far this season. The blueprint was there for all to see against Croatia and it is one in which plenty of players were encouraged to push into new zones away from those traditionally dictated by their positions. Hence Tuchel had the full-backs extremely high, the wingers making zipping runs off the sides.

It is about the combinations, the slicker the better, but also about players dropping into unusual areas to provide cover and using their footballing intelligence to ensure the overall structure retains its shape. Hence there was the sight of Harry Kane dropping into defensive spaces out of possession, the kind where most No 9s would never tread.

View image in fullscreen Jude Bellingham takes on Luka Modric during England’s thrashing of Croatia. Photograph: Raddad Jebarah/Shutterstock

It was impossible to ignore the ferocity of England’s counterpress; how if one player lost the ball, he and his teammates sought to regain it within two or three seconds. Croatia were overwhelmed, especially in the first half, which ended with England four goals up. The intensity has to endure. But it is the proactive add-ons that the management hope will drive the new tournament cycle, continuing against Czechia in the Nations League at Wembley on Tuesday night. It is no longer a positional style. The idea is that it is freer. Is it a reaction to the inhibitions England came to feel in the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina?

“We have moved to a more principle-driven approach, which allows for more flexibility and fluidity,” Barry says. “But fluidity only looks good if it’s anchored by real principles. There is always a danger in international football with such a lack of time to prepare that if you go for this fluid model it can look quite messy. With the IQ of the players we have, it’s been quite natural for them to work together, operate in different spaces.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It’s not about starting new, it’s about continuation and adding stuff on top. It’s less prescribed, less fixed in the idea of: ‘You play here, you play there.’ It’s more interchanges of position. We feel it suits this group of players and is the best way to break down opposing blocks.

“When you have players like Harry and Jude on the frontline that are really better at moving, that have this deep intuition and IQ for the game … [it is] to trust them, open up spaces for them to operate. It’s also part of the model that we’re moving forward with. We have elite penetration on the last line, whether that comes from our wingers or our full-backs. And we have fluid midfielders with Elliot [Anderson], Alex [Scott] and Declan [Rice], who are happy to move for miles.”

Kane is primed to win his 125th cap on Tuesday night and equal Peter Shilton’s England men’s record. It is a time for tributes and Barry was effusive in his praise of Kane’s professionalism and leadership, his selflessness, his lack of ego; how he is happy to “track back and do the dirty work”.

Barry had a better line. “He’s the best ball-striker I have ever worked with,” he said. It is worth noting Barry worked with Cristiano Ronaldo during his time with Portugal as the assistant manager to Roberto Martínez. It is one key reason for Barry’s sense of optimism. There are many others.

Sports.title: Schooled for success: how English lessons power Midtjylland’s talent factory
Sports.content:
If there is a secret to Midtjylland’s success in the transfer market then it starts in the classroom. Before this summer the Danish club renowned for an innovative approach had banked more than €200m (£170m) in sales since 2018, and they have just enjoyed the most profitable window in their short history.

The departure of the Guinea-Bissau striker Franculino Djú for Trabzonspor and the Chile forward Darío Osorio’s move to Crystal Palace on loan with an obligation to buy will potentially bring in €62m (£53.2m), with both deals completed in 48 hours at the end of the window. That followed the departures of the homegrown winger Aral Simsir and South Korean defender Lee Han-beom for Club Brugge for another €25m. The next batch of recruits included David Martínez, a 20-year-old Venezuela international from the MLS side LAFC. “I think hectic will be a good word,” says the technical director, Kristian Kjær, of the past couple of months.

What those sold have in common is that they were schooled for success by Midtjylland’s methodical approach that includes mandatory English lessons at least three times a week. “They are as important for them as it is to train,” Kjær says. “Because if they cannot understand English within six months, they cannot communicate with the coach. So it’s quite important for our common success.”

In a squad that has 17 nationalities from five continents, communication is key. Midtjylland employ coaches from all over the world to help new arrivals settle in. “We’re not running Midtjylland as a Danish club; we are an international club,” says Kjær, who describes Djú and Osorio as “poster boys for what we are trying to do”.

The fee for Osorio, whose move was confirmed almost two hours after the Premier League deadline had passed, is in line to become the most expensive Danish top-flight sale, with Palace having an obligation to pay £22.3m next summer and up to another £3.4m in bonuses. The 22-year-old made his first Palace start in their 3-0 Carabao Cup win against Middlesbrough after coming on against Fulham a few days earlier in the Premier League. He was spotted by Midtjylland’s scouts playing for Universidad de Chile and the club saw off competition from RB Leipzig, Milan and Atalanta to sign him in August 2023 – the month the Brentford owner, Matthew Benham, sold his controlling stake to the Danish businessman Anders Holch Povlsen.

“Darío prioritised the importance for him to start in a club and environment in Europe that could help him grow so one day he could go to the Premier League, which has been his dream since he was a small boy,” Kjær says. “His integration off the pitch was most important. Chilean football is not, and I don’t try to sound disrespectful, the most professional setup when it comes to nutrition and habits outside the pitch. Darío used to eat a lot of white bread for dinner and he couldn’t understand why he was not fully energised in the morning. That was one of the first things we did: look into his nutrition plan.”

View image in fullscreen Franculino Djú left for Trabzonspor in the final hours of the transfer window. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Osorio, a predominantly left-footed forward who prefers playing as an inverted right-winger but can also fill the No 10 role, hit the ground running in Denmark and ended his first season with eight league goals.

“Since then, we have seen him putting on layers and layers,” Kjær says. “Darío has been outgrowing the league for some time and he was by far, in my opinion, the best player by a distance. We are very happy to see him making the step and believe he has the quality to be competitive in the Premier League, not as a sub but as a starting lineup player.”

There were a few nervous moments on deadline day as Palace pursued Malick Fofana before pivoting back to Osorio at the last minute when the Lyon forward picked Sunderland.

“We prepared both the agent and the player that everything can easily end up being in the last days of the window because English clubs are not that brave to bring in players from outside England, especially not from the not top five leagues,” Kjær says. “It was a bit stressful, especially for Darío. But at the same time, mentally, he was also a bit prepared for that: ‘OK, I have to perform in the beginning of the season to keep myself in the shop window.’”

Midtjylland are hoping that the arrival of the 20-year-old Martínez for €7.3m, a Danish record, will help to fill the void left by Osorio and Djú, their top scorer last season with 17 goals. Thanks to the club’s FC Ebedei academy in Nigeria, which was established in 2004 and has helped to produce players such as Coventry’s Frank Onyeka, Midtjylland’s squad has also been boosted by the addition of the promising teenagers Olashile Musa Lawal and Ikenna Udechukwu as they attempt to win the title for the first time since 2024. They were runners-up last season to the surprise package AGF.

“We are just standing on the shoulders of the work we have done earlier,” says Kjær. “But, to sound a bit boring because it takes so much work, it’s also a bit according to strategy. This is what we hoped for, but also what we have worked for. That is why it makes us proud. It’s not just pure luck.”

Sports.title: How did some City fans become aggressive defenders of a nation state’s regime? | Sean Ingle
Sports.content:
A video of Liam Gallagher playing in a 1996 charity football match resurfaced on social media recently. Dressed in Manchester City blue and a bucket hat, in truth he appears to be in a fug of cigarettes and alcohol. But then, out of nowhere, he hits a shot into the top corner. Since last week, though, the Oasis singer has preferred to defend the honour of his club with his studs up.

As the fallout from the biggest scandal in British football history headed into a second week, Gallagher was asked what he made of rival fans wanting City to lose all their trophies after being found guilty of all the serious charges against them. “There all NEUROTIC little GIMPS,” came the reply on social media. It was one of dozens of sweary, punchy, and often amusing responses, all built on a solitary article of faith: that City will somehow find a way to wriggle free.

But Gallagher is hardly standing alone. Over at Bluemoon, the biggest City forum, the tone has been just as defiant – albeit with a sprinkle of gallows humour. “Have we been blamed for the Titanic hitting the iceberg yet?” asked one user. “Manchester City shot JFK,” wrote another. “This isn’t just a fight between the PL & City. It’s a fight for the heart, soul & future of football,” reckoned a third.

Staggeringly, the forum now has over 192,000 posts since the initial charges against City, dating back to 2023. Naturally the Premier League, jealous rivals and the media all come under heavy fire. Yet there remains a curious reluctance among fans to accept wrongdoing – or to criticise the club’s owners.

How might we explain that? I am not sure it is down to pure tribalism, or a determination among City fans to wait for the club’s appeal to play out. It’s more complicated, and more interesting, than that.

Let us try to get into the head of the most vociferous City fan since last Tuesday. For decades they were in United’s shadow, then everything changed. Their city did too, given how much Abu Dhabi United Group pumped into it. You can forgive them, then, for not wanting to believe that it was all built on sand during the legal process.

But now? Now there is no excuse. So what might explain the reluctance to accept what the independent commission report lays out in great detail? According to the Irish academic Colm Kearns, one reason is because the United Arab Emirates has not only brought unprecedented success and forged emotional bonds with City fans “but have also co-opted elements of the club’s fanbase as aggressive defenders of their regime”.

In 2023 Kearns and his colleagues analysed huge numbers of posts from City fans, going back years, and found that some of them would not only “overlook ethical violations by the Group, but decry and – in some cases – attack the Group’s critics.”

In other words the club’s owners had successfully leveraged the tribal loyalty of City fans into being Manchurian Candidates – or, rather, Manchesterism Candidates.

Kearns tells me that some sports journalists had even self-censored because of the impact of online abuse from City fans. “We had people talking about how fans would go online and try to find their troll through their personal social feeds, and it sent that on to their editor to get them in trouble,” he says.

There is another massive factor here: social media, and the way we now consume sport and communicate with other fans. Thirty years ago, most City fans would live near Manchester and see fans from other clubs at work and in the pub. Nowadays, they can dwell in an online space made up entirely of people who support their own club.

View image in fullscreen Social media has created tribal online spaces for sports fans. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

“I think it makes fans perhaps more tribally myopic than they would have been before and less likely to look outside of their own club’s perspective,” says Kearns.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Academics also talk of “sports fandom circles”, in which supporters across the globe increasingly mobilise and fiercely defend athletes or their teams. That phenomenon, which came out of east Asia with popular culture and music, leads supporters to be laser-focused on their own tribe. But it hardly encourages lighthearted banter, common ground, or compromise.

In City’s case, Kearns suspects that some fans are putting the club above the wider game, citing a Reddit post that said: “I am a City fan first and a football fan second.” Although, as he concedes, it is impossible to know how many online posters do not live in Manchester, or go to games, and therefore feel the need to prove their bona fide credentials by sticking up for the club at all costs.

Either way, where we could go next is interesting. If you were a far-right tech billionaire, why wouldn’t you want to buy a successful sports team – especially if you knew there was an army of potential defenders of your reputation among your new fanbase?

Over the weekend I went through the fan forums of other clubs to see what their supporters made of the guilty verdict against City. The overwhelming majority welcomed it, of course, even if some questioned whether City would really get properly punished for their crimes, given the relationship with Abu Dhabi and the British government.

“Once you lose faith that the rules apply equally, football becomes something else,” one wrote. “Every title, every match, carries a question mark. I feel cheated. I’m one of the victims. And for that, I hate Manchester City.”

Some will agree with that sentiment. Others will raise their eyebrows. I do wonder, though, would that poster feel the same way if the boot was on the other foot, and their club was in the line of fire?

Sports.title: Nations League roundup: Olise leads late charge as France bowl over Belgium
Sports.content:
Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the Nations League, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.

Dodi Lukébakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France. But the hosts turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in 14 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.

Désiré Doué hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later. Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.

France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late goal from Olise, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss, goals from Gianluca Scamacca, Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito doing the business.

Zidane heavily rotated his team for the last match of this three-week long international window, with only Ousmane Dembélé keeping his place among the 10 changes. The Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and the Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes made their debuts, with Dembélé again captaining the side in the absence of the injured Kylian Mbappé.

Belgium were without the suspended duo of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans but caught France cold when Roméo Lavia’s superb ball split open the home defence, allowing Lukebakio to race clear and produce a clinical finish. Maarten Vandevoordt, making his debut in goal for Belgium, kept out efforts from Esteban Lepaul and Cherki as France pressed for an equaliser, but the dam eventually burst.

Doué gathered the ball and shot on the turn, beyond the reach of Vandevoordt, to haul France level. Cherki then turned home a cutback from Olise to give the hosts the lead as the Bayern Munich winger stole the show late on.

Olise scrambled in a third in the 88th minute and rolled in a fourth after skilful work from Doué to complete a remarkable turnaround.

“That’s football, that’s what we love. There were ⁠difficulties, but that’s part of the game, part of the kinds of matches you can have,” Zidane told TF1.

“It’s good to put things right, and ​that’s what we did with an extraordinary second half. We were ‌just missing that final few metres in ‌the first half, but then we turned the match around, it was good.”

Sports.title: Mamardashvili saves penalty as Georgia hold Northern Ireland in Nations League
Sports.content:
This game concluded with mutual irritation and a touch of chaos. It is an indicator of Northern Ireland’s progress that scoreless parity led to wincing from players, management and fans alike. Isaac Price’s 84th-minute missed opportunity from the penalty spot added to the sense of annoyance.

Michael O’Neill’s team are atop B2 after a window which, going by the players’s physical condition in the dying stages, has been exhausting. Northern Ireland and their youthful setup are a fascinating international story. They are a team on an upward curve, with standards elevated accordingly. O’Neill bemoaned “immaturity” in the second half, saying: “The disappointing thing is we have eight points instead of 10.”

Georgia were reduced to fury with seconds of the five minutes of stoppage time remaining. The visitors were adamant they should have been awarded a spot-kick of their own as Saba Sazonov toppled under a challenge from Callum Marshall. Ramaz Svanadze, the Georgia coach, diplomatically said he would have to view the incident again.

The difficulty for Northern Ireland related to a rising expectation. The superb performance during Friday’s 3-0 win over Ukraine backed up victory away to Georgia and a draw with Hungary. O’Neill’s men were yet to concede a goal in this section. A team quietly tipped to peak around qualification for Euro 2028 was blossoming earlier than anticipated, and this without the long-term absentee Conor Bradley. Northern Ireland’s oldest starter for Georgia’s visit was the 28-year-old Ciaron Brown.

Georgia are a curious case, outside the top 70 in the world yet containing one of its finest players. Clearly Khvicha Kvaratskhelia cannot carry a nation on his own. Indeed, the superstar’s first act was to pass the ball straight to Ethan Galbraith in the Northern Ireland midfield. During the nondescript early exchanges, Kvaratskhelia also gifted possession to Jamie Donley.

What football existed in the first half came from the hosts. Ruairi McConville came closest to opening the scoring with a header from Justin Devenny’s cross, Giorgi Mamardashvili not at all convincing in denying him. Georgia responded, an excellent save from Pierce Charles necessary to deny Zuriko Davitashvili. The let-off triggered a sweeping Northern Ireland move which culminated in Devenny overhitting a low cross.

View image in fullscreen Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was kept relatively quiet, but even so came close to scoring a fantastic goal. Photograph: Cathal McNaughton/Reuters

Northern Ireland were frustrated by the wasting of umpteen set plays during that first period. That Davitashvili moment aside, Georgia offered nothing in an attacking sense. Northern Ireland should have edged ahead four minutes before the interval, Patrick Kelly instead fluffing his lines having evaded the Georgia defence from Trai Hume’s through ball. Kelly appeared in two minds over whether to shoot or play in a teammate, with the visitors seizing upon his indecision. The half ended with Price curling a free-kick into the wrong side of the side-netting.

Price, born in Yorkshire, exemplifies Northern Ireland’s diligence in sourcing players through bloodline eligibility. The Manchester-born Charles brothers – Shea, the captain, was once again classy in midfield as Pierce kept goal – do likewise. This is, however, no team pulled together from afar; Galbraith was a boy wonder in Belfast before being coaxed to Manchester United as a teenager. His imaginative playmaking will surely one day be worthy of a grander stage than Stoke and the Championship

This big-picture stuff was irrelevant as Georgia stood firm. This was a game of intrigue, where Northern Ireland were superior while lacking a ruthless touch. Georgia’s threat was understated but real.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Galbraith limped off with 25 minutes to play, in what constituted a blow to O’Neill. The game by now was tense and scrappy. While against better opponents that may have suited Northern Ireland, that was patently not the case this time. Georgia were managing to sap energy from the home support.

With fatigue apparent across the pitch, O’Neill turned to a 36-year-old who plies his club trade at Stevenage to beef up the attack. Josh Magennis edges ever close to 100 caps, this was No 93.

Kvaratskhelia had been strangely subdued for 79 minutes, but striding forward from midfield, the Paris Saint-Germain forward cracked a 20-yard drive just over the bar. What an outstanding goal it would have been.

Magennis was handed a golden chance but Mamardashvili saved. A melee from the subsequent corner led to the crossbar being struck but, more significantly, the video assistant referee’s attention drawn towards a kick in the face of McConville by Budu Zivzivadze. A spot-kick was correctly awarded. Up stepped Price, whose penalty was saved, low to his right, by the Liverpool goalkeeper. Northern Ireland had passed up their moment. Georgia believed they should have been given scope to rub salt into wounds.

Sports.title: Police occupy Djibouti FA headquarters amid attempt to oust Fifa council member
Sports.content:
Attempts to oust Souleiman Waberi as the president of the Djibouti football federation (FDF) reached a dramatic climax on Monday as police occupied the federation’s headquarters after a group of club presidents called an extraordinary general assembly aimed at removing the Fifa council member and his executive committee.

The FDF said police first occupied its national technical centre at about 5.30pm on Sunday, without presenting an administrative document or court order. According to the federation, on Monday a much larger police contingent ordered Waberi, members of the executive committee, staff and other federation members to leave the premises.

The FDF said 16 club presidents then entered the building under police escort and proceeded to hold what it described as a “purported” EGM. The federation rejected the meeting as illegitimate, saying it had not been properly convened and that the notice periods and procedures required under its statutes and electoral code had not been respected. It declared any decisions taken “null and void”. But sources in Djibouti have insisted the number of delegates required by the statutes was present. They unanimously voted to remove Waberi and the executive committee before establishing an interim committee to oversee the federation.

Quick Guide How do I 

The confrontation follows weeks of mounting opposition to Waberi, a member of the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee as well as Fifa’s council and a close ally of Gianni Infantino. At the start of September, a coalition of 27 clubs announced its intention to vote on the removal of the executive committee and insisted it had secured the two-thirds support required under the federation’s statutes.

The FDF disputed that calculation, saying it has 67 members and that 45 – not 27 – would be required to trigger an extraordinary assembly. The dispute escalated as additional clubs and delegates joined the campaign against the executive committee. The government then intervened, with the secretary of state for sport, Fatouma Ali Abdallah, ordering the FDF to convene an extraordinary general assembly within 72 hours.

The FDF has appealed to Fifa and Caf, arguing that the use of state security forces to remove elected officials could constitute interference in the affairs of a national football association. It warned that the consequences could include suspension, exclusion of Djiboutian clubs and national teams from international competitions, and a freeze on development programmes and funding. The Guardian has requested a comment from Fifa.

It is understood Waberi and several other officials could be facing charges this week after a police investigation of the FDF related to suspected embezzlement and money laundering was completed. They were arrested in September 2024 after a government inspection of the FDF identified financial and administrative irregularities, including weaknesses in procurement, cash management and financial controls. The government’s investigation also raised concerns about anomalies in payments to third parties, failure to pay tax on salaries and wages and “misuse of cash payments” totalling almost £500,000. The police then carried out its investigation.

Waberi has denied wrongdoing. He said in August after the FDF was accused by a club official of misusing funds that Fifa’s “monitoring mechanisms have revealed no indication of wrongdoing regarding the funds it disbursed”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa, which along with Caf contributes more than $1m (£760,000) a year to the FDF through its forward development programme, has financed football infrastructure and youth-development programmes in Djibouti, including the Douda academy and artificial-pitch projects in Arta and Dikhil. But it is understood that various tenders are under investigation because they did not comply with standard procedures.

Several foreign workers who were not in compliance with immigration regulations were sent back to their home countries, meaning construction was halted. According to several Caf and Fifa employees and contractors, the projects in Djibouti are “a complete farce”. “We pass on the information but nothing happens,” said one contractor. “The money has gone missing, the projects are never finished – or if they are, it’s just a bare-bones version – and nobody says a word. It breaks my heart for the young people who just want to play football.”

Sports.title: Celtic celebrate heated win over Rangers in final of revived Tennent’s Sixes
Sports.content:
The intensity of the football rivalry in Glasgow was evident on Sunday night as Celtic turned the tables on Rangers to win the Tennent’s Sixes. Celtic beat their rivals 5-4 in the final at Braehead Arena after being on the end of a 7-1 defeat by Rangers in the group stage on Saturday.

The tournament was for retired players from all 12 Premiership teams as the SPFL revived a tournament that took place between first teams from 1984 to 1993. But the reactions were similar to any major trophy final.

Celtic’s Charlie Mulgrew admitted he got carried away in his celebrations after he ignored handshake attempts from the Rangers captain, Andy Halliday, in order to salute the crowd, and exchanged words with the Rangers manager, Barry Ferguson.

There was a heated post-match analysis in the Rangers dressing room. In a video leaked on social media, Kirk Broadfoot appears to be heavily criticising the goalkeeper Lee Robinson.

Mulgrew had calmed only slightly when he spoke to Premier Sports. “A lot of adrenaline was flowing, a few nasty tackles,” the 40-year-old said. “I mean, I know it was the Tennent’s Sixes, but you get caught up in the moment.

“You don’t like to get beat from Rangers, our closest rivals, 7-1, so that hurt. We had a few beers, a wee chat, a wee night out, so we managed to turn it around. We got a few things ironed out, although I was a wee bit rough in the morning.

“It feels like I’ve won an actual, real cup. It’s mental. I got a bit carried away at the end there but it builds up. There was a lot of emotion in that. Sometimes that’s what happens, it spills over.

“Football’s like that. I got nutmegged a couple of times by [Martyn] Waghorn, and exchanged words with him, then that was me. I was just fired up and fired into a few tackles. In the end, because we had that spirit, we won.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Celtic’s manager, Tom Boyd, said he was “pretty angry” with his players on Saturday night and that it “feels like winning the league”.

His assistant, Simon Donnelly, admitted they were all “embarrassed” by Saturday’s heavy defeat and told Celtic Player after the final: “It’s against Rangers, so it’s as if it’s a Scottish Cup final there. That’s the feeling. You could play Rangers at tiddlywinks and you’d still want to win.” Press Association

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Leeds LIVE commentary: Gunners face injury chaos on Premier League return amid withdrawals
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has plenty of fitness worries to address ahead of Arsenal's return to Premier League action against Leeds.

Multiple key members of the Gunners' squad returned from international duty early across the three-week break.



4 Havertz, who has played every league game for Arsenal so far this season, could be out for a month and is expected to miss the clash with Leeds Credit: AFP

Declan Rice withdrew from the England squad before playing a game, while Kai Havertz, who has started every Premier League fixture so far this season, returned from Germany's camp.

He could potentially be sidelined for a month after picking up a hamstring problem after just half an hour against the Netherlands, meaning he is expected to miss out against Leeds.

As for Rice, the midfielder may be okay to feature despite his withdrawal, having seemingly pulled out to manage his minutes, appearing in the tunnel during England's defeat to Spain.



Elsewhere, Christos Tzolis looked devastated as he was forced off for Greece against the Netherlands last Thursday.

Tzolis appeared to suffer a hamstring injury, like Havertz, pulling up and looking emotional as he received treatment.



And Ezri Konsa joined Arsenal's list of concerns on Monday, as he officially pulled out of England's squad.

Konsa missed the Three Lions' win over the Czech Republic before playing the full 90 minutes in a 7-0 victory over Croatia, but he may have aggravated an injury in that thrashing, returning to the Gunners for further assessment.



Captain Martin Odegaard was also among the worries, having picked up an ankle injury while playing for Norway against Portugal.

However, he had an X-ray and was confirmed to have avoided permanent damage, with him returning to action on Sunday.

But the number of issues picked up in the last three weeks still leaves Arteta in a very tough position heading into his side's clash with Leeds at the Emirates this weekend, live on talkSPORT.

4 Tzolis was visibly emotional after pulling up with a hamstring injury while playing for Greece over the international break Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



4 Konsa also picked up an injury during the break and has since withdrawn from the England squad Credit: Getty

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

4 Arsenal's injuries may end up boosting Leeds' hopes of continuing their unbeaten Premier League start Credit: Getty



Arsenal vs Leeds: What about the away side?

Leeds may feel a potentially weakened Arsenal team gives them a great chance to maintain their unbeaten streak.

Daniel Farke's side have won two and drawn three in five Premier League games so far this season.

They sit fifth in the top-flight table and just three points behind the Gunners heading into their meeting this weekend.

As for their injury list, Harry Wilson could return after missing out on a place in the Wales squad during the international break.



However, Joe Rodon and Mateo Joseph will remain sidelined.

And wingers Dan James and Jean-Mateo Bahoya both seem to be carrying knocks picked up over the break.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi tipped to make surprise Argentina retirement U-turn
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has been here before.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner first retired from international football in 2016 after Argentina lost their fourth major final in nine years.

3 Messi is gearing up to play his 208th and final international game Credit: Getty



But one U-turn later and Messi now has a World Cup and two Copa America titles in his trophy cabinet.

He came agonisingly close to adding a second World Cup crown, only for Argentina to fall short in the final against Spain in July.

When will Lionel Messi play his final international game?

Just one month later, Messi announced his international retirement for a second time.

He's now set to tie the bow on his glittering international career against Benin in Buenos Aires on October 6 in what will be his 208th cap for Argentina.



To mark the occasion, Argentina kit supplier Adidas have designed a special one-off kit for Messi to wear.

It's all set up to be a fitting farewell to Messi's international career.



Tim Vickery's verdict on Lionel Messi's international retirement

However, South American football expert Tim Vickery questioned whether this truly would be the end for the pint-sized superstar in an Argentina shirt.

"I wonder if Messi, having a look at these kids coming through, might even end up thinking, 'You know what, this is fun, why don't I stay a little bit longer?'" Vickery said on talkSPORT's The S* Word.



"(Lionel) Scaloni makes it very, very clear, 'The day you want to come back, the door is open.'

"We will find out in the fullness in time if this is a Frank Sinatra retirement or if it is really definitive."

3 Argentina has been swept up in Messi fever ahead of his final international game Credit: AFP

The late Sinatra initially retired in 1971 but went on to perform for another two decades.



At age 39, Messi won't be able to pull a similar stunt to Sinatra in terms of prolonging his playing career.

His contract with Major League Soccer (MLS) outfit Inter Miami runs through to 2028, when he will be 41.

And even then, he may not be ready to hang up the boots just yet.

Lionel Messi's post-playing career

But whenever the time comes, Messi has already made a number of moves to prepare for his post-playing career.

One avenue Messi has explored is club ownership as he completed his purchase of Spanish second tier club Eldense in October.



3 Messi's international career is unrivalled Credit: talkSPORT

It is the second club in Messi's portfolio, having taken full ownership of third tier side Cornella in April.

Messi also boasts a remarkable business portfolio that, according to Forbes, placed his net worth at an estimated £831million.

The dizzying figure is aided by a lifetime Adidas deal and a luxury hotel collection called MiM Hotels.

Sports.title: Ex-Man United star Fred claims former teammate told him: ‘I’m rich, I don’t need to run’
Sports.content:
Ex-Man United star Fred claims former teammate told him: ‘I’m rich, I don’t need to run’

Jhon Duran 'completely quit' during his loan spell at Fenerbahce, according to former teammate Fred.

The former Aston Villa striker also believed that his healthy bank account entitled him to not need to run in training, it has been claimed.

3 Duran's attitude has been called into question once again Credit: Getty

Duran spent the second half of last season on loan at Fenerbahce, scoring five goals for the club during his seven-month spell in Turkey.

The Colombia forward would make just 21 appearances before the loan was ended early in February, with injuries a factor in his lack of action.

However, Fred has now provided a glimpse into Duran's attitude at the training ground too.

The pair made a total of 16 appearances together for the Turkish giants.

Duran's attitude at Fenerbahce

Appearing on the Charla podcast, Fred explained: "Jhon Duran didn’t really care about anything. ‘Come on Duran, let’s train, let’s run a bit over there,’ I’d say.

"‘Bro, I’m already rich. I don’t need to run,’ he’d say, then he’d go to the medical department and slack off."

The former Manchester United midfielder added: "When [Duran] went to Zenit St Petersburg, I said, ‘Ooo, now you’re gonna make even more money.’

"‘Bro, the more the better, the more the better,’ he’d say. Sometimes when we talked, he’d say, ‘I’ve already saved the lives of me, my family, and three generations…’

"At Fenerbahce, at least in the beginning he was showing up for training and stuff, then he completely quit."

Duran joined Fenerbahce on loan from Al Nassr last summer less than six months after completing a £64million switch from Villa.

3 Fred spent three years with Fenerbahce after five years at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

After his stint with the club ended prematurely, he went to Russia to join Zenit St. Petersburg for the remainder of the campaign.

The 22-year-old has since moved to Benfica on a season-long loan, his third temporary spell away from Al Nassr.

It could become a permanent switch, though, with an option to buy included in the deal.

Duran has already scored twice for Benfica in 12 appearances across all competitions.

However, only two of those have been from the start, with Duran completing 90 minutes just once.

As well as already playing for seven clubs, Duran has been left out in the cold for his national team.

3 Duran joined Benfica on loan this summer, making them his fourth club in 18 months Credit: Getty

Having made his Colombia debut aged 18 in 2022, he has not added to his three goals in 17 caps since June 2025.

His ongoing absence from the side also saw Duran miss out on a place in Nestor Lorenzo's World Cup squad this summer.

talkSPORT verdict

Duran was previously labelled a 'bad egg' by fellow former Villa forward Gabby Agbonlahor after joining Benfica.

Speaking in July, the talkSPORT co-host admitted: "When Jhon Duran left Aston Villa, everyone was a little annoyed but the manager did the right thing.

"He left Aston Villa for Al Nassr in January 2025 for £65million. Since then, he’s been on loan at Fenerbahce, Zenit and now Benfica, and there’s a buy-option in the loan of £22million.

"He’s 22 years of age, in 18 months look at what has happened to him. Sometimes players are bad eggs, and well done to Unai Emery for getting him out."

Sports.title: World Cup winner reveals 15-year health battle with illness that leaves sufferers in bed for ‘months’
Sports.content:
World Cup winner reveals 15-year health battle with illness that leaves sufferers in bed for ‘months’

World Cup winner and Italian football legend Gennaro Gattuso has revealed he has been battling illness for 15 years.

Gattuso admitted that he retired after being diagnosed with an autoimmune disease that he has been battling since.

3 Italy icon Gattuso has revealed that he has been battling an autoimmune disease for the last 15 years Credit: Getty

The iconic midfielder hung up his boots in 2013 after an impressive playing career spanning almost two decades.

And he has now opened up about his long-term struggles with his illness that takes a toll on him on a daily basis.

Speaking at the Festival dello Sport, Gattuso revealed: "I stopped playing because of the autoimmune disease I got.

"And I have been taking [medicine] cortisone for 15 years."

An autoimmune disease is a chronic condition that sees a person's immune system attack their own body's cells and tissues, instead of fighting off outside germs.

He continued: "Throughout all these years, I have said that there are people with my illness who stay in bed for four or five months because they cannot move.

"I accepted the illness. I work on it. But it takes its toll on me, because taking cortisone every day is not easy.

"It has been six or seven years since I drank any kind of alcohol.

"You keep going until God gives you the strength to carry on."

AC Milan icon Gattuso is currently the manager of Lazio in Serie A, continuing his involvement in football despite his health issues.

3 Gattuso won the World Cup, two Champions Leagues and two Serie A titles as a player before his illness led to his retirement in 2013 Credit: Getty

3 He went on to manage Italy, but after his sacking, he instantly moved on to join Lazio Credit: AFP

How is Gattuso doing with Lazio?

The 48-year-old won the World Cup with Italy as a player and ended up managing them from June 2025 to April 2026.

He was sacked as boss after failing to qualify for the 2026 World Cup despite winning six of his eight matches in charge.

Gattuso is also a two-time Champions League and Serie A winner, using his success on the pitch to build a career off it.

And after leaving the national team, he is now Lazio boss.

His side have started strongly, sitting level with leaders Roma and Inter Milan in the league table.

In five games, they have four wins, one draw and no losses.

"We have started well, but the road is long," Gattuso said. "But I'm proud of the lads, who are giving so much."

Sports.title: Liverpool sweat on fitness of star taken out of national team squad with hamstring injury
Sports.content:
Liverpool sweat on fitness of star taken out of national team squad with hamstring injury

Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was left out of the France squad on Monday evening after picking up a hamstring strain.

Jacquet was rested by Zinedine Zidane for his side's Nations League clash with Belgium, with Leny Yoro taking his place.



3 Jacquet felt a strain in his hamstring before France's match against Belgium on Monday night and sat out of the action Credit: Getty

The 21-year-old centre-back had started the last two games for his country, playing a full 90 minutes just three days ago.

However, the French Football Federetaion have confirmed that he missed out after suffering a strain to his left hamstring.

Manchester United's Yoro was then drafted in to make his international debut as Zidane shuffled his back line.



The issue will be a huge concern for Liverpool, with a crunch Premier League clash against Manchester City coming up on Sunday, as City play their first match since being found guilty of all charges for breaching financial rules from 2009 to 2018.

Jacquet has been a mainstay in Andoni Iraola's defence, becoming an instant key player next to Virgil van Dijk this season.



The Reds have also suffered injury setbacks with key forwards Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak returning early from Netherlands and Sweden duty respectively.

A disappointing end to a first call-up

This was Jacquet's first camp with the French senior side, having been called up by Zidane for his impressive showings.



Liverpool boss Iraola was delighted for his young star when speaking about his achievement, saying last month: "I'm happy for him because he's also received his first international call-up.

"He's going with France and that is a big national team and I know that he is happy. He's still very young, he is adapting really well to the Premier League."

But after making two appearances, his hamstring issue has forced him to miss out on picking up a third cap.

3 Jacquet could now be a doubt for Liverpool's upcoming clash with Man City on Sunday Credit: Getty



3 The young centre-back has been a revelation for the Reds since arriving at the club this summer Credit: Getty

Who could replace Jacquet for Liverpool?

Jacquet will return to Liverpool in the coming days ahead of the return of Premier League football this weekend.

Whether he will be fit to play against Man City is still unknown though, leaving the Reds sweating over his involvement.

If he does miss out, Joe Gomez could come in to replace him.

Iraola will be very disappointed if he does have to change his centre-backs after discussing Jacquet's improved fitness last month.



He said after Liverpool's last fixture before the international break: "I think in the first games, physically he was feeling the change of rhythm, he was finishing with cramps, finishing really tired and we had to sub him.

"Today has been a step forward. He looked solid until the end and I think he's finished physically also in a good place.

"I hope he can continue this development."

But could a hamstring issue picked up right at the end of the break end up hampering that development?

Sports.title: Big Harry Kane contract update as he continues Ballon d’Or bid
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is in the final stages of agreeing a new contract with Bayern Munich, talkSPORT understands.

The England captain, who joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023, is expected to sign a fresh three-year deal.



3 Kane joined Bayern from Spurs in 2023 and he is now set to commit his future to the German giants for another three years Credit: Getty

Kane has entered the last 12 months of his current contract in Germany, which is set to expire at the end of this season.

But he is now going to commit his future to the club until the summer of 2029, having scored a staggering 152 goals in 154 appearances for them across all competitions.

The two-time Bundesliga champion will be one month shy of his 36th birthday when his new contract runs out.



What has Kane said about a new Bayern deal?

Kane confirmed that talks were underway with Bayern over a new deal in August, admitting it may be the final one of his career.

He said on August 29: "The first meeting started last week. I'm 33. It's probably going to be, not my last contract.



"But it's a big contract for me to sign. They need to make sure I'm happy. They obviously need to make sure they're happy… there's no panic from either side.

"I'm sure we'll get to a point where both sides are happy."

And it now seems like that point has been reached, with Kane set to stay at Bayern to potentially see out his playing days.



Is there any chance Kane returns to Spurs?

Many Tottenham fans will have been dreaming of seeing Kane back at his beloved club that he played almost 450 games for, to have a go at breaking Alan Shearer's Premier League goal record.

And the striker does have a clause in his current Bayern contract that allows Spurs to match any transfer offers made.

3 Kane revealed talks over a new Bayern deal were ongoing in August and a breakthrough has now been reached Credit: Getty

That has reportedly led to a few issues in sorting out his new deal, and it is unclear whether that clause will remain.



If not, the dream of Kane returning to north London may be over, as well as his hopes of a brand new top-flight record.

Kane's bid for the Ballon d'Or

Kane's incredible form for Bayern Munich and England has him as one of the frontrunners to win the Ballon d'Or.

The 33-year-old scored 73 goals for club and country in the 2025/26 season and has maintained that form since.

He also led the Three Lions to the World Cup semi-finals after winning his third straight Bundesliga Golden Boot.



If he is to win the award and become the first Englishman to do so since Michael Owen in 2001, then he is sure to send some praise Bayern's way after committing his future to the club.

3 Kane's 73-goal season for Bayern and England in 2025/26 sees him as one of the leading contenders to win the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty

Lamine Yamal is expected to be his biggest rival after winning the World Cup, with Kylian Mbappe also a contender.

Kane's England teammate Anthony Gordon has been speaking about his skipper's chances of winning the prestigious title.



And he thinks that it is between Kane and Barcelona teammate Yamal for the crown.

Gordon said: “For me, it has to be one of the two in terms of what they've achieved. What Lamine's achieved at such a young age.
