Sports.title: Hamilton suspects he could have fought for win had he not started on slicks | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton believes he could have fought for victory at Sepang had he started on the right tyres.

The Ferrari driver qualified on the front row of the grid alongside Max Verstappen

“We were having a good weekend,” he said. “The car felt great in qualifying. It felt amazing to get to second.

“Me and my engineers were here ’til 11:30 last night just going over everything and I really, really felt today was the opportunity to have at least a good battle with Max.”

The original start was delayed due to rain. A further delay followed after a software problem caused several drivers, including Hamilton and Verstappen, to slow to a crawl during the formation lap.

“My power didn’t come back and I had to stop on-track and restart the car and then we all ended up in the pit lane,” said Hamilton. “Thankfully, we all got back to our positions.”

By the time race control were ready to start the race, the track had dried considerably, though it was still damp. Hamilton and his team chose to start the race on slick tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“There was such a long wait and we were debating what tyre to go on to. And I said, ‘look, there was a lot of spray on the laps to the grid.’

“I went into the pit lane, I looked at the ground, I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ I went to the pit wall and I was like, ‘It’s still wet.’ And they’re like, ‘Yeah, but because it’s been so long, it’s definitely going to dry up real quick and maybe we’re already in the crossover.’

“So, anyway, as a team we ended up taking that soft and when we were at the end of the pit lane and these two took off their blankets and they were on inters [I knew] we were in trouble.”

The track took a long time to dry and those who opted for intermediates gained a significant advantage at the start. Hamilton urged the team not to bring him into the pits for another change.

“As everyone had overtaken me, they’re like, ‘we stop.’ [But] I know we’ve already [lost] another 26 seconds, what’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I [said] ‘let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.’ And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people.”

Hamilton began to make progress on his softs once the Safety Car came out and he was back within range of other cars.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The car felt great then after that. Really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy.

“For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. But, of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.”

He said he will have an “open dialogue” with the team about the decision to start the race on slicks.

“We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that.

“So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which was the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting. I thought today, as I said, was a chance for us potentially to try and fight Max for the win, but maybe we can do that next week.”

Sports.title: Devin Haney Offers Shakur Stevenson 145-Pound December Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney has offered to face Shakur Stevenson at 145 pounds in December, lowering his proposed weight by two pounds while keeping his demand for no rehydration clause in a post on social media.

“Let’s do this 145 no rehydration clause @ShakurStevenson .. let’s see who’s the real pussy! December.. 2026. Somebody go wake Shakur up.. Tell him we got a deal,” Haney said on X.

The proposal moves Haney off the position he posted on October 4: “147.. no rehydration let’s get it done.” He is now offering to come below the welterweight limit, although the freedom to add weight afterward remains part of his terms.

That is a concession, but it only addresses part of the disagreement. Shakur would get a lower contracted weight without a limit on how much Haney could regain before entering the ring. If his concern is the size of the fighter facing him on the night, 145 pounds doesn’t settle that.

Haney would have to make the extra effort to lose those two pounds. Once the weight check is over, however, he could replenish without a contractual cap. The proposal could still leave Shakur facing a considerably heavier opponent.

From Haney’s side, this gives him something to point to when arguing that he is trying to make the fight. He has lowered his demand and named December as the month he wants. Shakur now has a specific offer to answer, rather than another challenge with no weight attached.

The December date adds urgency if both intend to fight this year. They would need to settle the remaining terms soon enough to arrange the event and prepare properly. A public callout can start that process, but it cannot substitute for their teams reaching a deal.

Haney is giving ground on the contracted weight while holding firm on rehydration. Whether that is enough depends on which concession Shakur wants most. If a cap on Haney’s weight gain remains a requirement, they could still be stuck despite moving closer on the official limit.

Sports.title: Artur Beterbiev Taunts Rivals While His Inactivity Grows
Sports.content:
Artur Beterbiev is taking shots at unnamed rivals while approaching 600 days without a fight, appearing in a gym video shared by The Ring with a message about others running while he works.

“While the bunnies are running, we’re working,” Beterbiev wrote.

He doesn’t name Dmitry Bivol, although the timing invites that interpretation. Bivol’s manager, Vadim Kornilov, has told The Ring that a trilogy is being explored for spring 2027. That remains a possibility rather than an announced fight.

Beterbiev has been out since losing their February 22, 2025 rematch. As of October 6, that is 591 days without a competitive round. A third meeting next spring could stretch the layoff beyond two years unless he fights someone else first.

The lucrative trilogy is understandable as a target. They have one victory apiece, and Beterbiev wants another chance after losing the rematch. But allowing that fight to dictate his schedule comes at a cost, particularly for a fighter who turns 42 in January.

Beterbiev should have pursued another fight while the Bivol talks continued. An opponent below championship level could still have given him rounds, a full training camp and a chance to work through whatever needed correcting after his defeat. Waiting has given him none of that.

The gym footage shows him putting in work, but lifting weights cannot tell him how he will react when an opponent makes him miss, catches him coming forward or forces him to work late in a fight. Those are questions he could have started answering against someone other than Bivol.

There is a financial reason to protect the trilogy payday. Taking another fight brings the possibility of defeat or injury. Yet staying out brings its own danger: Beterbiev could finally secure the opponent he wants after spending two years getting older without fighting.

The “bunnies” can take the insult. Beterbiev still needs to get back into a ring. If he keeps waiting for Bivol, he has to own what that wait costs him.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia And Devin Haney Exchange Rematch DMs
Sports.content:
Devin Haney appears open to a Ryan Garcia rematch, replying, “Let’s make the fight,” in an Instagram DM screenshot shared on X by Dan The Boxing Man and later reposted by Source of Boxing.

Haney’s apparent invitation follows Ryan asking, “Do I have to remind you again.” The exchange then turns to drug accusations, which Ryan denies before making claims about Haney smoking hookah.

Neither fighter discusses a date, weight, or purse in the screenshot. It shows interest in a rematch, but no agreed terms.

Ryan pursuing Haney suggests he may prefer a bigger payday over facing Isaac Cruz or Angel Fierro. That could fit Golden Boy’s plans for a May event, although waiting would bring the inactivity concerns outlined below.

Ryan Garcia Faces Eight Months Out Under Oscar’s Plan

Oscar De La Hoya wants Ryan Garcia to face Devin Haney or Teofimo Lopez in May 2027, saving his final contracted Golden Boy fight for a big payday. The downside for Ryan is that waiting until Cinco de Mayo would leave him inactive for roughly eight months before facing either opponent.

“Obviously we want to build a major fight for Ryan in May. I believe that Ryan should be fighting on those dates. He’s the guy that should be taking the throne on Cinco de Mayo,” De La Hoya told Fight Hub TV. “A Devin Haney or a Teofimo should be next.”

Ryan has discussed returning in December or January, but De La Hoya said he spoke with DAZN and there were no dates available in those months. Neither Haney nor Lopez is secured, with Oscar describing informal discussions rather than official negotiations.

You can understand why De La Hoya wants to wait. Ryan has one fight left with Golden Boy, and Oscar wants it to be a big one. A Haney rematch or a fight with Lopez would likely bring in far more money than Angel Fierro or Pitbull Cruz.

If Ryan finishes his contract against either of those two, Golden Boy could miss out on the bigger payday that follows. De La Hoya wants to continue working with Ryan, but there is no guarantee he will sign another deal.

Ryan has a reason to want that earlier return. Neither Haney nor Lopez is an opponent you want to face after eight months out. Fighting in December or January would keep him busy rather than sending him straight into a difficult fight after a long break.

The trouble is that saving the fight for May benefits Golden Boy more than it helps Ryan stay ready. Oscar gets the chance to cash in on a major event, but Ryan has to beat Haney or Lopez after eight months on the sidelines.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Urged To Face Devin Haney Without Restrictions
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson would give critics a reason to question a victory over Devin Haney by insisting on a catchweight and rehydration clause. Chris Mannix wants him to take the fight at 147 pounds, where the result could be judged without an argument over restrictions dominating afterward.

“If this fight happens with a catchweight and a rehydration clause, there is no way that Shakur Stevenson is going to get full credit for his win if he wins,” Mannix said during his podcast discussion with Sergio Mora. “If you’re Shakur, you should want to fight this guy on a level playing field.”

Mannix pointed to Gervonta Davis’s victory over Ryan Garcia as an example of how contractual limits can remain attached to a result long after the fight ends. His concern is that Shakur could outbox Haney only to spend the aftermath defending the terms rather than discussing his performance.

That is a reasonable concern. Asking Haney to come below welterweight and then limiting how much weight he can regain would create two separate talking points. Neither would automatically explain a defeat, but both would provide an alternative explanation for anyone unwilling to credit Shakur’s boxing.

Mannix also questioned the apparent difference between Shakur’s approach to Haney and his earlier interest in facing Ryan at 147. He qualified that comparison, saying a move to welterweight was what those discussions sounded like, rather than presenting unrestricted terms as an established agreement.

Shakur would still be accepting a physical disadvantage by moving up. Haney’s size could help him in clinches and make it harder for Shakur to control distance across twelve rounds. Superior defensive skills would not erase those demands.

But that additional risk is also what would make the victory more valuable. Beating Haney at his division’s limit, without restricting his recovery afterward, would give Shakur a stronger achievement and remove an obvious contractual argument from the discussion.

Haney doesn’t appear willing to move off his demand for 147 pounds, and Shakur has less room to pressure him than he might against a lesser-known welterweight. An opponent chasing the payday and exposure could be more willing to accept 144. Haney has his own name and earning power, so he can afford to hold his position.

That leaves Shakur with a decision beyond how much credit he would receive for winning. If Haney refuses to come down, Shakur must decide whether this fight is worth moving up for. Wanting Haney as an opponent doesn’t mean he can dictate the weight.

Sports.title: Dave Allen Backs Tyson Fury To Stop Joshua
Sports.content:
Dave Allen backs Tyson Fury to stop Anthony Joshua early, drawing on his experience sparring both heavyweights and his concern over Joshua’s punch resistance. The timing of those gym sessions is unclear, however, leaving questions about how closely they reflect either fighter’s current form.

“The Prenga fight, Joshua’s punch resistance looks to be all gone,” Allen told talkSPORT’s The Verdict with heavyweight Frazer Clarke. He also acknowledged that Joshua could knock Fury out.

Allen has felt both men’s power and tested himself against their timing in sparring, giving him a useful basis for judging the matchup. We don’t know how long ago those sessions took place, though, and he hasn’t revealed which fighter gave him more trouble.

If Joshua can no longer recover quickly from a hard shot, Fury has a reason to attack early. One clean punch could leave Joshua vulnerable to a follow-up barrage before he gets his legs back.

The question is whether Fury still has the speed and reactions to exploit that weakness without getting caught himself.

Fury’s appearance gives the impression that he has aged considerably over the last three years. Appearance alone cannot establish what he has left, but his reactions, balance, and ability to recover are just as important to this matchup as Joshua’s punch resistance. Allen’s sparring memories from an era when Fury had functioning legs solve none of those mysteries.

Marching into the pocket would put both heavyweights in immediate risk. If Fury rushes to wipe Joshua out, he comes directly into the path of a fresh, explosive right hand. Bullying Joshua toward the ropes without a tight guard or a blinding jab invites disaster, because Joshua throws his best counters off the back foot.

Fury could finish Joshua early, as Allen expects, but forcing the pace would put him within reach of Joshua’s right hand. If he rushes in carelessly, Joshua may land first.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Pressures Teofimo Lopez Over Mandatory Fight
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall is keeping his claim on Teofimo Lopez’s next fight visible while a potential Ryan Garcia matchup attracts attention. Catterall tagged Lopez on X with an eyes emoji and a staring-eyes GIF, a brief reminder that the ordered defense remains unresolved.

The WBA ordered the welterweight champions Teofimo and Catterall to negotiate in September, giving them until October 22 to reach an agreement before possible purse bids. Catterall holds the organization’s regular title, while Teofimo holds its super championship.

Catterall has earned his shot and has little reason to wait while Teofimo pursues Ryan. Agreeing to another delay would let the champion dictate when—or whether—he gets that opportunity. His public reminder keeps pressure on Teofimo to address the ordered defense

👀 @TeofimoLopez https://t.co/I6KqhNC0AN — Jack Catterall (@jack_catt93) October 5, 2026

Ryan brings the massive gate, the circus spotlight, and the blockbuster money for Lopez. Catterall brings none of that. Fighting Catterall means defending a belt against an awkward spoiler who could derail everything for a fraction of the pay.

That leaves Teofimo stuck. Chasing a blockbuster with Ryan sounds great, but the WBA order will not simply disappear. Hunting for a bigger payday is understandable, but actually getting sanctioning body approval to ignore a mandatory challenger is an entirely different battle.

Teofimo might need to vacate his belt to chase the massive check waiting with Ryan Garcia. Taking on Jack Catterall beforehand puts the entire jackpot in jeopardy. One slip against Catterall ruins his leverage, killing the buzz for the megafight.

Pretending the order does not exist invites the WBA to strip him. The October 22 cutoff marks the end of negotiations rather than an instant title stripping, yet Lopez cannot stall forever. Catterall forced the reality into the open: defend against him or walk away from the belt to fight Ryan empty-handed.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Targets William Zepeda After Lucas Bahdi
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield wants William Zepeda next if he beats Lucas Bahdi, with his father already forecasting a four-round stoppage of the Mexican pressure fighter. That is an ambitious projection before Schofield has secured his first world title.

“Zepeda is definitely who I want next. … That’s who I was going to call out and still going to call out after the fight,” Schofield told Chris Mannix. Floyd Schofield Sr. went further, arguing that Zepeda leaves too many openings and declaring: “Zepeda will get stopped in four rounds.”

Schofield faces Bahdi for the vacant WBA lightweight title this Saturday, October 10, in Chicago. A victory would give him a belt to bring into negotiations with Zepeda, making the proposed matchup more valuable than another contender callout.

Both fighters being represented by Golden Boy offers a practical reason to pursue it. The company could promote a unification involving two of its own fighters, with the winner emerging as a stronger attraction.

The competitive argument is less comfortable for Schofield than his father suggests. Zepeda’s pressure is built around making opponents work repeatedly, forcing them to defend, move, and return punches without long recovery periods. Finding openings against him is only part of the task. Schofield would also need to exploit them while managing the pace.

His knockout of Tevin Farmer showed how destructive he can be when an opponent gets caught early. It didn’t establish how he would handle Zepeda if the quick finish failed to arrive. Schofield Sr. acknowledges that facing Zepeda requires conditioning for 12 hard rounds, then assumes his son could end it in four.

There are also two immediate obstacles. Bahdi has his own chance to derail Schofield’s plans, while Zepeda has been ordered to defend against interim WBC champion Jadier Herrera. The proposed unification cannot simply be treated as available next.

Schofield naming Zepeda is a worthwhile challenge. Backing up his father’s prediction would require something considerably harder than identifying flaws on film: beating Bahdi first, then making Zepeda pay for those openings without being overwhelmed by everything coming back.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Doubts Ryan Garcia’s Zuffa Move
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya doesn’t believe Ryan Garcia will join Zuffa Boxing after completing his Golden Boy contract, despite Ryan’s praise for his experience at its recent event. Keeping him, however, will require more than questioning the alternative.

“He was very complimentary, and I’m glad that it turned out great for him because it’s Ryan’s career that’s on the line. But no, I don’t think he’ll go with Zuffa. I don’t think that’s a good fit for him,” De La Hoya told The Ariel Helwani Show.

Asked to explain, Oscar attacked Dana White’s handling of boxing press conferences and questioned his authority within the operation. He didn’t identify specific contractual or financial reasons that would make Zuffa unsuitable for Ryan.

That leaves his view looking more like a promoter defending his position than evidence of where Ryan intends to sign. Ryan’s positive experience gives Zuffa something to build on if it pursues him. Oscar’s criticism doesn’t erase that impression.

Golden Boy still has one fight remaining with Ryan, and De La Hoya named Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez as his preferred opponents. Neither matchup is finalized. Oscar indicated that arranging the next major fight comes before discussing an extension.

That remaining appearance offers Golden Boy its strongest opportunity to make a case for staying. Delivering Haney or Lopez would demonstrate that Oscar can still secure valuable fights despite the disagreements between promoter and fighter.

There is a complication: a successful final appearance could also increase Ryan’s appeal to competing promoters. Golden Boy might deliver the payday and exposure that help him negotiate a more attractive deal elsewhere.

De La Hoya says he has spoken with Ryan since the Conor Benn fight and describes their relationship as good. That should help them conduct business, but it isn’t a commitment to another contract.

Oscar can doubt a Zuffa move. His more useful task is giving Ryan a reason to choose Golden Boy again. The next opponent, the terms, and the handling of that final fight will make a stronger argument than another attack on Dana White.

Ghana News.title: Deaths of three children in Tamale vehicle now treated as murder – Police
Ghana News.content:
Police in the Northern Region are treating the deaths of three children found in the trunk of a vehicle as a murder case after a preliminary autopsy indicated that they did not die of natural causes.

The children — Dauda Abdul Aziz, 3, Saani Alsharaf, 5, and Dauda Fadilan, 7 — were found dead in the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson at Koblimahagu Zoo in the Tamale Metropolis on Monday morning.

The children had reportedly left home on Sunday to attend Islamic classes but failed to return.

According to JoyNews sources, preliminary findings from the autopsy indicate that the children may have been murdered.

However, a toxicological examination is still required to establish the circumstances and possible cause of their deaths.

“The autopsy revealed they did not die a natural death,” a source familiar with the investigation said.

“There is a need for toxicological examination to be conducted to fully establish the facts,” the source added.

The development marks a major turn in the investigation, which has generated widespread concern in the Northern Region.

The children were found in a black Hyundai Tucson with registration number AS 1770-14.

Police said the vehicle was found stuck in mud, with the driver’s door and rear passenger door open, while the boot and other doors were locked.

The owner of the vehicle, a member of the Ghana Immigration Service, has been arrested and transported to Accra to assist with investigations.

The officer reportedly told police that the vehicle had been stuck for five days.

Police have secured the vehicle for further forensic examination as investigators work to establish what happened to the children and how they ended up inside the boot.

The Inspector-General of Police has deployed forensic and crime scene experts to Tamale to support the investigation.

Homicide investigators and intelligence officers have also been dispatched to assist the Northern Regional Police Command.

The teams are expected to examine the vehicle and other evidence at the scene as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding the children’s deaths.

The preliminary autopsy findings have ruled out natural death, but authorities are awaiting toxicological results to provide further clarity on the cause of death.

Investigations remain ongoing.

Ghana News.title: Catholic Bishops urge stronger action against tramadol, marijuana abuse
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference has called for stronger measures to address the widespread use and abuse of tramadol, marijuana and other readily accessible drugs in the country.

The Bishops say the abuse of these substances is having a devastating impact on the country’s youth and requires greater attention as part of the national response to drug trafficking and abuse.

They argue that the fight against drugs should not focus solely on cocaine and other high-profile narcotics, but must also address substances that are easily accessible in communities.

Speaking to Citi News, President of the Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference, Most Rev. Matthew Gyamfi, said the increasing use of tramadol, marijuana and other drugs among young people required urgent action.

“In our villages and towns, we know the young men and women have taken to drugs—tramadol, ‘Red’, marijuana—and this is destroying many, many young men and women,” he said.

He said the national response must recognise the scale of abuse of substances that are readily available to young people.

“You should not concentrate only on drugs like cocaine, which is used, but not as massively as marijuana, tramadol, ‘Red’ and other similar drugs that are readily available on the shelves, and young people just go for it,” he stated.

Most Rev. Gyamfi called for stronger laws and enforcement measures to restrict the importation and illegal sale of such substances.

“They should make laws to ban the importation of these drugs and ensure that they are cleared away from the shelves,” he said.

The Bishops’ call forms part of their broader concerns about the growing drug menace and its implications for young people and communities across the country.

They are urging authorities to strengthen enforcement against the illegal supply of drugs while expanding efforts to prevent substance abuse among the youth.

Ghana News.title: Health experts warn women against unregulated breast enlargement products, herbal remedies
Ghana News.content:
Health experts have cautioned women against relying on unregulated breast enlargement products and herbal remedies to address breast-related concerns, warning that some may contain harmful substances or delay the diagnosis of serious conditions.

The warning was issued during a breast cancer awareness programme organised by the Ministry of Roads and Highways in Accra.

A midwife at the Ridge Hospital, Abigail Asiamah, said some women delay seeking medical attention when they notice changes in their breasts because they turn to herbal preparations or other unverified treatments.

She warned that such practices could make it more difficult for health professionals to diagnose and treat conditions at an early stage.

“To our women who are hiding in pain and visiting the herbalist, there is hope. Walk to any health facility and get treatment early,” she said.

Madam Asiamah also raised concerns about products marketed as breast enlargement solutions, cautioning that some may contain chemicals or other substances that could have harmful effects on the body.

“The medications we take to enhance our boobs may contain harmful chemicals. Let’s use the right channel to get things done rather than using medications that are not prescribed by the doctor,” she said.

The caution comes as Ghana joins global efforts to raise awareness of breast cancer during October, which is observed internationally as Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Breast cancer remains a major health concern in Ghana, with early detection considered critical to improving treatment outcomes.

Data from the Global Cancer Observatory show that Ghana recorded 5,025 new breast cancer cases in 2022, representing 18.4% of all cancers diagnosed in the country.

The disease also accounted for 2,369 deaths, representing 13.2% of all cancer deaths recorded that year.

Health professionals say these figures underscore the importance of paying attention to changes in the breasts and seeking medical assessment promptly.

A lump or swelling, changes in the size or shape of the breast, changes around the nipple, and unusual discharge are among symptoms that should not be ignored.

Although not every breast change is cancerous, health professionals advise that unusual changes should be assessed by a qualified professional rather than treated based on assumptions.

Early detection can improve the chances of successful treatment and reduce the risk of the disease progressing to more advanced

Ghana News.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
Ghana News.content:
There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola but some have been trialed.

Kenya has confirmed its first case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.

Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people have died. However, the World Health Organisation (WHO) declared the country free of the disease in August.

Since then, all cases of the disease have been declared in the DR Congo.

The current outbreak has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no known vaccine.

Duale confirmed that the Kenyan national had tested positive for the Bundibugyo species.

According to the minister, the patient first travelled by road from DR Congo to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, where he boarded a flight to Nairobi.

Duale said that after being taken to the Nairobi Hospital, the patient was transferred to an isolation facility which was built during the COVID-19 pandemic.

It was there that the patient "developed fever, chills, intense fatigue and weakness, painful swallowing, muscle pain and bleeding under the skin".

"Doctors suspected a viral haemorrhagic fever based on his symptoms and travel history and collected samples for testing. The sample tested positive for Ebola Bundibugyo virus," Duale said.

The patient died at 23:30 (20:30 GMT) on Monday, and his burial is planned for later on Tuesday in line with public health safety protocols.

At least 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers, have been identified, while health authorities are tracing a further 23 passengers and four crew members who travelled on the same flight.

So far, WHO has recorded 4,082 deaths out of 8,463 cases since the emergence of the Bundibugyo species of the virus.

There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for the species, which is highly infectious.

Ghana News.title: Assemblies of God World Congress: Ghana to host first African edition from October 14 to 16
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is set to host the Assemblies of God World Congress for the first time on the African continent, with more than 10,000 delegates and visitors expected to participate in the three-day event.

The congress, scheduled for October 14 to 16, will bring together members of Assemblies of God from different parts of the world for worship, revival, seminars and discussions on the church’s global mission.

Speaking on Joy FM's Super Morning Show on October 6, Special Aide to the General Superintendent of Assemblies of God Ghana, Evangeline Gbenartey, described the event as a historic moment for Ghana and the African continent.

“This year’s World Congress is so special because it is coming to Africa for the first time and to Ghana.”

The World Congress is held every three years and provides an opportunity for members of Assemblies of God worldwide to meet, worship and renew their commitment to the church’s mission.

According to Ms. Gbenartey, Ghana was selected through a voting process involving participating countries, following a proposal from Tanzania.

This year’s congress is being held under the theme “Commission: One Mandate, Every Nation.”

The theme reflects the church’s focus on fulfilling its global evangelistic mission and expanding its presence through church planting.

Ms. Gbenartey explained that Assemblies of God Worldwide has an ambitious agenda to plant one million churches around the world.

“Assemblies of God Worldwide is focused on one particular agenda. This agenda focuses on getting one million churches planted worldwide.”

She said the congress is therefore expected to serve as a platform for participants to renew their commitment to spreading the gospel across nations.

Organisers expect more than 10,000 people to attend the congress, making it one of the major international religious gatherings to be hosted in Ghana.

The programme will include daytime seminars as well as evening open-air gatherings featuring worship and other activities.

Ms. Gbenartey urged Ghanaians to take advantage of the occasion and participate in the activities.

“Everyone is invited. Please come.”

Beyond its religious significance, organisers believe the congress could provide a boost to several sectors of Ghana’s economy.

The arrival of thousands of visitors is expected to create increased demand for hotels, restaurants, transportation and other services.

“Imagine the resources to our hospitality industry. Imagine the transport industry. Imagine the food industry. The restaurants. Everyone.”

Ms. Gbenartey said the event would give businesses an opportunity to benefit from the influx of international visitors.

She also believes the congress will help showcase Ghana as a welcoming destination for major international events.

For the organisers, hosting the World Congress in Ghana is also an opportunity to challenge negative perceptions about Africa.

Ms. Gbenartey said international visitors will have the chance to experience Ghana and see the opportunities available on the continent.

“There are still people who believe that Africa is a dungeon. It’s not.”

She added: “Africa is thriving. And this is a chance for people to change their lives.”

Ghana News.title: Humanity Haven Foundation supports 100 pupils in Wiamoase with educational supplies
Ghana News.content:
Humanity Haven Foundation (HHF), an Ashanti Region-based non-governmental organisation, has presented essential educational supplies to 100 basic school pupils in Wiamoase, located within the Sekyere South Municipality.

The items, which included school bags, exercise books, pens, pencils, and mathematical sets were handed over to selected beneficiaries during a brief ceremony held on Friday morning at the local Salvation Army Church.

Speaking at the event, Madam Emelia Frimpong, President of the Foundation, explained that the donation aims to motivate pupils and ensure they remain committed to their education.

"As a foundation, our research revealed that many parents struggle to purchase basic learning materials when schools reopen," Madam Frimpong noted.

She added, "we stepped in to alleviate this burden and ensure these young learners do not miss out on quality education due to a lack of supplies."



Expressing gratitude on behalf of the municipal education directorate, Mr. Andrew Osei Twumasi, the Sekyere South Deputy Director in charge of Supervision and Monitoring, commended the foundation for its timely intervention.

He urged parents to ensure their children maintain the materials and make consistent use of them in school.

Additionally, Mr. Twumasi praised local school administrators for their dedication to student oversight and encouraged teachers to instill strong moral values alongside academic instruction.

"We are deeply grateful to Humanity Haven Foundation for this support," Mr. Twumasi stated.

He added, "I charge the beneficiaries to make good use of these items so that this investment in their future yields meaningful results for the entire community."



Elaborating on the foundation’s vision, Emmanuel Asante Amoabeng, Secretary to Humanity Haven, disclosed that the organization was established three years ago to support marginalized populations, including prison inmates, orphans, and underserved rural communities.

Operating with a core team of 34 members, the foundation funds its initiatives primarily through internal member contributions.

While outreaches are currently conducted on an annual basis, Mr. Amoabeng noted that the group aims to increase the frequency of its interventions as it expands its volunteer network.

"We hope our ongoing humanitarian efforts will inspire more benevolent individuals to join us so we can scale our support to those most in need," he said.



Beyond the general donation, the foundation announced two key welfare commitments.

These were the full educational adoption of two young boys, and ongoing support for a bedridden mother in the community who has been struggling to keep her child in school.

Ghana News.title: Local Government Service HR practitioners urged to embrace digital systems
Ghana News.content:
The Head of the Local Government Service, Professor Lord Mensah, has urged human resource practitioners within Ghana’s Local Government Service to embrace the digital revolution to enhance efficiency and improve service delivery.

He warned that human resource managers who continue to rely on analogue methods of working risk being left behind as the public service increasingly adopts digital systems.

Professor Lord Mensah was speaking at the 2nd Annual General Conference of the Human Resource Practitioners of Local Government Service–Ghana (HRPLGS-G), held in Kumasi.

He said human resource practitioners must ensure that staff report to work on time, remain at post during official working hours and are productive enough to meet the expectations of leadership and the demands of the Service.

“It is important for them not to be left behind because of the digital revolution we find ourselves in. If you continue to do things the analogue way, by the time you realise it, you may no longer be part of the Service because the Service would have moved far ahead,” he said.

Professor Mensah also urged HR practitioners to ensure that information provided for decision-making is accurate and credible.

He explained that inaccurate data could negatively affect decisions taken by management, particularly as the Public Service works towards introducing new digital systems.

“As for computer programmes, when you feed them with wrong information, they will also give you wrong information, and that can affect decision-making,” he added.

According to him, the Public Service is developing software that will require reliable data from Human Resource practitioners to support effective planning and decision-making.

The conference brought together Human Resource managers from various Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies across the country to deliberate on challenges confronting the profession and ways of improving Human Resource management.

The conference also featured the election of new executives for the Human Resource Practitioners of Local Government Service–Ghana.

The President and Convener of the Association, Mr. Vivien Akumiah, also called on the government to invest more in capacity building and training for staff of the Local Government Service.

He said inadequate funding continues to affect the ability of the Service to provide regular training and professional development opportunities for its personnel.

“We lack training because we always lack funds to train. When we get support to build our capacities, I think it will go a long way to help Ghana,” she said.

She noted that Human Resource practitioners operate across the country’s 276 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies and play a critical role in advancing Ghana’s decentralisation agenda.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Malaysia’s Anwar to host Myanmar leader as repatriations near 10,000
World.content:
Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing to visit Kuala Lumpur ‘in the next few days’, Anwar Ibrahim says.

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says about 10,000 ⁠people have been sent back to Myanmar since January, despite safety warnings by human rights groups and the United Nations refugee agency.

Anwar told parliament on Tuesday that a number of those deported were sent back by ⁠planes arranged by the Myanmar government, while nearly 1,500 were returned by sea last week as part of a bilateral arrangement.

Anwar acknowledged concerns by rights groups and lawmakers over the ⁠potential safety risks faced by those being repatriated, especially those from the Rohingya Muslim minority, but said Myanmar authorities had given ⁠assurances that they would not be harmed ⁠upon their return.

“The conditions that we placed on Myanmar is that they must bring home their citizens,” Anwar said. “Secondly, it is that they treat their people fairly so ‌that there are no abuses, coercion or rights violations.”

Anwar said he would continue to discuss the ‌matter ‌with Myanmar’s President Min Aung Hlaing, who is due to visit Kuala Lumpur “in the next few days”.

The visit is part of a diplomatic push for legitimacy by the Myanmar leader, whose 2021 coup plunged Myanmar into civil war and who led a 2017 military crackdown that forced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya people to flee the country.

Malaysia insists all returnees agreed to repatriation, but rights monitors have raised concerns that Myanmar refugees had little choice.

The UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said last week that its staff was not allowed to meet the Myanmar nationals to confirm whether their decisions to return “were genuinely free and informed”.



The deportations come amid escalating raids on refugee communities in Malaysia by immigration officials, which led to the detention of more than 50,000 refugees in 2026.

Rohingya make up the majority of Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, but it remains unclear how many members of the persecuted group were among those deported.

Malaysia took in about 193,000 refugees from Myanmar, according to UN data.

While Malaysia is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention and treats refugees as undocumented migrants, it is home to about 215,600 refugees and asylum seekers registered with the UNHCR.

Myanmar has been accused of committing genocide against the Rohingya. Earlier this year, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) opened its first genocide case it has heard in full in more than a decade.

The UNHCR and rights groups said returnees could face persecution and forced military conscription in an active war zone. Myanmar has been embroiled in a civil war since the military seized power from the elected government in 2021.

The war has killed more than 100,000 people since the coup, according to the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) project.
