World.title: Nigeria mourns 32 killed as military plane crashes into swamp
World.content:
Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has declared three days of national mourning after a military aircraft crashed in southern Ondo State, killing 32 people.

Authorities say the plane was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when it came down in a swamp near a naval base on Monday morning. After reaching the site, the aircraft was found to be submerged under water, officials said.

A resident told the BBC that clothes and shoes had been found at the site. Smoke could be seen rising from the area.

Tinubu offered his deepest condolences for the 25 passengers and seven crew members on board and has ordered a full investigation.

The president also ordered national flags to be flown at half-mast across the country as a mark of respect for those who died.

"This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation," Tinubu said.

"Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten," he added.

Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo earlier said he had been informed "of the disappearance of a military aircraft with tail number NGR 931, enroute Lagos from Benin at 0913 hours earlier today".

He said "efforts to raise the aircraft on radio proved abortive" before subsequent confirmation that it had crashed near a naval base in Igbokoda, Ondo state.

He said search and rescue efforts were ongoing.

The crashed plane, described as an ATR-42 aircraft, carries between 30 and 50 passengers, according to its manufacturers.

World.title: Separatist party projected to win Quebec election, adding new test to Canada's unity
World.content:
Canada's Parti QuÃ©bÃ©cois (PQ) is projected to have won enough seats in Quebec's provincial election to form a minority government, though the separatists will need other parties' support to achieve their aims - such as a new public vote on independence.

It marks the first time the PQ has been in power since 2014, with Paul St-Pierre Plamondon set to become the province's new leader.

In his victory speech, St-Pierre Plamondon again raised his independence plans but vowed to be "the premier of everyone in Quebec".

The result could prove a fresh test for Prime Minister Mark Carney, also setting up confrontations with QuÃ©bec over issues like immigration and the monarchy.

In its effort to achieve independence, the PQ has pledged to hold a referendum on separating from the rest of Canada.

The majority French-speaking province has held other votes on this, in 1980 and 1995. On both occasions, the independence movement was defeated. Polls indicate only 30% of Quebecers back such a move this time.

St-Pierre Plamondon has previously said the vote would occur after President Donald Trump is out of office south of the border in the United States, explaining that would require "conditions that allow for an informed and serene debate". The US and Canada are in a trade war as a result of Trump's programme of tariffs.

In his victory speech after Monday's election results, St-Pierre Plamondon said of the potential referendum: "Our national destiny will be achieved one day."

But it is not clear how the PQ leader would secure the vote that he wants - given that rival parties, upon whose support he would depend, oppose independence.

With most votes counted on Tuesday morning, the party was set to win fewer than the 64 seats needed to command a majority in the province's assembly, according to projections from Canadian media.

The Liberals - the party of Carney's government - are projected to have increased their number of seats in the assembly, as have the Conservatives.

All parties benefited from the collapse of the Coalition Avenir QuÃ©bec (CAQ), which was previously the province's governing party but is not projected to have won a single seat this time.

Carney congratulated Plamondon, saying he looked forward to working with the new provincial leader, adding: "Building a stronger Quebec is at the heart of our mission to build a stronger Canada."

World.title: Fort Hood shooter to be executed by firing squad - a first for US military since World War Two
World.content:
The Pentagon has announced it will execute a former US Army major by firing squad, the first such military execution in more than 60 years.

Nidal Malik Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US soldiers at Fort Hood in 2009, injuring another 32.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell announced on social media on Monday that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth had made the recommendation and President Donald Trump approved it.

It will be the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War Two.

Parnell said the secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution.

"Judgement day for Hasan has finally come," he wrote on X.

Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist from Virginia, killed 13 soldiers at the base in Texas in 2009 and later admitted in court he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".

He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

The attack took place in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

Hasan is currently one of four inmates on the US military's death row.

A military execution requires approval from the US president, according to military law.

It also requires appellate review and a final judgment on its legality to move forward.

The US Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces deemed the military death penalty unconstitutional in 1983 but it was reinstated the following year by an executive order under then-President Ronald Reagan.

Military executions differ from those carried out at the state level.

The majority of executions in the US are carried out on the state level, with 27 states, the military and the federal government still having capital punishment as a legally available option.

Death by firing squad is rather uncommon. There was an execution by firing squad carried out last year in South Carolina, a first for the state and the first time the method was used in the US in 15 years.

Four other states allow the use of a firing squad, including Idaho, Mississippi, Oklahoma and Utah.

World.title: OpenAI admits response to Australian government hacks 'not good enough'
World.content:
OpenAI has admitted its actions were "not good enough" after one of its rogue agents breached Australian government websites in June, saying it had added more precautions to its training environments.

The company's chief strategy officer Jason Kwon faced a parliamentary hearing into AI on Tuesday in Sydney, saying the breach "should not have happened" and it "should have handled our response better". It took weeks before Australia was notified via an email to a generic inbox.

"We are sorry and we know we have work to do to rebuild trust with the Australian people," Kwon said.

Anthropic also appeared and said it had not found any cases of Australian breaches during a recent investigation.

Executives from Microsoft and Google were also present.

An OpenAI agent went "rogue" and "infiltrated" a private statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare in June, in what cyber-security experts said was the first hack of its kind.

When asked why OpenAI had not directly contacted government ministers immediately after it found out about the breaches, Kwon acknowledged it was a mistake.

"In retrospect, we should have done what you're suggesting," Kwon said.

"The reason why it happened the way that it did is I think people were thinking about this as a technical situation and they wanted to contact the technical counterparties, but it's not good enough."

Kwon said the company has changed how it handles such incidents.

"Even if we don't fully understand the situation, we are just going to notify and start working through the situation collaboratively with the impacted party."

OpenAI has also added "more precautions" to its training environments since the incidents, Kwon told the 12-member committee, which is made up of Labor, Liberal and independent MPs and senators looking at AI and its impact on Australia.

The company was also establishing a local taskforce in Australia to investigate "how to better manage the risks associated with increasingly capable AI", it said.

Kwon told the committee that training models were now monitored in real time during tests, and that an alarm was triggered if they interacted with the internet in a way they were not meant to.

This meant that OpenAI had been able to alert the New South Wales government to another hack last week within 48 hours.

The company would also support a framework on mandatory disclosure of incidents, Kwon said, as it would set out "clear expectations".

"We were trying to come up with a standard to apply to our voluntary actionsâ¦ Based on our learned experience here, we should have been probably talking to more people about how to do that well."

Anthropic's head of safeguards Dave Orr said that in the wake of OpenAI agents hacking tech platform Hugging Face in July, it had reviewed "hundreds of millions of transcripts" to detect any potential breaches of Australian government websites similar to OpenAI.

"We haven't found anything like this and we have looked," he told the committee.

The public hearings, which will continue until Friday, also heard evidence from arts and media organisations about copyright and their concerns on how AI models use their materials. AI companies want Australia to relax copyright laws so they can use books and music, for example, to train their AI models.

An opt-out model - where the onus would be on the artist to ask AI not to use their material for training purposes - was flawed and could mean artists do not get paid for their content, the committee heard.

"In other words, Australia's artists will be the roadkill in the rush to this AI deal," said Annabelle Herd, chief executive of the Australian Recording Industry Association.

Anthropic's special envoy Jeff Bleich told the hearing the company had "never tried to dictate" to Australia on its copyright laws.

World.title: CSOs demand probe of TikTok blackout in Northern Nigeria
World.content:
A coalition of 12 civil society organisations (CSOs) has called on the federal government, telecom regulators, and TikTok to address an unexplained disruption affecting the social media platform in parts of northern Nigeria.

In a joint press statement, the coalition raised alarms over a “multi-week digital blackout” that began as intermittent access difficulties around 14 September.

The outage has primarily impacted users in Kaduna, Kebbi, Kano, and Sokoto states.

Preliminary investigations by the groups reveal that millions of citizens reliant on the platform for their livelihoods are struggling to load contents, view videos, or upload media via standard mobile data connections.

The coalition noted that the issue spans multiple internet service providers, with access currently only guaranteed for users bypassing the network via Virtual Private Networks (VPNs).

Despite over two weeks of disruption, no official cause has been established by platform operators or government authorities, the group lamented, demanding an explanation.

“Unexplained social media disruptions not only undermine democracy but also truncate the local economy,” the coalition stated, expressing grave concern over the continued institutional silence surrounding the situation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

To resolve the impasse and restore public trust, the coalition—which includes Paradigm Initiative, Media Rights Agenda (MRA), Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID), and Spaces for Change, among others—outlined several key recommendations.

Investigate and publicly disclose causes

It urged the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), and affected state governments to collaboratively investigate the blackout and publish their findings.

If the disruption is an intentional block, it said the authorities must immediately halt any throttling or restriction that lacks a clear legal foundation, strictly adhering to Section 39 of the 1999 Constitution (as amended) regarding freedom of expression.

Should any official order or directive exist regarding TikTok’s access, its legal basis, scope, and duration must be disclosed to the public, the group said.

It added that mobile operators should be required to issue timely outage notifications to consumers.

The NCC was urged to conduct independent technical testing to check for DNS interference, IP blocking, or network filtering.

Require Action from TikTok

The group demanded that the platform itself clarify whether technical glitches or infrastructure changes on its end are responsible for the outages in northern Nigeria.

Authorities were advised against penalising citizens, journalists, or researchers documenting the outage, and urged not to implement overly broad restrictions on VPN usage.

The coalition called for the implementation of a national Internet disruption transparency protocol and requested that the NCC publish a comprehensive final report outlining the cause, government involvement (if any), and remedial measures taken.

“The reported disruption to TikTok access in parts of northern Nigeria warrants prompt, transparent, and independent investigation,” the coalition concluded, committing to monitor the situation continuously as further evidence becomes available.

World.title: 2027: Lulu-Briggs dismisses Rainbow Coalition, vows to transform Rivers if elected governor
World.content:
Dumo Lulu-Briggs, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Rivers State, said he is unperturbed by the much-talked-about Rainbow Coalition, insisting that the power to determine the state’s future ultimately rests with the people.

Speaking with journalists in Port Harcourt on Monday on his “Reset Rivers” agenda, Mr Lulu-Briggs said he had “ultimate confidence” in the ability of Rivers people to make informed choices at the ballot box.

The Rainbow Coalition is a multi-party political arrangement created by Federal Capital Territory Minister, Nyesom Wike, a former governor of Rivers.

“I’m not bothered about any coalition,” he said. “I have ultimate confidence in the capacity of Rivers people to make an informed decision. The people will protect their votes and ensure that their votes count.”

Drawing a biblical analogy, he added: “If I may reference that time in the Bible when Goliath was beating his chest and asking, ‘Where is that man in Israel?’ David came, and Goliath fell. So, I’m not bothered about any coalition.”

Speaks against ethnic division

Mr Lulu-Briggs lamented what he described as the growing culture of ethnic division in Rivers, warning that politicians who exploit ethnic sentiments for political gain are damaging the social fabric of the state.

“I don’t understand this stuff about ethnicity in Rivers State,” he said. “We grew up not knowing who was Kalabari, who was Ikwerre, who was Ogoni; we were all brothers and sisters. Today, we have become so disunited and spiteful of one another.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, ethnicity, religion and similar considerations cannot serve as the foundation for effective governance.

“Ethnicity, like religion, is not a value-respecting tool for running a successful state,” he stated. “We must open up the political space and give everybody a fair chance.”

Discloses how he’ll tackle unemployment

Mr Lulu-Briggs described the unemployment situation in Rivers as alarming, noting that despite its abundant human and natural resources, the state continues to struggle to create jobs.

He pledged to pursue an aggressive economic expansion strategy, saying his administration would focus on skills development, entrepreneurship and private-sector growth.

“We are going to invest heavily in human opportunity,” he said. “We will equip our people with the skills and tools they need to succeed in a highly competitive economy.”

The NDC candidate said he would provide interest-free loans to small and medium-scale businesses through financial institutions if elected governor.

“If you need ₦2 million, ₦10 million, ₦20 million or ₦30 million and you have a bankable business, we will support you,” he said. “We are going to be very deliberate about creating employment and growing businesses.”

He also set an ambitious target of expanding Rivers State’s economy from about $20 billion to $200 billion over time.

“If we are going to grow our GDP from $20 billion to $200 billion, it means almost every home will become a workshop,” he said. “There will be opportunities for our young people everywhere.”

The businessman-turned-politician stressed that transparency and accountability would be central pillars of his administration if elected governor.

“Every penny we make from internally generated revenue and every allocation we receive will be made public,” he declared. “Communities will have input into the budgeting process. Transparency must be the standard.”

He added: “If you are not transparent, then you are not able to achieve anything in that state.”

Mr Lulu-Briggs explained that the “Reset Rivers” mantra goes beyond politics and seeks to restore public confidence in governance, rebuild institutions and reposition the economy.

“Today, Rivers State is split,” he said. “We have become so hateful of one another that even if your twin brother belongs to another political party, you have to be careful how often you visit him.”

“Our politics has become so divisive. If we don’t get the politics right, we won’t get governance right. And if we don’t get governance right, the economy will continue to suffer.”

Comparing Rivers’ economic trajectory with that of Lagos State, he argued that both states were on similar economic footing in 1999 but have since moved in vastly different directions.

“In 1999, Lagos and Rivers had GDPs of about $20 billion. Today, Rivers remains around $20 billion, while Lagos has grown to over $250 billion. That tells the story of stagnation.”

He cited the poor state of critical infrastructure, including the Port Harcourt International Airport and seaports, as evidence of the state’s economic decline.

Recalling a recent meeting with a delegation from the British High Commission, Mr Lulu-Briggs said the lack of electricity and air conditioning in the VIP lounge at Port Harcourt International Airport embarrassed the state.

“When I arrived, there was no air conditioning, no electricity and everywhere was dark,” he recounted. “I asked the delegation, ‘You don’t need me to say anything. It speaks for itself.’”

‘You have to reset Rivers politics’

The NDC candidate said Rivers must urgently reset its politics, governance and economy to unlock its enormous potential.

“You have to reset the politics, open up the political space and allow broad participation,” he said. “You have to reset governance so institutions work and the rule of law is respected. You have to reset the economy and create growth opportunities.”

He also emphasised the importance of education in tackling poverty and driving sustainable development.

“We must invest heavily in education. Our public schools used to be among the best. We need to return to those standards because education remains the surest path to prosperity.”

Responding to the allegations that he often sacrifices political ambition for personal business interests, Mr Lulu-Briggs firmly rejected the claims, insisting that his political involvement is driven by service and concern for Rivers people rather than financial gain.

“I’m not a regular politician. What drives me into politics is my humanity. In and out of season, I continue to invest in the lives of Rivers people.

He recounted his decisions following the 2019 and 2023 elections, saying he chose actions he believed were in the broader interest of peace and stability in Rivers.

“My primary concern has always been Rivers State and its young people. Whatever I will do to ensure that Rivers State is prioritised, I will do.”

Mr Lulu-Briggs also dismissed suggestions that he has business interests in Lubrik Construction, a company that has featured in public discussions in Rivers politics. He challenged anyone with evidence linking him to the company to make it public.

“Not a penny has come to me from Lubrik,” he declared. “I have no direct or indirect relationship with the company. If it is because of me that their contracts were cancelled, then I am asking that their contracts be returned.”

Mr Lulu-Briggs urged Rivers people to embrace a shared vision for the future and support what he described as a comprehensive agenda for renewal.

“It’s not about candidates. It’s about making sure our state is productive, and our people are productive. Every second and every minute, I will do my utmost for the benefit and well-being of Rivers people.”

World.title: Russia vs Nigeria Preview: Super Eagles face stern test as Chelle demands victory
World.content:
The Super Eagles will look to end a turbulent international window on a high when they face Russia in a friendly at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on Tuesday.

Kick-off is scheduled for 6pm Nigerian time, with Eric Chelle’s side seeking a response after a mixed opening to the window.

Nigeria began with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign before suffering a 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau.

The setback has raised expectations for a stronger showing against Russia, with striker Akor Adams saying Chelle has set victory as the target despite the squad changes.

“There are a lot of new boys in the squad, but it’s still the Super Eagles,” Adams said in an interview with NFF TV.

“The coach has made it clear – we have to win. Russia are a good team. They’re hungry to play games because of their peculiar situation (FIFA ban). For us, it is to give our best, come out with a good result and a good performance.”

Chelle works with changed squad

Chelle has had to adjust his plans following a series of withdrawals and player-release issues.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Captain Wilfred Ndidi is out with an injury, while Eintracht Frankfurt did not release Raphael Onyedika. Bright Osayi-Samuel is also unavailable, while goalkeeper Maduka Okoye, who was not initially invited, will not feature.

The squad eventually reached 19 players following the late call-up of Ibrahim Ajasa. The FC Rostov midfielder joined the team in Nizhny Novgorod ahead of the game.

Among those in camp are Stanley Nwabali, Emmanuel Fernandez, Benjamin Frederick, Kenneth Igboke, Chibuzor Nwoko, Umar Abubakar, Peter Edokpolor, Abdullahi Bewene, Umar Abdullai, Atata Michael, Aderemi Adeoye, Isaac James and Michael Stephen.

The reshuffle gives several fringe players a chance to make a strong impression on the coaching staff.

Iheanacho returns

Kelechi Iheanacho is expected to return to the starting line-up after missing Nigeria’s recent AFCON qualifiers.

The Bursaspor forward has been recalled after more than 16 months away from the national team and comes into the fixture in impressive form, having scored 11 goals in eight appearances in Turkey.

His return could provide additional firepower alongside Moses Simon and Adams, while the Russia friendly offers Iheanacho an opportunity to re-establish himself in Chelle’s plans.

“I am really happy to be here, and I will enjoy it with the boys, and hopefully we will have a very lovely outing on Tuesday,” Iheanacho said in an interview with the Super Eagles media team.

Russia bring strong momentum

Russia will start as confident hosts after recording consecutive victories over Iran and Namibia.

Their latest result was particularly emphatic, a 6-0 demolition of Namibia on Saturday that showcased the attacking depth available to Valery Karpin.

Dynamo Moscow forward Konstantin Tyukavin scored in that victory and remains one of the players Nigeria will have to monitor closely. He has also contributed four goals and an assist in seven league appearances this season.

Russia will also be without some key personnel, with Aleksandr Golovin sidelined by an ankle injury and Krasnodar striker Dmitry Vorobyov leaving the camp.

Despite those absences, the hosts have enough attacking options to pose a significant test for Nigeria.

Tuesday’s meeting will be only their second.

Their first encounter ended 1-1 at Moscow’s Luzhniki Stadium in June 2025.

Russia took the lead through a Semi Ajayi own goal before Tolu Arokodare equalised in the 71st minute, scoring his first goal for the Super Eagles after capitalising on a poor back pass.

More than 38,000 tickets have been sold for Tuesday’s return fixture at the 41,300-capacity Nizhny Novgorod Stadium.

The Verdict

This is a useful test for a Nigeria side still taking shape under Chelle.

The coach will want more defensive discipline than his team showed against Guinea-Bissau. At the same time, the return of Iheanacho and the involvement of several less-established players offer chances to assess his options.

Russia, meanwhile, arrive with the confidence of a side that has scored seven goals in its last two matches.

With both teams missing important players, the contest could come down to which side adapts better to the changes.

For the Super Eagles, however, Chelle’s brief is clear: deliver a convincing performance and leave Nizhny Novgorod with a positive result.

World.title: Gymnastics Federation appoints 44 coaches for national teams
World.content:
The Gymnastics Federation of Nigeria (GFN) has appointed 44 coaches to handle various disciplines across its national teams.

The appointments cover senior and junior teams in artistic gymnastics, aerobics gymnastics, trampoline, double mini trampoline (DMT), tumbling, parkour, acrobatics and rhythmic gymnastics.

The list was contained in a statement signed by Rose Verisimo, the federation’s technical director.

Isaiah Oni Erhunwunse (OLY) has been appointed head coach of the senior men’s artistic gymnastics team, with Bala Magaji Juwara and Anthony Duilemi as assistants.

Helen Albert will head the senior women’s artistic gymnastics team, assisted by Edem Umor Patric and Adejoh Emmanuel.

For the junior teams, Kennedy Osawaro will head the men’s artistic gymnastics team, assisted by Jimoh Wasiu and Jimoh Azeez. At the same time, Abosede Olatundun Oladele will lead the women’s team, with Deborah Ajiboye and Noel Egbunu as assistants.

In aerobics gymnastics, Edina Ahue has been appointed senior head coach, with David West Tamunuosaki and Jennifer Eke as assistants. Michael Ocheke will lead the junior team, assisted by Dimeji Aluko and Toyosi Glory Adeyemi.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Dorcas Abel will head the senior men’s trampoline, DMT and tumbling team, with Osamudiamwenam Amennaghawon as assistant coach.

Osasu Obasohan will lead the senior women’s team, assisted by Godwin Bamidele and Awokunle Ojo.

Michael Jos, Stephen Taiwo and Christopher Akhidenor will handle the junior men’s team, while Adekemi Ademuwagun, David Egbunu and Ashiagu Charles will take charge of the junior women.

Federation targets Los Angeles 2028

GFN President Kelvin Erhunwunse said the appointments were based on the coaches’ experience and records in their respective disciplines.

“These appointments were made based on merit, dedication, and the track records of the individuals. We have absolute confidence that these coaches possess the requisite experience and passion to elevate Nigerian gymnastics to unprecedented heights,” he said.

Mr Erhunwunse said the federation’s immediate objective was to improve Nigeria’s medal prospects at international competitions, with qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles also among its targets.

“Our primary goal is clear: we want to produce world-class athletes who will not only dominate the African continent but also stand on the podium at the global stage.

“Preparation for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics begins now, and we are putting the right technical crew in place to achieve this vision.”

He urged the newly appointed coaches to approach their responsibilities with discipline and professionalism.

“I urge all our coaches to view this appointment as a sacred call to serve our fatherland. We expect high levels of discipline, professionalism, and teamwork as you groom the next generation of Nigerian gymnastics,” Mr Erhunwunse said.

Other appointments

Victoria Itodo was appointed head coach of the senior women’s parkour team, while Olorunfemi Samuel Adeyemi will lead the senior men. Davidson Erhunwunse will handle the junior men, with Stephen Soyimiegha listed as an assistant coach.

In acrobatics, Elkana Sabo will head the senior team, assisted by Friday Omigie, while Kunle Adedoyin and Amos Dauda will handle the junior team.

Cathrine Sasode was appointed head coach and general coordinator for the senior rhythmic gymnastics team, with Valentina Ojo as assistant. Chinedu Oyegbata will lead the junior team, assisted by Praise Amsey.

The federation also appointed Lesli Amadi as head coach for Gymnastics for All, with Kayode Olusegun Adesola and Maureen Ugiagbe as assistants.

Uwa Anthonia was named safeguarding officer, while Mary Ibrahim was appointed anti-doping officer. Mr Erhunwunse will serve as gymnastics development director, while Ms Verisimo will retain her position as technical director.

The appointments are expected to form part of the federation’s technical structure as it prepares its athletes for upcoming national and international competitions.

World.title: Alleged Sexual Affairs: Apostle Sam Pamilerin apologises, steps aside
World.content:
Apostle Sam Pamilerin of Elijah Generation Church has apologised following allegations of sexual misconduct made against him by several women from his congregation.

The women, in leaked WhatsApp conversations, accused Mr Pamilerin of having sexual relationships with female church members between 2019 and 2026, including shortly before his wedding.

According to the women, his alleged conduct previously prompted some members to leave the church. They said others stayed after believing he had repented, only to discover the alleged behaviour later continued.

The women also accused the cleric of showing little remorse and allegedly believing that no one could hold him accountable. They expressed concern about the welfare of women within his church and ministry, alleging that he had manipulated and indoctrinated some of them.

However, Mr Pamilerin acknowledged some of the allegations in a statement published on his Facebook page on Monday. He admitted that he was sexually involved with some women before his wedding.

He also said he had stepped back from his ministerial responsibilities to seek counsel and address issues from his past.

He said: “Over the past few weeks, I have stepped back from public ministry and social media to reflect, seek counsel, and honestly address matters from my past. Before I was married, I was involved in sexual relationships with women that I deeply regret.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Although these events occurred before my marriage, I acknowledge that my actions were wrong and fell short of the standards of holiness, integrity, and self-control I am called to uphold as a Christian and minister of the Gospel.”

Full responsibility

Mr Pamilerin also acknowledged his actions and said he had taken responsibility.

He added that he had apologised to his wife, family, church, colleagues and everyone who had looked up to him for spiritual guidance.

He said he has since sought God’s guidance and consulted pastoral and professional advisers.

“I take full responsibility for my actions and sincerely apologise to the women involved for any hurt, disappointment, or harm I may have caused. I also apologise to my wife, my family, my church, my colleagues, and everyone who has trusted me and looked to me for spiritual leadership.

“I am not making excuses for what happened or seeking to minimise it because it occurred before my marriage. I have been seeking God, receiving pastoral and professional counsel, examining my conduct honestly, and taking necessary steps toward genuine repentance and accountability”, said Mr Pamilerin.

Consequences acceptance

He said he sincerely regretted his actions and pledged to conduct himself with greater integrity, responsibility and accountability going forward.

According to Mr Pamilerin, he was willing to bear the consequences of his actions and remain subject to relevant spiritual, pastoral and professional accountability.

“I recognise that repentance is demonstrated not only through words, but through changed conduct, accountability, and a willingness to accept the consequences of one’s actions. I will therefore continue to submit myself to appropriate spiritual, pastoral, and professional accountability throughout this process.

“I ask for prayer, not that my actions would be excused, but that I would have the humility and courage to face them honestly, make amends where appropriate, protect those affected, and allow God to produce genuine transformation in my life.”

World.title: Russia vs Nigeria: Five danger men Super Eagles must contain
World.content:
The Super Eagles will face a Russia side brimming with attacking confidence when the two countries meet at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on Tuesday.

Valery Karpin’s men head into the international friendly on the back of an emphatic 6-0 victory over Namibia on Saturday, a result that showcased the depth and variety of their attacking options.

The scoreline was built around several impressive individual performances, with five players standing out for their contributions.

For Nigeria, Tuesday’s encounter will offer a different kind of defensive test, with Russia bringing midfielders capable of scoring from distance, forwards who can exploit space inside the box, and substitutes who can change the game.

Lechi Sadulaev

Gone are the glorious days of Andrey Arshavin as Lechi Sadulaev heads the list after producing the performance that earned him the Player of the Match award against Namibia.

The Akhmat Grozny midfielder opened the scoring and was a constant influence in the attacking third, displaying the confidence to move into dangerous positions and make things happen around the penalty area.

Sadulaev’s performance highlighted the attacking responsibilities he carries from midfield. His movement can pull defenders out of position, while his willingness to join attacks gives Russia an additional body around the box.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria’s midfield will therefore have to maintain its shape and avoid giving him the freedom to dictate proceedings in advanced areas.

Maksim Glushenkov

Maksim Glushenkov showed the quality Russia can bring off the bench.

The Zenit attacking midfielder came on against Namibia and quickly established his influence, scoring after his introduction before playing another important role in Russia’s sixth goal.

Glushenkov also delivered the corner that eventually produced the final goal of the contest, underlining his ability to contribute from open play and set-piece situations.

His presence gives Karpin another attacking weapon, particularly in the latter stages when defensive fatigue begins to create spaces.

Konstantin Tyukavin

Konstantin Tyukavin also made his impact after coming off the bench against Namibia.

The Dynamo Moscow forward found the net shortly after his introduction, adding another goal to Russia’s already commanding performance.

Tyukavin offers a different profile from the Russian midfielders. His game is built around movement in and around the final third, with positioning that can force difficult decisions from opposing centre-backs.

Nigeria’s central defenders will need to maintain close communication whenever Russia begin supplying their forwards, particularly when Tyukavin drifts between the defensive lines.

Maksim Petrov

Maksim Petrov produced a performance that combined creativity with finishing quality.

The Baltika midfielder recorded both a goal and an assist against Namibia, supplying Glushenkov for Russia’s fourth goal before converting a penalty for his first international goal.

Petrov’s contribution showed his ability to influence a game in different phases. He can help create openings for teammates before arriving in scoring positions himself.

His movement from midfield could become an important part of Russia’s approach if Karpin’s side controls possession and pushes Nigeria deeper.

Danil Prutsev

Danil Prutsev completes the group after also finding the net against Namibia.

The Spartak Moscow midfielder started the match and scored in the second half, providing another example of the attacking contribution Russia can generate from deeper areas.

Prutsev’s movement gives the Russian attack an extra dimension because he can arrive late around the penalty area while the forwards occupy Nigeria’s defenders.

That could leave the Super Eagles tracking runners from several positions rather than focusing solely on the front line.

Russia’s attacking depth

The five players offer a glimpse into why Russia will approach Tuesday’s encounter with considerable confidence.

Sadulaev and Prutsev provide attacking thrust from midfield; Petrov combines creativity with an eye for goal. At the same time, Glushenkov and Tyukavin have already shown that they can make an immediate impact when introduced from the bench.

Russia’s 6-0 victory over Namibia also showed that their attacking threat does not depend on one individual.

For the Super Eagles, the challenge will be to maintain their defensive structure, limit the spaces between the lines and deal with Russia’s movement from midfield into the final third.

After the disappointment of the 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, Nigeria will be looking for a much stronger showing in Nizhny Novgorod.

The friendly offers another test for the Super Eagles against a Russian team that has already shown just how ruthless it can be in front of goal.

World.title: Military Aircraft Crash: How naval personnel and residents try to rescue victims – Gov Aiyedatiwa
World.content:
The Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, said no survivor had been found after a Nigerian Air Force aircraft crashed in the Igbokoda area of Ilaje Local Government Area of the state.

Mr Aiyedatiwa disclosed this on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, hours after the incident.

The aircraft had 32 people on board, comprising seven crew members and 25 passengers, according to the governor.

He said residents, emergency responders, and security personnel had combed the swampy crash site but had not found anyone alive.

“No survivors yet, from the information I’ve gotten from the people in there. I haven’t been able to speak to the naval captain leading the base, but my security adviser contacted the Amotekun leader in the local government and the local government chairman.

“From all indications, there are no survivors yet that we can record.”

‘There was no fire’

Mr Aiyedatiwa said residents first heard a loud sound before seeing the aircraft nose-dive into a swampy area.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“They heard the sound like an air tremor, the shaking. There was no fire, nothing, but some people saw the aircraft nose-dive into the swamp,” he said.

He said Nigerian Navy personnel initially stayed back from the crash site for fear that the aircraft could explode or catch fire.

“So immediately, the Nigerian Navy men, from the information I got, stayed back a bit so that there wouldn’t be an explosion or fire outbreak.

“So, when they noticed that it was just an area and they didn’t see any sign of fire, they moved in, trying to see if they could rescue the people.

“Then the local emergency management agency from the local government also tried to move in with residents. Then the Amotekun base at Ilaje Local Government also moved in on time to see if they could rescue some of the victims.

“But from the information we got, no single life was saved up to this moment.”

Mr Aiyedatiwa said rescuers found wreckage from the aircraft, including parts of its wings, identity cards and military uniforms.

“They could not see any living soul that was in that aircraft, but they saw the ruins, some of the wreckage from the wings of the aircraft, with some ID cards that were retrieved, and then some uniforms. That was when they knew it was a military aircraft,” he said.

A video circulating on social media showed a small crowd gathered near a river as rescuers searched the area by boat.

Dayo Akinte, 39, a firewood hawker who lives about one kilometre from the scene, told AFP that she heard a sound she initially thought was thunder.

The governor said the Nigerian Air Force had launched an investigation to determine the cause of the crash.

“It’s a sad situation today, and we’re all really, really aggrieved as Nigerians. And also, it happened in my own state, not just my state, even in my own local government where I’m from,” he said.

“So everybody has been mourning what happened to Nigerian military officers who signed up to protect the territorial integrity of our country and are involved in such accidents. It is so painful.”

In an earlier statement by his Chief Press Secretary, Ebenezer Adeniyan, Mr Aiyedatiwa expressed his “heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft.”

“Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time,” he said.

Tinubu mourns, orders probe

President Bola Tinubu has mourned those involved in the crash and ordered a thorough investigation into the incident.

In a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, Mr Tinubu described the crash as “a painful moment” for the Armed Forces and the country.

“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten,” the president said.

He commended the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate search-and-rescue operation following the crash and prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died.

“I pray for the repose of the souls of the gallant officers and for Almighty God to grant their families and the Nigerian Air Force the fortitude to bear the unfortunate loss.

“I assure the Nigerian Air Force of the continued support of our administration as they continue their vital role in securing our nation. I also commend the swift response of first responders and the Ondo State Government at the crash site,” Mr Tinubu said.

The president also declared a three-day mourning period for the victims of the crash.

World.title: Four African countries call for de-escalation of tension in Ethiopia
World.content:
Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia and Sudan have called for a de-escalation of the conflicts across their region, including Sudan’s civil war and the crisis in Ethiopia.

In a joint statement issued Sunday at the end of a meeting in New Alamein City, Egypt, the countries called for dialogue and a peaceful resolution of the conflicts.

The statement was signed by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki, Somali President Hassan Mohamud and Sudanese army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, according to Al Jazeera.

The countries declared that cross-border challenges required “a dialogue, not confrontation.”

They also demanded that the coastal states retain control of the Red Sea; a stance that appears to respond to Ethiopia’s pursuit of sovereign access to the sea and a naval presence.

This call comes amid the growing tension between Ethiopia’s federal government and authorities in the northern Tigray region; a situation that has many in the country fearing that it could tip back into the kind of war that devastated it a few years ago.

PREMIUM TIMES reported renewed armed clashes in the northern Tigray region between the Ethiopian government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) two weeks ago.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The rebel forces also seized control of Mekelle and the Alula Aba Nega Airport.

Government and allied forces, however, retook the city of Mekelle on Sunday after the TPLF said it “temporarily moved out of” Tigray’s regional capital to “operate from somewhere else.”

According to local media, Tigray interim leader Abraham Belay accused the government of preparing a new temporary administration for the region and said it hopes to hold regional elections within months.

Meanwhile, Ethiopia has accused neighbouring Eritrea of directly backing the rebel alliance during Ethiopia’s 2022 civil war. It also accused Egypt and Sudan of backing the armed alliance in the recent confrontation.

Sudan, which has been at war since April 2023, has accused Ethiopia of interfering in its crisis.

World.title: Israel puts military on alert for Oct 7 anniversary, warns Gazans
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks during the state memorial ceremony for the third anniversary of October 7 attack, at Mount Herzl military cemetery in Jerusalem on October 5, 2026. Netanyahu on October 5 vowed there would be no Hamas rule in Gaza as he attended a memorial event marking three years since the militant group’s October 7, 2023 attack. (Photo by DEBBIE HILL / POOL / AFP)

Israel’s defence minister on Tuesday said he had put the military on high alert before the anniversary of Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, warning Gazans would pay a “heavy price” if forces were harmed.

The office of Defence Minister Israel Katz said the instruction came “in light of intelligence regarding Hamas’s intentions to attempt to carry out attacks and terror operations against our forces in Gaza on that day”.

“If, heaven forbid, our forces are harmed, the ones who will pay the heavy price will be Hamas and the population of Gaza — beyond all proportion,” the statement added.

Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack was the deadliest day in Israel’s history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.

In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

Since a ceasefire was declared last October, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people in Gaza, according to the ministry.

On Monday, during a state ceremony to mark three years since the attack, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said there would be “no Hamas rule in Gaza” and vowed to continue targeting anyone who was involved in the attack or who held hostages.

World.title: Ondo crash: Nigeria owes an enduring debt of gratitude to officers – Shettima
World.content:
VP Shettima

Vice President Kashim Shettima has said Nigeria owes an enduring debt of gratitude to officers who died in Monday’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Ondo State.

In a condolence message to the families of the deceased, officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force on Tuesday, Shettima assured that the Federal Government would continue to stand by them beyond the period of national mourning.

The vice president described the tragedy as a painful national loss.

Shettima noted that a nation that asks its citizens to serve must also remember those who pay the ultimate price in that service.

“32 of our compatriots left on a routine mission in the service of their country. They were colleagues, friends and comrades.

“But beyond the uniforms they wore and the ranks they held, they were husbands and wives, fathers and mothers, sons and daughters, brothers and sisters.

“Somewhere today, there is an empty chair. Somewhere, a family is still trying to comprehend the sudden silence left by someone who was expected to return home.

“These are the human faces of the supreme sacrifice we speak about as a nation,” he said.

Shettima, who reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s message following the tragedy, noted that the president had declared three days of national mourning.

He also said that the President directed that flags be flown at half-mast in honour of the deceased.

According to Shettima, the ultimate sacrifice made by the deceased imposes an enduring obligation on the nation to remember both their service and the loved ones they left behind.

“We cannot ask the bereaved to be strong today. Grief does not obey instructions.

“We can only assure them that Nigeria remembers, Nigeria mourns with them, and Nigeria will stand beside them beyond these days of mourning,” Shettima said.

He also extended his solidarity to officers, airmen and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.

Shettima noted that the tragedy had taken from the service members of a professional family bound together by duty and sacrifice.

“To the men and women of the Nigerian Air Force, we know that this loss is yours in a particularly personal way.

“Your fallen colleagues have paid the supreme price. A grateful nation honours their courage, their service and the families who shared them with Nigeria,” he stated.

The vice president prayed for the repose of the souls of the deceased and for comfort and strength for their families, colleagues and loved ones. (NAN)

World.title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
World.content:
This aerial view shows a giant shirt marking Lionel Messi’s farewell from the Argentina national football team displayed at the National Flag Memorial in Rosario, Argentina, on the eve of the international friendly football match between Argentina and Benin. (Photo by Marcelo MANERA / AFP)





Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina’s sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.

Some 85,000 Argentina fans will be on hand to watch the 39-year-old idol perform his wizardry in a friendly against Benin that brings down the curtain on his 21-year international career.

Millions more will be following the action in South America’s largest stadium, Buenos Aires’ Estadio Monumental, on TV.

The most-capped player in Argentine history is hanging up his boots two-and-a-half months after losing the World Cup final to Spain.

“I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

On Monday, he took part in his last training session with the team at the complex that bears his name in the Buenos Aires suburb of Ezeiza.

“You can’t ask for more, that’s it,” Nahuel Nieva, a retail worker who took the day off work to watch his hero train, told AFP.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

– Filling the void –

No effort has been spared for the sendoff of a player considered one of the game’s greatest ever.

Several of the teammates with whom he reached football’s pinnacle in Qatar, and who will lead the post-Messi team, will play in the game, including defender Cristian “Cuti” Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.

After the game the captain’s armband will pass to Romero.

Coach Lionel Scaloni has vowed to try fill the “void” left by his talismanic captain and the signs from the next generation, some of whom weren’t even alive when Messi debuted with the team in 2005, are auspicious.

In their first games since the World Cup final last week, minus Messi, Argentina thrashed Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba on Wednesday before running rings around Burkina Faso on Saturday at Monumental stadium.

Franco Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni, two of Argentina’s brightest new hopes, both scored their first international goals against Burkina Faso in a 7-0 romp.

The results helped lift the gloom of the defeat in the World Cup final when Argentina and a visibly tired Messi were outplayed by Spain and resorted to thuggish tactics which have been punished with bans and fines for a number of players.

– Coveted number 10 jersey –

Messi is not only Argentina’s record appearance-maker but also its leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.

“La Pulga” (The Flea) won the eternal gratitude of Argentines — and sealed his place as rightful heir to Diego Maradona — in 2022 when he ended their 36-year World Cup drought in Qatar.

During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina were also crowned 2005 World Youth Champions, 2008 under-23 Olympic champions and they won the Copa America in 2021 and 2024. They also won the 2022 Finalissima, a match between the champions of South America and Europe.

But there were tears along the way too, notably after Argentina’s defeat by Germany in the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil, their loss to Spain in this year’s final and their shock humiliation by Chile in the 2016 Copa America final.

One detail remains unclear, however: who will inherit Messi’s coveted number 10 jersey?

“Until Leo’s game, we won’t give the number 10 to anyone,” said Scaloni. “After that, we’ll see.”

World.title: 2027: ADC dismisses The Economist’s report on Tinubu as ‘poor journalism’
World.content:
ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) spokesperson, Bolaji Abdullahi, has described a recent report by The Economist on President Bola Tinubu’s chances in the 2027 presidential election as “poor journalism”.

The Economist had reported that Tinubu could retain the presidency in 2027 despite public discontent over insecurity and economic hardship.

Reacting to the report in an interview with Trust TV, Abdullahi criticised what he described as elevating a news story to the level of an electoral projection.

“I’m embarrassed the way we are elevating a mere story to the level of an electoral projection, and if this were a logic class, then we would be guilty of what is called argumentum ad veracundiam,” he said.

He explained the phrase as an appeal to authority, arguing that the fact that a report was published by The Economist did not automatically make its conclusion credible.

“I read that story, and I think even as a piece of journalism it’s poor journalism. The fact that it’s published by The Economist does not excuse the fact that it is poor journalism,” Abdullahi said.

According to the ADC spokesperson, the report was based on limited interviews conducted in Borno, which he said could not reasonably be used to draw conclusions about the entire country.

“How do I mean? When you sit in one place in Borno, and probably Borno town, just the town, then you spoke to a couple of people and used that to extrapolate for the entire country, that’s not journalism,” he said.

Abdullahi, a former newspaper editor, said he would have rejected such a report if it had been submitted to him during his time at ThisDay newspaper.

“That’s not the way we do this work. And like I said on a different TV platform yesterday, if a reporter brought that to me as an editor, when I was at ThisDay newspaper, I would throw it back at him and say it’s lazy reporting,” he said.

When asked whether his criticism meant The Economist was a lazy platform, Abdullahi distinguished between the publication and the particular report.

“I’m saying that that story is poor journalism, and it cannot be excused just because it was published by The Economist,” he said.

The ADC spokesperson’s comments come amid growing political activities ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with parties and political actors increasingly scrutinising reports and projections on the contest.

World.title: 2027: NGE ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​​‍​⁠⁠⁠‍‌​tasks INEC on transparency, timely disclosure of information
World.content:
Anaba

The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to ensure transparency and timely disclosure of information to safeguard the integrity of the 2027 general elections.

NGE President Eze Anaba made the call on Monday in Abuja, during a strategic workshop organised by INEC in collaboration with the NGE.

The theme of the three-day workshop is “Strengthening Democracy Through Partnership Among Editors, Civil Society and Electoral Institutions”.

While acknowledging that the media cannot shoulder the trust-building responsibility on its own, Anaba added the vital role that timely and accessible information from the electoral body plays in a symbiotic relationship between both sides.

Anaba urged media managers and the electoral umpire to forge a deeper partnership based on mutual respect and open communication to effectively combat misinformation.

“Elections are not merely about casting ballots. They are about trust.

“They are about citizens believing that their votes will count, that the process will be transparent and that the institutions responsible for conducting elections will act fairly and professionally,’’ he said.

He pledged editors’ commitment to working with INEC and other stakeholders to promote elections that Nigerians could trust and a media that citizens could rely upon for credible information.

“In an environment increasingly polluted by misinformation, disinformation, manipulated content, deepfakes and partisan narratives, the relationship between INEC and the media must therefore be one founded on openness, mutual respect and regular engagement,’’ Anaba said.

Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), Dr Akin Akingbulu, called for mutual transparency between institutions and the media.

He said, “Newsrooms cannot verify what institutions do not disclose.”

Akingbulu advocated for an “INEC–Editors Verification Compact” to define clear obligations for both information sharing and responsible reporting, cautioning against the rising threat of AI-generated electoral falsehoods.

”Ballot papers may decide an election’s winner, but the quality of information surrounding the process shapes whether citizens trust the outcome.”

Arogundade called on the media to prioritise verification over speed, while emphasising the need for robust measures to ensure the safety of field journalists during election coverage.

The INEC Director of Publicity and Voter Education, Mrs Victoria Eta-Messi, warned against the widespread threat of fake news on electoral process.

She described fake news as “a cancer” with its attendant effect on citizen participation in the electoral system.

Eta-Messi said that distorted reports directly contribute to voter apathy and charged editors to leverage their gatekeeping positions to verify field claims before publication.

Team Leader of DAI, Rudolf Elbling, commended both INEC and the NGE for initiating the platform, stating that strong media-institution synergy remains indispensable for preserving democratic stability in Nigeria.

Elbling, describing media as the oxygen of democracy, emphasised the need for timely and accurate information.

“Media is the oxygen of democracy, but today, there’s a lot of poisonous oxygen out there as well, which is hard to breathe, especially for these guys here.

“It really becomes a horrible mess out there. But you, as respectable media, still stick to the facts that are more important than ever,’’ he said.

Speaking on the operational objectives of the workshop, the Chief Press Secretary to the INEC Chairman, Adedayo Oketola, said that the session was designed to establish direct, round-the-clock verification channels between newsrooms and the commission.

This, according to Oketola, was to prevent unverified claims from undermining public peace.

“Beyond reporting the news, the media, civil society, and electoral institutions share a joint obligation to protect the integrity of the ballot.

“Our goal today is to align on ethical gatekeeping, conflict-sensitive reporting, and civic enlightenment—especially as the nationwide collection of Permanent Voters’ Cards (PVCs) commences in four days, on Oct. 9,” he said.

Mohammed Haruna, INEC National Commissioner, commended media support for the commission, which, according to him, made its achievements possible.

Haruna, who is also the Chairman of the Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), called for greater collaboration between the media and INEC.

He said that upcoming milestones, including the countdown to the general election, required even stronger collaboration with media executives to keep the public accurately informed.

(NAN)

World.title: Trump approves firing squad for convicted US military base shooter
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump. Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP.

President Donald Trump has approved the execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, a US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people at a military base in 2009, the Pentagon said on Monday.

Hasan’s execution for the attack at Fort Hood in Texas — which also wounded more than two dozen people — will be the first carried out by the US military since 1961.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth “has recommended — and President Donald J. Trump has approved — death by U.S. Army firing squad for convicted terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan,” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a post on X.

“The Secretary of the Army will set the time and place of the execution. Judgement day for Hasan has finally come,” Parnell wrote.

Hasan was sentenced to death by a military jury in 2013 for carrying out the Al-Qaeda inspired mass shooting at Fort Hood.

He chose to conduct his own defense during the trial but called no witnesses and gave no testimony, and made no attempt to deny the charges. Court-appointed defense attorneys expressed concern that he was seeking execution.

– Base shootings rare –

Hasan, US-born Muslim of Palestinian descent, opened fire on November 5, 2009, at a medical facility in the sprawling Fort Hood base, which served as a staging point for soldiers to deploy to combat zones in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Twelve of the dead and 30 of the wounded were soldiers. Hasan was shot and partially paralyzed by a civilian police officer who responded to the attack.

The court that convicted Hasan was told that he was opposed to the US military’s occupations of Iraq and Afghanistan, and that he had spoken online with an alleged Al-Qaeda figure, radical cleric Anwar al-Awlaki, an American citizen subsequently killed in a US drone strike in Yemen.

While mass shootings in the United States are common, they are rare at military facilities.

In 2025, a soldier opened fire at a US military base in the state of Georgia, wounding five fellow troops before he was tackled and apprehended.

In 2019, a US sailor fatally shot two people and wounded a third at a base in Hawaii, while a Saudi military student shot dead three people at a military facility in Florida the same year.

A Kuwaiti-born US citizen attacked two military installations in Tennessee in 2015, killing four Marines and a sailor. The FBI concluded the violence was inspired by a “foreign terrorist group.”

Two years earlier, a man killed 12 people and wounded eight at the Washington Navy Yard in the US capital, before being shot dead by officers.

World.title: NEMA activates search team for crashed air force aircraft in Ondo
World.content:
… deploys search and rescue director, technical team to Igbokoda

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has activated a specialised search-and-rescue team to intensify operations following the crash of a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft near Igbokoda in Ondo State.

NEMA Director General, Mrs Zubaida Umar, directed the Director of Search and Rescue, Air Commodore Bature Usman, to lead a technical team to the crash location as part of efforts to reinforce ongoing search and recovery operations.

The deployment comes as NEMA personnel already at the scene continue to work with other emergency responders involved in the operation.

Umar stated that the agency intervened to enhance coordination and offer extra technical and operational support to the teams responding to the incident.

She commended the prompt activation of search-and-rescue operations following the crash and reaffirmed NEMA’s readiness to deploy the necessary resources to support the ongoing response.

The NEMA chief also expressed deep sadness over the incident, describing it as a painful loss to the nation and acknowledging the sacrifices made by Nigerian Air Force personnel in the service and defence of the country.

She extended condolences to the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Nigerian Air Force family and families affected by the crash.

Umar prayed for the repose of the souls of those who lost their lives, comfort for their families and speedy recovery for anyone injured in the incident.

World.title: Peter Obi wants to destroy APGA that made him – Opara
World.content:
Peter Obi

By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has warned its members against supporting former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, accusing him of working to undermine the party he once belonged to.

The party, in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Mazi Ejimofor Opara, titled “A Betrayal Alert for Ndi APGA,” alleged that Obi had consistently worked against APGA in successive electoral cycles.

APGA questioned why Obi, if he remained committed to the party, had allegedly backed candidates against its candidates in various elections.

The party asked: “If Mr. Peter Obi so loved APGA, why has he fought so hard against APGA in every electoral cycle?”

It also queried why, “for every seat APGA is contesting,” Obi allegedly had candidates positioned to challenge the party.

According to APGA, “APGA made Peter Obi, yet Peter Obi wants to destroy APGA.”

The party declared that a vote for Obi and the National Democratic Congress (NDC), which it described as a Special Purpose Vehicle, amounted to a vote against APGA.

“A vote for Peter Obi and the NDC is a vote to kill APGA,” the statement said.

APGA further alleged that Obi had pursued a mission to destroy the party since 2014, accusing him of backing opposition forces against APGA in the 2017 and 2021 electoral cycles.

“Since 2014, Mr. Peter Obi has had one mission — to destroy the Party that made him,” the party alleged.

It also claimed that while President Bola Ahmed Tinubu supported APGA in 2025, Obi backed opposition forces against the party.

The party dismissed reports or suggestions of an agreement with the NDC, insisting that there was no formal or informal arrangement between both groups for power-sharing.

“There is no formal or informal consultation or agreement between APGA and NDC for power-sharing,” APGA stated, adding that the NDC was “merely a Special Purpose Vehicle,” while APGA remained “a Political Party of Record.”

The party also defended its support for President Tinubu, saying the decision was based not only on APGA’s convention of collaborating with the party at the centre, but also on what it described as the President’s commitment to infrastructure development in the Southeast.

“APGA’s support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is not only predicated on the unwritten convention that the Party collaborates with the Party at the center,” it said.

It added that the support was “more fundamentally anchored on the fact that President Tinubu has demonstrated utmost good faith in the infrastructural development of the Southeast, more than any other government since Nigeria’s return to democracy in 1999.”

APGA urged its members to reject what it described as attempts to deceive them, accusing Obi of abandoning the party when it needed him and treating political parties as “mere Special Purpose Vehicles to be used and dumped at will.”

The party concluded by reaffirming its control of Anambra State, saying: “Anambra is APGA. It remains in our informed best interest to defend our fortress.”

World.title: Rite Foods Targets Zero Waste to Landfill by 2030
World.content:
Fadekemi Ajakaiye

Rite Foods Limited has pledged to achieve zero waste to landfill by 2030 as part of efforts to promote a circular economy and strengthen environmental sustainability in Ogun State.

The company also called for stronger collaboration between the private sector and government in tackling the growing challenge of waste management, saying materials that would ordinarily end up in drains and landfills could be repurposed into useful products.

Speaking during the company’s World Cleanup Day initiative in Ogun State, the Head, Corporate Affairs and Sustainability, Rite Foods Limited, Ekuma Eze, said the company was committed to ensuring that environmental sustainability remained central to its operations.

Eze said the initiative, carried out in partnership with the Ogun State Waste Management Authority (OGWAMA), was designed to recognise the efforts of street sweepers while promoting the concept of waste recovery and recycling.

According to him, Rite Foods distributed 600 coveralls to street sweepers, with about 30 per cent of the materials used in producing the protective clothing sourced from the company’s waste materials.

He said the initiative demonstrated that waste could be transformed into useful resources instead of being discarded.

“We want to drive the message of circularity home. Nothing should be wasted,” Eze said.

He explained that the company recycled waste labels from its sausage and beverage products for use in producing the materials for the coveralls.

Eze said the initiative was also part of the company’s broader commitment to its host community, noting that Rite Foods, being based in Ogun State, had a responsibility to support efforts aimed at maintaining a clean environment.

He said the partnership with OGWAMA was not a one-off activity but would continue for as long as the company remained in operation.

The Rite Foods executive added that World Cleanup Day had become an annual platform through which the company identifies initiatives that align with the United Nations’ theme for the event.

He recalled that the company had previously distributed school bags made from recycled waste materials to pupils.

“We believe that by 2030, we should have achieved zero waste to landfill. None of the waste we generate from our operations should end up in landfills. All of it should be useful, repurposed, reused or recycled,” he said.

Responding, the Special Adviser on Environment to the Ogun State Governor and Managing Director, Ogun State Waste Management Authority, Farouk Akintunde Adeniyi, commended Rite Foods for supporting the state’s waste management efforts.

Adeniyi said the government could not shoulder the responsibility of maintaining a clean and healthy environment alone, stressing that businesses, communities and individuals must play active roles.

He described the Rite Foods initiative as a demonstration of corporate social responsibility and urged other companies operating in Ogun State to emulate the gesture.

“This is a challenge to other corporate organisations across Ogun State to support the government. The effort to ensure a conducive environment is not the responsibility of government alone. It is a collective responsibility involving the government, organisations and all citizens of Ogun State,” he said.

Adeniyi also urged residents to comply with environmental laws and stop indiscriminate disposal of waste.

He disclosed that OGWAMA had introduced the Blue Box Initiative to increase the collection and recycling of recyclable materials across communities.

Under the initiative, officials and aggregators visit communities to educate residents about recyclable waste and purchase the materials from them, thereby turning waste into a source of income.

According to him, the initiative is helping the state move away from the traditional practice of sending waste to landfills towards recycling and resource recovery.

Adeniyi further stated that Ogun State currently hosts the highest number of recycling companies in Nigeria, describing this as evidence of the state’s growing emphasis on the circular economy.

He said the state government would continue to encourage initiatives that create economic value from waste while improving environmental sanitation.

The partnership between Rite Foods and OGWAMA, he added, demonstrated how private-sector investment and government regulation could complement each other in addressing Nigeria’s environmental challenges.
