World.title: Camps Bay tragedy: 8 Year-old drowns on last day of school holiday
World.content:
An 8-year-old boy has drowned at the Camps Bay tidal pool. Image via CoCT

An 8-year-old boy has tragically drowned on Camps Bay beach in Cape Town on Monday, 5 October, the last day of school holidays.

The tragedy comes as the search continues for the bodies of three other teens – one in Cape Vidal, another at Mtunzini Main Beach and a third at Glen Beach in Cape Town – who were all swept out to sea during strong rip currents.

YOUNG BOY DROWNS ON CAMPS BAY BEACH

National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) confirmed that an 8-year-old boy had drowned while swimming in the Camps Bay tidal pool on Monday, 5 October – the last day of the third term school holidays.



The CoCT (City of Cape Town) water rescue network was alerted, with authorities on the scene including NSRI Bakoven crew and medics, Clifton Surf Lifesaving lifeguards, CoCT lifeguards, various ambulance and law enforcement personnel, and Camps Bay CID (City Improvement District).

Despite extensive advanced life support CPR efforts to resuscitate the child, he was declared deceased by paramedics.

NSRI stated that the child, believed to be a foreign national living in Cape Town, had visited the Camps Bay tidal pool with family.

Police have opened an inquest.

SEARCH CONTINUES FOR MISSING TEENS

Meanwhile, the NSRI has continued its search for three teenage boys, who have all been presumed drowned during various incidents over the past few days.

Last Thursday, 19-year-old Jonathan Bradfield was swept out to sea at Mtunzini Main Beach whilst swimming in the surf zone.



The Eastern Cape matric learner had been visiting KwaZulu-Natal with his girlfriend and her family.

Another learner, a 16-year-old from Mtubatuba, went missing whilst swimming at Cape Vidal Beach on Saturday. The teen and a 14-year-old pal, who was later rescued, were also caught in rip currents.

A third teen, an 18-year-old from Mfuleni, is also presumed to have drowned after he disappeared in the surf at Glen Beach in Camps Bay over the weekend.

World.title: Johannesburg murder accused is number 85 on a waiting list. Here’s why
World.content:
The Johannesburg murder accused is due back in the Booysens Magistrate's Court on 29 October. Image: Pexels

The Johannesburg man accused of killing his mother in Bassonia is back in the headlines.

This time, it’s not only about the murder charge.

At his latest court appearance, two new charges were added from a separate case.



And before his case can move forward, he’s waiting in a very long queue.

He’s number 85.

James Gibson, 29, is accused of murdering his mother, Celeste Antiga, 57.

Here’s why he’s waiting. Gibson is expected to undergo a psychiatric evaluation linked to the new charges.

He’s reportedly number 85 on the list of people waiting for a bed to be allocated for the assessment.

Until that happens, and the outstanding reports are in, his case can’t move forward.



NEW CHARGES ADDED IN THE BASSONIA MURDER CASE

Gibson appeared before Magistrate Shumani Oriel Vele at the Booysens Magistrate’s Court in Johannesburg South.

Two more charges were added: assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm, and contravening a domestic violence order.

According to the Southern Courier, the new charges stem from a district court case in which Gibson had previously appeared.

Both matters were postponed to 29 October.

They’re expected to be consolidated on that date, meaning they’ll be dealt with together.

Meanwhile, the murder investigation continues.

Police are still waiting for the crime-scene photo album and the post-mortem report.

WHAT HAPPENED IN BASSONIA

Bassonia is a quiet residential suburb in Johannesburg South.

According to police, the incident happened at about 19:10 on 14 July at a home in Blouklip Avenue.

Antiga was allegedly found unconscious, lying in a pool of blood, with severe injuries to her upper body.

She was taken to hospital but died the following day, 15 July.

Gibson allegedly fled the scene and was on the run for several days.

Police arrested him on 21 July and detained him at Mondeor Police Station.

He faces a Schedule 6 murder charge, the most serious category under the Criminal Procedure Act 51 of 1977.

To get bail, an accused must prove that “exceptional circumstances exist which in the interests of justice permit his or her release.”

HE HAS TOLD THE COURT HE WANTS TO PLEAD GUILTY

This case has already had an unusual twist. When Gibson appeared on 31 August, he again told the court he wanted to plead guilty to murder.

Magistrate Hasina Habib explained that a set procedure must be followed before a formal guilty plea can be entered.

Habib instructed the State to speed up the process.

That process now has another hurdle.

Until the outstanding reports are finalised, and the new charges are consolidated, the case can’t move forward.

No formal plea had been entered at the time of reporting.

Gibson remains in custody and is presumed innocent until proven guilty. He’s due back in court on 29 October.

World.title: AKA’s mom Lynn Forbes makes heartbreaking admission about Tibz
World.content:
Lynn Forbes has opened up about the emotional toll of the AKA murder trial, including a painful admission about Tebello ‘Tibz’ Motsoane’s death. Image: Facebook/Lynn Forbes

AKA’s mother, Lynn Forbes, has opened up about Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane’s death as seven men stand trial for the murders of the two friends.

Her comments came after she attended the first day of the high-profile murder trial at the Durban High Court on Monday.

Lynn also turned to Instagram following the emotionally charged day, sharing another post about her late son as his murder case finally plays out in court.



But it was her admission about Tibz that laid bare the toll the killings have taken on both families.

LYNN FORBES OPENS UP ABOUT TIBZ

Gunmen shot AKA and Tibz outside the now-defunct Wish restaurant on Durban’s Florida Road on 10 February 2023.

Lynn sat alongside Tibz’s father, Sylvester Motsoane, when the trial opened.

She comforted him in court as proceedings turned to the deaths of their sons.

“I always felt a little bit guilty that Sylvester lost his son, because my son was supposed to be the one,” Lynn said.

Her comments refer to her belief that AKA was the intended target of the shooting.



Seven men now stand accused of plotting and carrying out the murders.

‘IT’S ABSOLUTE TORTURE’

Lynn does not plan to sit through every day of the trial.

She made it clear that listening to evidence about her son’s murder would come at a heavy emotional cost.

“I don’t want to be here to sit and listen and torture myself, ’cos it’s absolute torture,” she said in an interview.

Instead, she plans to follow proceedings without putting herself through every detail presented in court.

Lynn also thanked investigators and prosecutors for getting the case to trial more than three years after the murders.

She pushed back against criticism over how long authorities took to bring the matter before court, saying investigators needed time to build their case.

For her, a verdict will not change the reality her family faces.

“My son’s gone,” she said.

KAIRO KNOWS TRIAL IS UNDERWAY

AKA’s daughter, Kairo, also knows that the men accused of killing her father are standing trial.

However, the family has tried to shield her from the details.

“Kairo knows I am at court today, but we try not to speak too much about it to her because it is upsetting,” Lynn said.

The family has kept the focus on protecting her while the case moves through court.

SEVEN MEN FIGHT MURDER CHARGES

All seven accused pleaded not guilty when the trial opened on Monday.

They face 11 charges, including conspiracy to commit murder, two counts of murder, five counts of attempted murder and firearm-related offences.

The State alleges the men formed part of a plot to kill AKA.

The trial is expected to continue into November.

World.title: Stats: Nkota must beat Moremi to replace him in Pirates starting line-up
World.content:
Orlando Pirates supporters are itching for Nkota’s return to the green grass. The 21-year-old from Kimberley made his sensational return with a loan deal from Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ettifaq until the end of the season.

As a left-footed right winger, Nkota has to dislodge the Bafana Bafana international, Moremi, who is one of coach Abdeslam Ouaddou’s most-trusted soldiers.

WHAT TSHEPANG MOREMI OFFERS ORLANDO PIRATES

Since moving from AmaZulu FC before the start of the 2025/26 season, Moremi became an instant regular. His debut season resulted in 28 appearances with five goals and four assists.



Despite missing the past month’s action due to injury, Moremi has started the current season with three goals in seven games.

These are some of the levels Nkota has to aim for to break into the Orlando Pirates side. The 26-year-old Moremi has delivered more than goals and assists. The Sharpeville-born winger has averaged 33.95 passes per 90 minutes with an impressive 82.83% pass-completion rate.

BIGGEST DEMANDS FOR MOHAU NKOTA

Perhaps the biggest challenge for Nkota will be his output without the ball. This is one of the cornerstones of coach Ouaddou’s game model.

Despite his attacking flair, Moremi delivers on Orlando Pirates’ pressing style. He has made 22 tackles and eight interceptions in his seven games this term. That could be just as important for Nkota as his attacking numbers.

The 21-year-old will not only have to provide goals and assists but also demonstrate that he can contribute to the team’s pressing and defensive responsibilities.

For Nkota, the opportunity is now clear. Moremi has set the benchmark with five goals and four assists in his debut PSL season, followed by another three goals in the current campaign, while also contributing 33.95 passes per 90, an 82.83% completion rate, 22 tackles and eight interceptions.



If Nkota can match or surpass those numbers while fitting into Ouaddou’s tactical demands, his chances of becoming a regular starter for Orlando Pirates will only increase.

The Buccaneers take on Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final on Saturday 10 October at the Moses Mabhida Stadium at 18:00.
