The Fund and the Contractor Behind the Rebuild

The US$500 million figure is not new. Keyamo spoke of roughly half a billion dollars for Lagos in April, Daily Trust reported.

He announced Tinubu’s approval of the sum at the Invest Lagos 3.0 summit on Monday 8 June 2026, Premium Times reported.

The programme behind it is older still. On Thursday 31 July 2025, the Federal Executive Council, Nigeria’s cabinet, approved N712.26 billion (US$535 million) for the Lagos works.

Keyamo said then that the works would be paid for entirely through the Renewed Hope Infrastructure Development Fund, BusinessDay reported. The government fund covers roads, rail, ports, farming and aviation.

A presidency statement said the fund targets pension funds, concessionary loans, insurers and diaspora investors.

The contract went to China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), which built the airport’s newer Terminal Two. The plan is to strip the old International Terminal One to its frame and refit it with new mechanical and electrical systems.

Terminal Two gets a new apron, access roads and bridges. The council set a 22-month schedule for the Lagos works.

More than 2,000 local workers, including welders and plumbers, are on the site every day, Keyamo said on Monday.

Abuja’s Second Runway and Other Airports

Keyamo also said Tinubu had approved CCECC’s return to Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, the capital. The firm is to build the airport’s long-delayed second runway.

Keyamo recalled that lawmakers blocked the runway 15 to 20 years ago, when it was priced at N45 billion (US$33.8 million at today’s rate). At the exchange rates of that era, the sum was worth roughly US$300 million.

It now costs nearly N500 billion (US$376 million), he said, according to Punch and Tribune.

He first announced the runway approval in April. CCECC had agreed to build it in 2022, then raised its price to about N532 billion (US$400 million) in 2024.

The government rejected that figure and the firm left the site, The Guardian Nigeria and Daily Trust reported in April.

The July 2025 cabinet package also covered Kano and Port Harcourt. It approved N46.39 billion (US$34.9 million) for Kano’s runways, taxiways and lighting, and N42.14 billion (US$31.7 million) for similar work at Port Harcourt.

A rail link is planned too. Designs are being finalised to extend the Lagos Red Line through the General Aviation Terminal to the new international terminal, BusinessDay reported.

Why the Subsidy Fight Is Back Before the Election

Tinubu ended the petrol subsidy on 29 May 2023, moments after he was sworn in, Vanguard noted. Critics blame the move for the rising cost of food and transport that households face.

Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, has pledged to bring the subsidy back. Nigeria’s presidential election is set for 16 January 2027, Vanguard reported.

Keyamo called the critics’ complaints “cheap blackmail” and said jobs come from investment and infrastructure. “Jobs don’t fall from heaven,” he told the audience.

What It Means for US Readers

Travellers: roughly two-thirds of Nigeria’s international air passengers use Lagos airport, Premium Times reported. Expect building work around the old terminal while the 22-month programme runs.

Investors: reserves near US$55 billion give the central bank firepower to defend the naira, BusinessDay noted. The naira traded at about 1,331 to the US dollar on 6 October 2026.

Muda Yusuf heads the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise. He puts the cost of restoring a universal petrol subsidy at about N19.16 trillion (US$14.4 billion) a year.

That bill would compete with spending on infrastructure, health and education, he says.

Policy watchers: both headline jobs sit with a Chinese contractor, and earlier terminals ran on Chinese loans, Keyamo said. Many African airports struggle to pay their way, as the head of Airports Council International Africa said in Abuja in September.

What Is Not Known

The government has not published how much of the US$500 million has been spent, or how the fund raised it. How that sum relates to the N712.26 billion (US$535 million) contract is also not spelled out.

The runway price is unclear. BusinessDay and Leadership quoted Keyamo as saying nearly N400 billion (US$301 million).

Punch, Tribune and the News Agency of Nigeria quoted him as saying nearly N500 billion (US$376 million).

No contract value or completion date for the renewed Abuja runway deal has been released. Keyamo did not say which measure of reserves his US$3 billion starting figure refers to.

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is Nigeria spending to rebuild Lagos airport?

Aviation minister Festus Keyamo says President Bola Tinubu raised US$500 million for the rebuild. The cabinet approved N712.26 billion (US$535 million) for the Lagos works in July 2025.

Did Nigeria borrow the money for Lagos airport?

Keyamo says the Lagos airport money was not borrowed and credits savings from ending fuel and currency subsidies. The Renewed Hope Infrastructure Development Fund that pays for it also targets pension funds and concessionary loans.

Who is building the new airport works?

China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC) holds the Lagos terminal contract. Keyamo says Tinubu has also approved its return to build a second runway at Abuja airport.

Why is the fuel subsidy in the news again?

Tinubu scrapped it on 29 May 2023, and opposition candidate Atiku Abubakar now promises to restore it. The presidential election is set for 16 January 2027.

What does the rebuild mean for travellers?

Lagos airport handles roughly two-thirds of Nigeria’s international passengers, so the works sit on the main route into the country. A rail link from the Lagos Red Line to the terminals is also planned.

World.title: Kenya’s Ndegwa Family Cleared to Buy Back 24% of Insurer ICEA Lion
World.content:
KENYA · INSURANCE

Key Facts — The country Kenya, in East Africa, is home to ICEA Lion, a Nairobi-based group selling insurance, pensions and investments in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

— What happened Kenya’s competition regulator has cleared First Chartered Securities, the Ndegwa family’s investment firm, to take sole control of the group.

— The price The family will pay KSh8.5 billion (US$65.5 million) for the remaining 24.1 percent stake, Business Daily reported on Monday 5 October.

— The seller US insurer Prudential Financial holds the stake through a LeapFrog Investments fund and agreed to sell it in January 2026.

— Then and now The same stake was sold for KSh2.4 billion (US$18.5 million at today’s rate) in a deal agreed in 2020.

— Still open No completion date has been published, and neither Prudential nor LeapFrog has disclosed the price.

The family of a former Kenyan central bank governor is set to regain full ownership of ICEA Lion, a Nairobi insurance group. Kenya’s competition regulator has cleared the family’s investment firm, First Chartered Securities, to take sole control.

Business Daily reported on Monday 5 October that the family will pay KSh8.5 billion (about US$65.5 million) for the remaining 24.1 percent. The stake is held by a fund run by LeapFrog Investments, through which US insurer Prudential Financial owns it.

Who Is Buying and Who Is Selling

The buyer is First Chartered Securities, the investment company controlled by the Ndegwa family. It already owns 75.9 percent of ICEA Lion Insurance Holdings, the group’s parent company.

The family is that of the late Philip Ndegwa, who governed the Central Bank of Kenya from 1982 to 1988. Business Daily said the deal will give the family sole ownership again.

The minority stake is held by Eastern Africa Holdings, the vehicle a LeapFrog fund used to buy it. Kenya’s competition regulator cleared that purchase without conditions in January 2021, The Standard reported at the time.

Yesterday’s subject line: “Egypt PM: no new IMF loan; Suez income US$4.4bn” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Prudential Financial, based in Newark, New Jersey, says it owns a 24% equity interest in ICEA Lion. It holds it through a private equity partnership managed by LeapFrog, and agreed in January 2026 to sell.

Prudential Financial is not the same company as Prudential plc. The two insurers have an agreement on how each may use the shared name.

Dollar figures here use about 129.75 Kenyan shillings to the US dollar on 6 October 2026.

What Kenya’s Competition Regulator Approved

The Competition Authority of Kenya published its decision as Gazette Notice No. 15918, dated Friday 21 August 2026. It was printed in the Kenya Gazette in the week to Friday 2 October.

The notice authorises First Chartered Securities Capital Limited to acquire sole control of ICEA Lion Insurance Holdings Limited. Kenyan business sites Khusoko and TechTrendsKE reported it on Monday 5 October.

The notice does not state the price or set any conditions, Khusoko reported.

Prudential’s quarterly report, filed on Wednesday 5 August, said closing was subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The competition clearance followed about two weeks later.

What the Stake Cost in 2020

The Ndegwas brought in the private equity investor six years ago. In July 2020, Business Daily reported a KSh2.4 billion (US$18.5 million at today’s rate) sale of 24.1 percent to LeapFrog.

Business Daily said that deal valued the whole group at KSh10 billion (US$77 million at today’s rate). By our calculation, the reported buyback price implies a value of about KSh35.3 billion (US$272 million) for the whole group.

In shillings, the exit price is about 3.5 times the 2020 price. The return measured in US dollars depends on how far the shilling has moved since then.

What the Insurer Does

ICEA Lion sells life and general insurance, pensions, unit trusts and trustee services. It has head offices in Nairobi, in Kampala in Uganda and in Dar es Salaam in Tanzania.

The group traces its roots to 1895, it says. Its current form dates from a 2012 merger of the Insurance Company of East Africa (ICEA) and Lion of Kenya Insurance.

The company reported assets of KSh194.2 billion (US$1.5 billion) at the end of 2023. With only two shareholders, its shares are not listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange.

What It Means for US Readers

For Prudential Financial (NYSE: PRU), the Kenyan stake is a minor holding. It was not a significant contributor to the company’s International Businesses segment, Prudential says.

Since late 2025, Prudential has reported the stake’s results among its divested and run-off businesses. In April 2026 it also agreed to sell a 49% Indonesian life insurance stake and PGIM India, its Indian fund arm.

Prudential keeps strategic investments in insurers in Ghana and South Africa, including Enterprise Group in Ghana. The Kenyan exit trims, but does not end, its exposure to African insurance.

For investors in African private equity, the deal shows one exit route. The fund is selling back to the local owner, not through a stock market listing.

Ownership is shifting elsewhere in Kenyan finance too. In late August, Kenya’s central bank cleared South Africa’s Nedbank to buy up to 66% of NCBA Group.

What Is Not Known

The sale has not been reported as completed, and no completion date has been published. Neither Prudential nor LeapFrog has disclosed the KSh8.5 billion (US$65.5 million) price reported by Business Daily.

The parties have not said whether Kenya’s Insurance Regulatory Authority must still approve the change of ownership. The same applies to insurance supervisors in Uganda and Tanzania.

The family has not announced any change to the insurer’s management, brand or strategy. Prudential has not said whether it expects to book a gain or a loss on the sale.

More: Kenya news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is ICEA Lion?

It is an insurance and investment group based in Nairobi, Kenya. It sells life and general insurance, pensions and investment funds in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

Who are the Ndegwas?

They are the family of the late Philip Ndegwa, a former governor of Kenya’s central bank. Their firm, First Chartered Securities, already owns 75.9 percent of ICEA Lion.

Why does a US company own part of a Kenyan insurer?

Prudential Financial invested through a private equity fund managed by LeapFrog Investments. That fund bought 24.1 percent of the group in a deal agreed in 2020, and Prudential agreed to sell in January 2026.

Can Americans buy shares in the insurer?

No. The group is privately owned and its shares are not listed on any stock exchange. Once the sale closes, the Ndegwa family’s firm will own all of it.

How big is the deal in US dollars?

The reported price is KSh8.5 billion (US$65.5 million), at roughly 129.75 shillings to the dollar on 6 October 2026. Business Daily reported the price; Prudential and LeapFrog have not disclosed it.

World.title: Zambia Says Lobito Corridor Road Financing Is Secured
World.content:

ZAMBIA · CRITICAL MINERALS

Key Facts — The country Zambia is a landlocked copper producer in southern Africa that wants faster rail and road links to the Atlantic.

— What happened On Monday 5 October, Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said the money for Zambia’s Lobito Corridor road links is secured.

— Who pays He named the African Development Bank, the US Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Zambian government as funders.

— The next step He said the focus is now on speeding up procurement and starting construction.

— The rail plan In August, the African Development Bank approved a US$255 million loan for new Zambian rail and road links.

— The US stake A US government development bank provided US$553 million for the corridor’s Angolan rail leg, whose financing closed in July.

— The catch No amounts or start dates for the roads were reported, and Zambia’s 550 km rail link is still to be built.

Zambia says the money for its road links along the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed copper route to Angola’s coast, is now secured. Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane told a three-country meeting in Lusaka on Monday 5 October that procurement comes next.

He named the African Development Bank (AfDB), the US government’s Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and the Zambian government as funders. Reports of his speech gave no amounts for the road package.

What Musokotwane Told the Lusaka Meeting

Musokotwane spoke at the opening of the Second Lobito Corridor Coordination Meeting at the InterContinental Hotel in Lusaka. The two-day talks bring together Zambia, Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and partners such as the World Bank.

“We’ve sealed financing for Lobito Corridor,” read the News Diggers headline on his remarks. The Lusaka paper reported that the money covers road connectivity and that Zambia is now awaiting procurement.

According to the Lusaka Times, he said the package came through partnerships with the AfDB, the MCC and the Zambian government. The focus now, he said, is on speeding up procurement and starting construction.

Musokotwane also said the railway’s viability depends on higher output of copper, other minerals and farm goods, Zambia Monitor reported. That growth, he added, would need “investment in roads, warehouses and other logistics infrastructure.”

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Paying for Zambia’s Corridor Roads

Reports of his speech gave no figure for the road package. Two of the funders he named have already committed large sums to Zambia’s side of the Lobito Corridor.

On 6 August 2026, the AfDB board approved a US$255 million loan for Zambia from its African Development Fund. It added a US$10 million grant from the Rome Process/Mattei Plan Financing Facility.

The project will build about 550 km of new railway in Zambia, linking the country to Angola and the port of Lobito. It will also upgrade 105 km of the Mwinilunga–Jimbe road in North-Western Province.

The bank calls the loan a first tranche, with later phases that could take the total to US$500 million. On 15 September, a call went out for consultants to supervise paving of a 63 km stretch to the Jimbe border post.

The MCC is an independent US government agency that funds development through grants. In October 2024, Musokotwane signed its US$491 million Zambia compact: US$458 million from the US and US$33 million from Zambia.

That compact first targeted farm-to-market roads and agriculture. In June 2026, an amendment aligned its priority road segments with the corridor in North-Western and Copperbelt provinces, Zambian media reported.

What Angola, Congo and the World Bank Said

Angola’s transport minister, Ricardo Viegas d’Abreu, told the meeting the railway to the Atlantic is fully operational, News Diggers reported. Congo’s planning minister said a development agreement for the Dilolo–Sakania rail segments has been signed.

World Bank Managing Director Anna Bjerde said the International Finance Corporation, its private-sector arm, has found 118 anchor investment opportunities. They lie along the Lobito Corridor and are worth more than US$28 billion, in mining, energy, farming, logistics and forestry.

She warned against a rail-only approach. “If we coordinate only on rail, we will have built a very expensive conveyor belt,” Bjerde said, according to Zambia Monitor.

Bjerde said Zambia and Congo together account for more than 17% of global copper supply and more than 70% of cobalt production. President Hakainde Hichilema, who opened the meeting, said bureaucracy must be cut to get the corridor working, News Diggers reported.

A Finance Minister Kept On for a Second Term

Musokotwane remains in charge of Zambia’s treasury in Hichilema’s second term. The president re-appointed him and swore him in at State House on Monday 14 September 2026, the Lusaka Times reported.

He signed the October 2023 corridor agreement for Zambia, as well as the 2024 MCC compact. At his swearing-in, Hichilema told him: “Let’s drive investments, growth and projects.”

What It Means for US Readers

The United States signed an October 2023 agreement backing the Lobito Corridor, alongside the EU, the AfDB and the three countries. That deal named the Africa Finance Corporation lead developer of the Zambia–Lobito rail line.

A State Department official called it the most significant transport infrastructure the US had helped develop in Africa in a generation. The US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) later provided US$553 million for the 1,300 km Angolan line.

That line runs from Lobito to the Congolese border under a concession held by Lobito Atlantic Railway, a Mota-Engil and Trafigura venture. The Development Bank of Southern Africa added US$200 million, and the financing closed in July 2026.

For investors in copper and cobalt, the corridor is meant to give Zambian and Congolese metal a faster route west. For background, see how Zambia plans to ship its copper west by rail.

Zambian media reported that the realigned MCC grant will also strengthen transport links serving Zambia’s critical minerals sector.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how much the road package is worth or which roads it covers. The share paid by each of the three funders is also undisclosed.

Reports of his speech gave no start date for construction. The AfDB approval notice gives no completion date for the 550 km rail line either.

It is also unclear whether the package is new money. It may instead be road funding already on record, such as the 105 km Mwinilunga–Jimbe road and the MCC’s realigned road segments.

The news does not mean Zambia’s Lobito Corridor rail link is fully financed. The AfDB describes its US$255 million loan as only a first tranche.

More: Zambia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Lobito Corridor?

The Lobito Corridor is a rail and road route from Zambia’s Copperbelt and southern Congo to Angola’s Atlantic port of Lobito. Zambia, Angola and Congo are developing it with Western and multilateral lenders.

What did Zambia announce on 5 October 2026?

Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said the financing for road connectivity along the Lobito Corridor is secured. He said the focus is now on procurement and starting construction.

Who is paying for the roads?

He named the African Development Bank, the US Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Zambian government. Reports of his speech gave no amounts and no breakdown by funder.

How is the United States involved?

The US signed the 2023 agreement behind the corridor’s rail plan. A US development bank later provided US$553 million for the Angolan rail leg. In June 2026, Zambian media reported that a US grant to Zambia had been realigned toward the corridor.

Is Musokotwane still Zambia’s finance minister?

Yes. President Hakainde Hichilema re-appointed him and swore him in on 14 September 2026, at the start of the president’s second term.

World.title: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, Morocco’s New PM
World.content:
MOROCCO · POLITICS

Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri is a lawyer, a former mayor of Marrakech and Morocco’s first woman head of government. King Mohammed VI appointed her on 29 September 2026, six days after her party, the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), won the most seats in parliament.

She matters abroad because Morocco is a US free-trade partner, a 2030 World Cup co-host and a key player in the Western Sahara dispute. As of 6 October 2026 she is still negotiating a majority, and no cabinet has been announced.

Key Facts — What it is El Mansouri, 50, is Morocco’s first woman head of government, a post most media call prime minister. King Mohammed VI appointed her on 29 September 2026.

— Why it matters PAM won 97 of 395 seats on 23 September 2026. She must build a majority that can win a confidence vote.

— The numbers A majority needs 198 seats. One option reported on 5 October 2026 reaches 207 with three allies.

— The catch No cabinet had been named by 6 October 2026. Reports differ on whether PAM has ruled out the National Rally of Independents (RNI), the outgoing government’s lead party.

— Who is who Allies in talks include Nizar Baraka of Istiqlal and Driss Lachgar of the Socialist Union of Popular Forces (USFP). The Justice and Development Party (PJD) says it will stay in opposition.

— What it means for you Foreign policy, the army and religion remain with the King. Housing, jobs and living costs will be shaped by her coalition.

Who Is Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri?

El Mansouri was born on 3 January 1976 in Marrakech. Her father, Abderrahman El Mansouri, headed the Marrakech Bar and also served as ambassador to the United Arab Emirates, according to Hespress.

She studied private law at Mohammed V University in Rabat and business contract law at the University of Montpellier in France. She has been registered with the Marrakech Bar since 2005, specialising in land and property law.

Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri in a video published by Anfas Press on 2 September 2026. (Photo: Anfas Press, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat this means, and what's next › RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. × Economy impact Key players Stability What's next Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

From Marrakech Lawyer to Mayor

El Mansouri joined the Movement of All Democrats in 2007 and helped found PAM in 2008, according to Yabiladi. In June 2009, aged 33, she became mayor of Marrakech. Hespress calls her the first woman to head the city’s municipal council.

A court annulled the vote in one district that year, but an appeals court reversed the ruling, Bladi reported. She served until 2015. She was elected to the House of Representatives in 2011 and re-elected in 2016.

She won back city hall on 17 September 2021 with 79 council votes, Bladi reported.

Housing Minister in the Akhannouch Government

On 7 October 2021 King Mohammed VI appointed her Minister of National Territory Planning, Urban Planning, Housing and City Policy in the cabinet of Aziz Akhannouch of the RNI.

Her flagship measure is direct housing aid, launched in January 2024. It pays about US$10,000 (MAD 100,000) for homes priced up to about US$30,000 (MAD 300,000), and about US$7,000 (MAD 70,000) for homes up to about US$70,000 (MAD 700,000). MAD means Moroccan dirhams, converted here at about 10 per US$, the rate on 6 October 2026.

By June 2026 about 105,000 people had received aid, according to Morocco World News.

Critics cite the September 2023 Al Haouz earthquake. An official said in September 2025 that reconstruction in Al Haouz province was over 91 per cent complete, with lower rates elsewhere, but a victims’ group said in October 2025 that hundreds of families still lacked aid. In July 2025 she denied social media allegations of irregular land sales, saying her late father bought the land privately in 1978, and announced legal action.

How She Leads the Authenticity and Modernity Party

PAM was founded in 2008 and is usually described as centrist and liberal. Carnegie analyst Sarah Yerkes notes that a top royal adviser formed it, that it stays close to the palace, and that it faced corruption allegations before the vote.

El Mansouri chaired its National Council from January 2016 to February 2024. In February 2024 PAM replaced its secretary-general with a three-person collective leadership, with her as coordinator. Mohamed Mehdi Bensaid and Fatima Saadi are the other two members.

On 1 September 2026 PAM presented a programme promising one million net new jobs and a cut in unemployment from 10.8 per cent to 7 per cent by 2031. It costs about US$35 billion (MAD 350 billion) over 2027 to 2031, and Atalayar says the financing remains uncertain.

How Morocco’s System Works

Under Morocco’s 2011 constitution, Article 47 has the King appoint the head of government from the party that comes first in the House of Representatives election. He then appoints ministers on that person’s proposal. The government must win a confidence vote from an absolute majority of the House’s members under Article 88.

The King chairs the Council of Ministers, is supreme head of the armed forces and, as Commander of the Faithful, oversees religion. He accredits ambassadors and can dissolve parliament.

The 2026 Election and the Coalition Maths

Morocco voted on Wednesday 23 September 2026. Final tallies on 25 September matched the provisional results, and turnout was 38.08 per cent.

PAM won 97 of 395 seats, the RNI 66 and Istiqlal 65. The PJD, which led governments until 2021, rose from 13 seats to 54. Our election results story has the first-night figures.

A majority needs 198 seats. The main options are these.

PAM, RNI and Istiqlal, 228 seats: The 2021 trio. The RNI says it is ready, but some PAM members voiced opposition at a party meeting on 3 October 2026. PAM, Istiqlal, USFP and the Party of Progress and Socialism (PPS), 207 seats: Le360 and Hespress report that El Mansouri favours this grouping. Istiqlal, the USFP and the PPS form the “Koutla”, a long-standing alliance. The total clears 198 by nine seats. Other options: PAM and Istiqlal alone reach 162 seats. Adding the Popular Movement and the Constitutional Union gives 208, a narrow majority Assahifa calls fragile.

The timeline as of 6 October 2026:

30 September to 1 October: First round at PAM headquarters. The PJD declines, having voted on 26 September to stay in opposition. 3 October: PAM’s National Council gives her and a negotiating committee a unanimous mandate to lead the talks, and Istiqlal votes to take part. Istiqlal’s leader says PAM has ruled out the RNI, then retracts, and PAM denies a formal decision. 5 to 6 October: Second round with the PPS and USFP. Le360 reports that PAM has set aside the RNI, while Hespress calls its place uncertain. The PPS Central Committee meets on 6 October, and we could not confirm its decision.

Bank Al-Maghrib, Morocco’s central bank, in Rabat. File photo. Photo: Wikimedia Commons contributor, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons

Who Are the Other Parties?

Our guide to the parties and the palace adds background.

PAM, 97 seats: Centrist and close to the palace. Led by a trio under El Mansouri. It stresses women’s rights and decentralisation. RNI, 66 seats: Centre-right, liberal and business-friendly. Led since February 2026 by Mohamed Chouki, after Aziz Akhannouch stepped aside. Istiqlal, 65 seats: Founded in 1944. Centre-right, stressing social justice inside a market economy. Led by Nizar Baraka. PJD, 54 seats: Islamist-rooted, focused on transparency and anti-corruption. Led by Abdelilah Benkirane. It will sit in opposition. Popular Movement, 29 seats: Centrist, with rural roots. Led by Mohamed Ouzzine. It stresses agriculture and does not rule out joining. USFP, 26 seats: Centre-left socialist party backing a welfare state and workers’ rights. Led by Driss Lachgar. PPS, 19 seats: Left-wing successor to the Moroccan Communist Party, stressing social justice and human rights. Led by Nabil Benabdellah. Constitutional Union, 17 seats: Centre-right and free-market, focused on institutional stability. Led by Mohamed Joudar.

Six smaller parties and alliances hold the other 22 seats.

What Prediction Markets Say

A Polymarket market titled “Next Prime Minister of Morocco? (Invested)” showed El Mansouri at 94.8 per cent on 6 October 2026, with about US$33,900 traded. Mohamed Ouzzine was at 2.9 per cent, Mohamed Chaouki at 0.5 and Nizar Baraka at 0.55.

The market settles only when a head of government wins the confidence vote in the House of Representatives. Her appointment on 29 September is therefore not the end point, and the price reflects traders’ bets that her coalition will pass that vote. It is not a forecast by The Rio Times.

What It Means for You

US readers: The two countries have had a free-trade agreement since 1 January 2006. The US Trade Representative put two-way trade in goods and services at about US$9.6 billion in 2025. Washington recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara on 10 December 2020.

Western Sahara: On 31 October 2025 the United Nations (UN) Security Council adopted Resolution 2797 by 11 votes to none, backing talks on the basis of Morocco’s autonomy proposal. The mandate of the UN mission there expires on 31 October 2026. Foreign policy stays with the palace, so the cabinet is not expected to change Rabat’s line, as our guide to Morocco’s geopolitics explains.

Investors, expats and travellers: Morocco co-hosts the 2030 World Cup with Portugal and Spain, confirmed on 11 December 2024. The talks do not by themselves change visa or travel rules, and our guide to Morocco’s role in Africa covers the region.

What Is Not Known

We do not know whether the RNI will be in or out, how the PPS Central Committee decided on 6 October 2026, or where the USFP stands. The cabinet list and its date are unknown.

We found no report on whether she will keep the Marrakech mayoralty or on the outcome of her legal action over the land allegations.

The next milestones are the PPS decision, the cabinet list and the House of Representatives’ confidence vote. They will show how far a first woman head of government can set the agenda where the palace holds key powers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri?

Also spelled Fatima Zahra Mansouri, she is a Moroccan lawyer born in Marrakech on 3 January 1976. She was mayor of Marrakech, housing minister from 2021 and coordinator of the collective leadership of the Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM). King Mohammed VI appointed her head of government on 29 September 2026.

Is El Mansouri already Morocco’s prime minister?

She holds the title of head of government, the post English-language media call prime minister, since her appointment on 29 September 2026. As of 6 October 2026 she is still negotiating a coalition, and no cabinet has been announced.

How many seats does a majority need?

A majority in the House of Representatives needs 198 of 395 seats. PAM won 97, so it needs partners. The government must win a confidence vote from an absolute majority of the House’s members.

Who chooses Morocco’s head of government?

The King does. Article 47 of the 2011 constitution says he appoints the head of government from the party that comes first in the House of Representatives election. He then appoints ministers on the head of government’s proposal.

Which parties could join her coalition?

Istiqlal has voted to take part, and the Socialist Union of Popular Forces and the Party of Progress and Socialism are in talks. The National Rally of Independents says it is ready, but reports differ on whether PAM will accept it. The Justice and Development Party says it will stay in opposition.

Will her appointment change Morocco’s Western Sahara policy?

The cabinet does not set that policy. Foreign policy stays with the King, who accredits ambassadors under Article 55 of the constitution. United Nations Security Council Resolution 2797, adopted on 31 October 2025, tells the parties to negotiate on the basis of Morocco’s autonomy proposal.

What did she do as housing minister?

From 7 October 2021 she led the ministry of national territory planning, urban planning, housing and city policy. Her ministry launched direct housing aid in January 2024, which had reached about 105,000 people by June 2026. A victims’ group says hundreds of families still lack aid after the 2023 Al Haouz earthquake.

World.title: Kingsley Chinda and the Rivers Governor Race
World.content:
NIGERIA · ELECTIONS

Key Facts — What it is Kingsley Chinda is the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for governor of Rivers State. He won the party primary on 21 May 2026 as the only aspirant.

— Why it matters Rivers is an oil-producing Niger Delta state. It received the third-largest federal revenue share among states in the first half of 2026.

— The numbers The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) schedules the vote for 6 February 2027 and has published the particulars of 19 candidates. Polymarket, a prediction market, priced Chinda at 91.5 per cent on 6 October 2026.

— The catch A Federal High Court in Port Harcourt hears a suit on 4 November 2026 that challenges how he left the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

— Who is who Nyesom Wike, minister of the Federal Capital Territory, backs him. Governor Siminalayi Fubara withdrew and now endorses him.

— What it means for you Investors in Port Harcourt should watch the 4 November hearing and the February result.

Kingsley Chinda is a Nigerian lawyer and member of the House of Representatives who is now the ruling party’s candidate for governor of Rivers State. Rivers votes on 6 February 2027, and the prediction market Polymarket priced his win at 91.5 per cent on 6 October 2026.

Rivers is an oil-producing state, and its governor grants land rights and shapes the business climate around Port Harcourt, the state capital. In 2025 the president suspended the elected state government after unrest and pipeline vandalism.

Who Is Kingsley Chinda?

Kingsley Ogundu Chinda was born on 24 March 1966 and hails from Elelenwo Town, in the Obio/Akpor local government area of Rivers State. He studied at the Rivers State University of Science and Technology and the Nigerian Law School in Lagos. He was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1995.

He is a partner in the law firm Onyeagucha, Chinda and Associates.

Until 2026 he belonged to the PDP. On 21 May 2026 he became the APC candidate, with Major Jack, the Rivers Assembly’s majority leader, as his running mate.

The Port Harcourt refinery in Rivers State. File photo.

RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat this means, and what's next › RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. × Economy impact Key players Stability What's next Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

From Port Harcourt to the National Assembly

The National Assembly’s profile lists Chinda as legal adviser to the Obio/Akpor Local Government Council from 2005 to 2007. It then lists him as Rivers State Commissioner for Environment from 2007 to 2010.

He entered the House of Representatives in 2011 for the Obio/Akpor Federal Constituency. He won again in 2019, with 67,661 votes, and in 2023, so he is in his fourth term. ThisDay reports that he has chaired the House Public Accounts Committee.

Minority Leader in the House of Representatives

The Minority Leader speaks for the opposition parties in the House and coordinates their strategy. The PDP caucus chose Chinda on 16 June 2023, after a rival withdrew. Speaker Tajudeen Abbas announced him as Minority Leader of the 10th House on 4 July 2023.

BusinessDay called him an ally of Wike who helped elect Abbas as Speaker. In June 2025 he described President Bola Tinubu’s emergency rule in Rivers as a constitutional step.

His resignation letter is dated 23 April 2026, yet the House read it on 2 June, after he had won the APC primary. The lawyer Chidi Odinkalu, a former head of the National Human Rights Commission, strongly criticised the sequence.

Rivers State and Nigeria’s State System

Nigeria has 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, which holds the capital, Abuja. Each state elects a governor for four years, with a limit of two terms.

Under the Land Use Act, all land in a state is vested in the governor, who holds it in trust and can grant rights of occupancy. State assemblies pass state laws, and a split between governor and assembly paralysed Rivers in 2025.

Rivers is the third-largest oil-producing state, at about 344,000 barrels a day in 2024, according to regulator data BusinessDay reported in March 2025. Oil-producing states also receive a 13 per cent derivation share of oil revenue.

Rivers received ₦295.99 billion (about US$223 million at ₦1,329 per US$) in federal revenue sharing in the first half of 2026, third among states. Of that, ₦117.33 billion (about US$88 million) was derivation money.

Rivers State’s Political Crisis Explained

The crisis began as a fight between two men from the same party. Nyesom Wike governed Rivers from 2015 to 2023 and became federal capital minister on 21 August 2023. His chosen successor, Siminalayi Fubara, won the 18 March 2023 election with 302,614 votes and took office on 29 May 2023.

They fell out within months. The Assembly complex burned on 29 October 2023, and lawmakers loyal to Wike began impeachment moves the next day. Tinubu brokered a peace deal on 18 December 2023, but the rivalry resumed.

On 28 February 2025 the Supreme Court restored the Wike-aligned Assembly Speaker, Martin Amaewhule, and voided Fubara’s council elections. On 18 March 2025 Tinubu declared a state of emergency. He suspended Fubara, his deputy and the Assembly for six months and appointed a retired admiral as administrator.

Tinubu ended the emergency on 17 September 2025. Amaewhule and other lawmakers left the PDP for the APC on 5 December, and Fubara announced the same move on 9 December 2025.

By January 2026 Wike was promoting the Rainbow Coalition, a cross-party alliance behind Tinubu’s re-election. Allies bought APC nomination forms for Fubara, but he withdrew on 20 May 2026, a day before the primary. Wike says that under an earlier settlement Fubara agreed not to talk about a second term.

On 22 July 2026 Fubara backed Chinda. “The time of war is over,” he said.

The 2027 Governorship Race

INEC schedules the governorship and state assembly elections for 6 February 2027, and campaigning runs until 4 February. INEC published the particulars of 19 Rivers governorship candidates on 29 August 2026, and its final list is due on 10 October 2026.

The APC declared Chinda its candidate on 21 May 2026. He polled 268,497 votes as the only aspirant, after Fubara and two other hopefuls withdrew. The party had uploaded his name to INEC’s portal by 27 July.

Two legal questions hang over the ticket. First, the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt will hear a suit by Samuel Amatonjie on 4 November 2026. He argues Chinda’s defection was incomplete under the Constitution when he joined the APC process, because the House read his letter only on 2 June.

Second, a rival faction of the Rivers APC, backed by a Court of Appeal ruling of 29 May 2026, declared the party’s primaries void. The state party spokesman says the ruling does not threaten the executive that ran them.

On 24 September 2026 the Supreme Court restored rules on party membership registers. At least one group asked INEC to disqualify Chinda, but the judgment did not name him. The Rivers APC says he is fully qualified.

NNPC Towers, headquarters of Nigeria’s national oil company, in Abuja. File photo. Photo: Uncle Bash007, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Who Are the Other Players?

Nyesom Wike Federal capital minister since 21 August 2023 and Rivers governor from 2015 to 2023. He remains a PDP member and supports Chinda and Tinubu. Siminalayi Fubara Governor since 29 May 2023, who joined the APC in December 2025. His first term ends in May 2027, and he has stepped aside for Chinda. Rainbow Coalition Wike’s cross-party alliance backing Tinubu’s re-election, active by January 2026. APC governors have warned that it could confuse voters. Bola Tinubu President since 29 May 2023 and leader of the APC. He seeks re-election in 2027 and declared the 2025 emergency in Rivers. All Progressives Congress Ruling party chaired by Nentawe Yilwatda. It backs Tinubu’s economic reforms, including the end of the petrol subsidy. Peoples Democratic Party Ruled Nigeria from 1999 to 2015 and is now split. INEC recognises the faction Wike backs, chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed. Its Rivers candidate is Sam Ejekwu, a former state transport commissioner. African Democratic Congress Opposition party chaired by David Mark. Atiku Abubakar is its presidential candidate, with Rotimi Amaechi, a former Rivers governor, as running mate. Its Rivers candidate is Gabriel Pidomson, a former state government secretary. Nigeria Democratic Congress Opposition party fielding Peter Obi, a former Anambra State governor, for president. Its Rivers candidate is Dumo Lulu-Briggs, an oil businessman.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket is an online platform where users trade contracts on future events. Its market titled Rivers, Nigeria Governor Election Winner priced Chinda at 91.5 per cent on 6 October 2026. About US$18,300 has traded since it opened on 21 August 2026.

That is a small sum, and the price reflects traders’ bets, not polling. The market resolves after the 6 February 2027 vote.

What It Means for You

For oil and gas investors, a Chinda government would be aligned with Abuja and with Wike, which may ease the governor-Assembly clash behind the 2025 emergency. The court cases could still change the field.

The 2025 emergency followed unrest and pipeline vandalism. On 28 September 2026 the Rivers Assembly voted 25 to 0 for a constitutional change to allow state police. At least 24 of 36 state assemblies must approve it.

Foreign residents cannot vote. Election periods in Nigeria can bring road closures, security checks and delays in official approvals. Further developments will appear in our Nigeria coverage.

What Is Not Known

The Federal High Court has set a hearing for 4 November 2026, but we found no ruling date. We found no INEC statement on whether the Supreme Court’s judgment on membership registers affects Chinda.

We found no independent opinion poll of the race and no detailed manifesto from Chinda. It is also unclear how voters will treat the APC and PDP candidates, who both have links to Wike’s coalition.

The next fixed dates are 4 November 2026 for the court and 6 February 2027 for the vote.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Kingsley Chinda?

Kingsley Ogundu Chinda is a Nigerian lawyer born on 24 March 1966. He has represented Obio/Akpor in the House of Representatives since 2011 and is the All Progressives Congress candidate for governor of Rivers State.

When is the Rivers State governorship election?

The Independent National Electoral Commission has scheduled the governorship and state assembly elections for 6 February 2027. Campaigning runs until 4 February 2027.

Which party is Chinda in?

He is the All Progressives Congress candidate. His resignation letter as House Minority Leader is dated 23 April 2026, and the House read his defection from the Peoples Democratic Party on 2 June 2026.

Is Chinda’s candidacy being challenged in court?

Yes. The Federal High Court in Port Harcourt will hear a suit by Samuel Amatonjie on 4 November 2026. It argues that Chinda’s defection was incomplete under the Constitution when he joined the party’s primary process.

How is Chinda linked to Nyesom Wike and Siminalayi Fubara?

Chinda is a political ally of Wike, the federal capital minister and former Rivers governor. Fubara, the current governor, withdrew from the party primary on 20 May 2026 and endorsed Chinda on 22 July 2026.

What do prediction markets say about the race?

On 6 October 2026 the market Polymarket priced Chinda at 91.5 per cent to win, with about US$18,300 traded. This is a small market price and not a poll or a forecast by The Rio Times.

Who else is running for governor of Rivers State?

INEC has published the particulars of 19 candidates. The main rivals are Dumo Lulu-Briggs of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Gabriel Pidomson of the African Democratic Congress and Sam Ejekwu of the Peoples Democratic Party.

World.title: Zambia’s US Health Deal: Specimen Clause Dropped From US$1.5 Billion Pact
World.content:
ZAMBIA · HEALTH

Key Facts — The country Zambia is a landlocked copper producer of about 21 million people that counts Washington as its biggest health donor.

— What happened Health Minister Roma Chilengi said on Sunday 4 October that Zambia is ready to sign its US health deal.

— What changed A clause on sending disease specimens to the United States was dropped; he said no specimen would leave Zambia.

— How big Chilengi says Washington would provide US$1.5 billion over five years, with the yearly amount falling as Zambia raises its own health spending.

— The bigger picture By September, the United States had signed 35 health pacts under its new aid strategy, including with six of Zambia’s neighbours.

— The catch The final text is not public, and an opposition leader wants it published before anyone signs.

— What comes next Chilengi hoped the memorandum would be signed during the week that began on Monday 5 October.

Zambia’s US health deal is ready for signing, Health Minister Roma Chilengi said on Sunday 4 October. A clause that would have sent Zambian disease specimens to the United States has been removed.

Under the five-year memorandum, Washington would provide US$1.5 billion for Zambia’s health system, with the amount falling each year, the minister said. Zambia would raise its own health spending in return, so programmes continue once American money tapers off.

What the Health Minister Said on State Television

Chilengi spoke on the Sunday Interview, a programme on ZNBC, Zambia’s state broadcaster. He said the two governments had settled the disputes that stalled the US health deal earlier this year.

“We are completely aligned,” he said of the memorandum of understanding, or MOU. “We are completely comfortable with the MOU that has been finalised now.”

The biggest change in the US health deal concerns biological specimens, the samples that health workers collect to track disease outbreaks.

“We have completely dropped the specimen-sharing requirements. No specimen would leave this country as a result of that MOU,” he said.

Talks ran long. Zambia suspended the signing earlier this year to allow more diplomatic and technical discussion, the state-owned Zambia Daily Mail reported.

Chilengi led the Zambia National Public Health Institute before he became health minister on Monday 14 September. President Hakainde Hichilema named him among the first four ministers of his new term.

The minister kept his tone warm towards Washington. He called the US government “our biggest supporter to the health sector” and “a very cherished partner”.

What the Specimen-Sharing Clause Required

Health GAP, a US-based HIV advocacy group, published a draft of the memorandum in March. It said both countries “shall negotiate a specimen sharing arrangement” covering physical samples and related data, including genetic sequence data.

The clause applied to germs with “epidemic potential” and set a deadline of five days after detection. Both sides intended the arrangement to last 25 years.

Chilengi pointed to a mismatch. Parts of the original proposal would have run for 25 years, he said, even though the money covered only five.

Zambia also sought clear rules on intellectual property and benefit sharing, plus training links between Zambian and American scientists. The concern was what Zambia would gain if research on its samples produced new medicines or vaccines.

In July, Lloyd Mulenga, the ministry’s director of infectious diseases, spelled out the worry to Managed Healthcare Executive, a US health journal. “If vaccines are developed from the specimens shared from Zambia, will Zambia have access to those?”

How the Minerals Link Was Broken

The leaked draft also tied the health money to a separate “Bilateral Compact”. According to the text, the US secretary of state proposed that compact to Zambia’s president on 17 November 2025.

Under clause 6.2 of the draft, the memorandum would end at once if no compact was agreed by 1 April 2026.

In early May, Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe objected to attempts to link the US health deal to a proposed critical minerals agreement. He said each should be judged on its own merits and raised concerns about citizens’ privacy.

Talks with US officials at the UN General Assembly in New York settled the point, Lusaka Times reported on 29 September. “The linking, the coupling of the critical minerals agreement with the health assistance… has also been set aside,” Haimbe said.

The opposition wants proof, Lusaka Times reported on Tuesday 6 October. Antonio Mwanza, who leads the opposition Democratic Progressive Party, urged the government to “publish the final agreement before signing it”.

A New Model for American Health Aid

The US health deal falls under the America First Global Health Strategy, launched by the Trump administration in September 2025. It replaces much of the old aid system with multi-year agreements signed directly with governments.

Each partner must raise its own health budget, which the State Department calls co-investment. By September 2026, Washington had signed 35 such memoranda, 24 of them in Africa.

Those deals cover US$14 billion in US health aid, a State Department fact sheet says. Partner countries add more than US$10 billion of their own.

In February, the Ministry of Health said Zambia’s yearly health spending would climb under the proposed memorandum. It projected about US$628 million in 2026, rising to more than US$1 billion by 2030.

Six of Zambia’s eight neighbours have signed: Angola, Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania. Not every government agreed.

Ghana’s President John Dramani Mahama has said his cabinet rejected a proposed US$109 million compact, calling the terms “humiliating”. Zimbabwe walked away from its own talks over control of health data, Lusaka Times reported.

What It Means for US Readers

The US health deal is paid for by American taxpayers through the State Department. The leaked draft covered HIV, tuberculosis, malaria, mother-and-child health, vaccination and disease surveillance.

PEPFAR, the US HIV programme begun in 2003, committed nearly US$7 billion to Zambia in its first two decades, the US Embassy says. The same draft credits US investment with helping more than 1.3 million Zambians now on HIV treatment.

On 2 September, Washington marked the arrival of US-funded lenacapavir in Lusaka. The twice-yearly HIV prevention drug is made by Gilead Sciences (Nasdaq: GILD).

For investors, the minerals question matters more, because Zambia is a large copper producer. Washington backs the Lobito Corridor, a transport corridor linking Zambia’s Copperbelt with Angola’s Atlantic port of Lobito.

In May, Haimbe said Zambia would not accept preferential treatment of foreign companies over its critical minerals. “Me being in Beijing does not mean that I’m against Washington, and vice versa,” he said in September.

What Is Not Known

The final text of the US health deal has not been released. Haimbe said in September that the disputed provisions would be “replaced completely”, but the new wording is not public.

The money has also shifted during the talks. President Hakainde Hichilema announced a five-year health package worth US$1.5 billion in November 2025, Lusaka Times reported.

The leaked draft then listed US$1.01 billion from Washington for 2026 to 2030, falling from US$321 million in the first year. In May, Lusaka Times put the proposed memorandum at US$2 billion.

Chilengi now speaks of US$1.5 billion from Washington. A Lusaka Times report on 29 September put the direct US contribution at “more than US$1 billion”, and the yearly split is not public.

It is also unclear how the final text handles intellectual property and access to any vaccines built on Zambian samples. No signing date or venue has been announced.

More: Zambia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Zambia’s US health deal?

Zambia’s US health deal is a five-year memorandum of understanding. Health Minister Roma Chilengi says Washington would provide US$1.5 billion, with the yearly amount falling while Zambia raises its own health spending.

What was the specimen-sharing clause?

A draft said both countries would negotiate sharing samples and genetic data on epidemic-prone germs within five days of detection. It was meant to last 25 years, and Zambia says it has now been removed.

Is the deal linked to Zambia’s copper and other minerals?

An early draft made the health money depend on a separate Bilateral Compact. Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe said in September that the link to a critical minerals agreement had been set aside.

What is the America First Global Health Strategy?

It is the Trump administration’s health-aid policy, launched in September 2025. Washington signs multi-year agreements directly with governments, which must also raise their own health budgets.

When will the US health deal be signed?

Health Minister Roma Chilengi hoped it would be signed during the week that began on Monday 5 October. Neither government has announced a date or venue.

Sources: Lusaka Times, 6 October 2026; Zambia Daily Mail, 6 October 2026; Zambian Observer, 5 October 2026; Solwezi Today, 5 October 2026; Lusaka Times (Haimbe, New York talks), 29 September 2026; Lusaka Times (Haimbe press briefing), 5 May 2026; Lusaka Times (cabinet appointments), 14 September 2026; Lusaka Times (draft amounts, November 2025 pledge), 25 January 2026; Lusaka Times (Ministry of Health statement), 4 February 2026; Health GAP (draft Zambia MOU), 16 March 2026; US Department of State fact sheet, 24 September 2026; US Embassy in Zambia, 2 September 2026; Managed Healthcare Executive, 31 July 2026.

World.title: Egypt and Chevron Sign US$88 Million Lotus Block Exploration Deal
World.content:
EGYPT · ENERGY

Key Facts — The country Egypt, the most populous Arab country, wants to lift its own gas output and cut imports.

— What happened On Monday 5 October, Egypt’s state gas company and Chevron signed a deal to explore the offshore Lotus block.

— How big The deal carries minimum investment of US$88 million, including two exploration wells.

— Where it is The block lies about 200 km off Egypt’s Mediterranean coast, in water 2,000 to 2,800 metres deep.

— Why it matters No deep exploration well has been drilled in the area before, the petroleum ministry says.

— The catch Minimum spending is not a discovery, and no drilling date has been announced.

— The bigger picture Chevron now invests in six offshore exploration areas in Egypt, including Nargis, where it has found gas.

Egypt and US oil major Chevron have signed a deal to explore the Lotus block in the deep Mediterranean Sea. The agreement carries minimum investment of US$88 million, including two exploration wells, Egypt’s petroleum ministry said on Monday 5 October.

The block lies about 200 kilometres offshore, in water 2,000 to 2,800 metres deep. No deep exploration well has been drilled there before, the ministry says.

What Egypt and Chevron Signed

Sayed Selim signed for the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS), the state company that runs Egypt’s gas business. He is its executive managing director.

Chevron’s exploration manager for the Middle East, North Africa and the Mediterranean signed for the US company. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi witnessed the signing, with Chevron’s Egypt country manager, Channa Kurukulasuriya, also present.

Besides the two wells, the deal covers reprocessing of 3D seismic data. These are sound-wave images of the rock layers under the seabed, and reprocessing runs them through newer software for a clearer picture.

We never share your email.

The ministry called the Lotus block agreement an important step toward new exploration frontiers. It said the deal improves the chances of finding new natural gas and crude oil.

A Deal Six Months in the Making

The signing follows two earlier approvals in Cairo. In April, the cabinet approved the draft concession with Chevron Egypt Holdings Ltd, the Cairo news site Youm7 reported.

On 30 June, the House of Representatives passed a bill licensing the minister to sign it, Masrawy reported.

Why Egypt Wants More Exploration

Badawi said a wider exploration map is a main part of the ministry’s plan to raise local oil and gas output. The ministry plans to offer more areas, from the Mediterranean and the Western Desert to Sinai and southern Egypt.

The minister also credited the state’s payment of what it owed its oil and gas partners. Settling those dues, he said, restored confidence and led companies to raise investment and restart exploration.

Those dues were arrears that had built up with foreign oil and gas firms. On 30 September, the ministry said investment had returned to target levels once the arrears were settled.

The same statement said four wells, three new and one repaired, had added 45 million cubic feet of gas a day. The ministry framed this as part of a push to restore growth in local gas output and cut imports.

Chevron’s Growing Footprint in Egyptian Waters

Chevron already invests in six offshore exploration areas in Egypt, the ministry said. They are Nargis, North El Dabaa, Lotus, North West Atoll and North Simian, plus North Cleopatra in the western Mediterranean.

In North Cleopatra, Chevron is a partner of Shell. There, the Shell-operated Velox-1X well recently showed promising signs of crude oil, according to the ministry.

The ministry also pointed to Chevron’s Nargis gas discovery in the Mediterranean. Badawi praised the partnership and said the Lotus block deal shows Chevron is still putting new money into exploration in Egypt.

What It Means for US Readers

For Chevron (NYSE: CVX) shareholders, the sums are small. The Houston-based company has budgeted US$18 billion to US$19 billion in capital spending for 2026.

The US$88 million minimum is less than half of 1% of that. Still, the deal fits Chevron’s plans for the Eastern Mediterranean.

Chevron’s 2026 budget includes about US$7 billion for offshore projects, mainly supporting growth in Guyana, the Gulf of America and the Eastern Mediterranean. The Gulf of America is the US name for the Gulf of Mexico.

For policy watchers, the Lotus block ties a major US company more closely to Egypt’s energy plans. Cairo wants more of its own gas so it can import less, the ministry says.

The deal does not mean new gas soon. Two wells in deep, untested water may find nothing, and even a find would need years of work before any production.

What Is Not Known

The ministry did not give the agreement’s length or any signing bonus. It also did not say when drilling on the Lotus block will start.

The ministry gave no estimate of how much gas or oil the Lotus block might hold. That will stay unknown until the two wells are drilled and tested.

More: Egypt news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Lotus block?

It is an offshore exploration area in Egypt’s Mediterranean Sea, about 200 km from the coast. Water depths there range from 2,000 to 2,800 metres, and no deep exploration well has been drilled there before.

How much will be invested in the Lotus block?

The agreement carries minimum investment of US$88 million. That covers two exploration wells and the reprocessing of 3D seismic data.

Who signed the deal?

Sayed Selim signed for the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company (EGAS), where he is executive managing director. Chevron’s exploration manager for the Middle East, North Africa and the Mediterranean signed for Chevron. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi witnessed the signing on Monday 5 October.

Where else does Chevron explore in Egypt?

The ministry says Chevron invests in six offshore areas: Nargis, North El Dabaa, Lotus, North West Atoll, North Simian and North Cleopatra. In North Cleopatra it is a partner of Shell.

Why is Egypt signing more exploration deals?

The government wants to raise local oil and gas output and reduce imports. The petroleum ministry plans to offer more areas to foreign companies, from the Mediterranean to southern Egypt.

World.title: Algeria Hands Down First Death Sentences Under Its New Drug Law
World.content:
RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

ALGERIA · JUSTICE

Key Facts — The country Algeria, Africa’s largest country by area, is a gas-exporting North African state that keeps the death penalty in law.

— What happened A criminal court in Algiers sentenced nine people to death over 113 kg of cocaine and 225,030 pregabalin pills.

— Why it matters These are the first death sentences under Law 25-03 of July 2025, which added capital punishment for major drug crimes.

— Who was sentenced Three defendants were present at the hearing, while six fugitives were tried and sentenced in absentia.

— The catch Algeria has carried out no execution since September 1993, according to its own report to the United Nations.

— The wider push On Thursday 1 October, the lower house of parliament voted to extend the death penalty to arson and child abduction.

An Algerian court has handed down the country’s first death sentences under a tough 2025 drug law. A criminal court in Algiers condemned nine people over 113 kilograms of cocaine, the state news agency reported on Monday 5 October.

Three of the nine were present at the hearing, and six fugitives were tried in absentia. Algeria has carried out no execution since September 1993, its government told the United Nations in 2017.

What the Algiers Court Decided

The verdicts came from the criminal court attached to the Cour d’Alger, the regional appeals court in the capital. APS, Algeria’s state news agency, said the cases involved 113 kg of cocaine and 225,030 pregabalin pills.

Ennahar, an Arabic-language daily, said the ruling came from the first-instance criminal court in the Algiers suburb of Dar El Beida.

The charges included importing, transporting and storing hard drugs and psychotropic pills for sale within an organised criminal group. They also cited an aim of harming national security and public order.

Smuggling, identity theft, illegal immigration, illegal residence and money laundering were also listed, APS reported.

Other defendants received terms ranging from 20 years in prison to acquittal, Ennahar reported. Two got seven years and a 5 million dinar fine (about US$37,300, at 134 dinars to the dollar on 6 October 2026).

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Algeria Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Cocaine Case Began

The case dates to September 2025. Prosecutors at a specialised court in Algiers said then that police had caught seven members of a 16-strong transnational gang.

The seven were found with about 113.5 kg of cocaine and some 220,000 pregabalin pills, TSA reported. Prosecutors also published the suspects’ photos and names, a step the 2025 law allows.

According to Ennahar, police followed a truck from M’sila, south-east of Algiers, to Ouargla in the Sahara and back north. The drugs were seized on 12 September 2025 at a farm in Ouled Fayet, west of Algiers.

Pregabalin is a prescription medicine for nerve pain and epilepsy. In Algeria it is often diverted and resold to young users, the news site Algérie360 reported.

What Law 25-03 Changed

President Abdelmadjid Tebboune signed Law 25-03 on 1 July 2025, and the Official Journal, Algeria’s legal gazette, published it on 13 July. It amends Algeria’s 2004 law on drug use and trafficking.

As late as 2017, Algeria told the UN that its drug-trafficking law did not provide for the death penalty. Amnesty International says the 2025 law introduced it.

Major trafficking offences now carry the death penalty if they directly cause a death or are likely to seriously harm public health. The same applies to crimes by transnational gangs or aimed at undermining national security.

Acting for a foreign state, using a firearm or using children to deal drugs near schools can also bring death sentences. Crimes involving synthetic hard drugs that carried life imprisonment now carry death.

A foreigner convicted of a drug felony must be permanently banned from Algeria. Job applicants in public and private recruitment competitions must show a negative drug test.

No Execution in Algeria Since 1993

Algeria still passes death sentences but has not carried one out in more than three decades. “No executions have been carried out since September 1993,” the government told the UN Human Rights Committee in 2017.

The same report said people convicted in absentia are entitled to a retrial. In 2018 the committee, a UN expert panel, took note of “the de facto moratorium observed by the State party since 1993”.

Amnesty International recorded no executions in Algeria in 2025 and 11 new death sentences, all for murder. At least 273 people were on death row at the end of 2025.

Amnesty lists Algeria as “abolitionist in practice”. Its May 2026 report also criticised the “over broad phrasing” of the new drug provisions.

On Thursday 1 October, the lower house of parliament voted to add the death penalty for deliberate forest fires and child abduction. The bill now goes to the upper house, the Council of the Nation, TSA reported.

President Tebboune had ordered the arson change after deadly wildfires this summer. A public appeal signed by several dozen citizens has called for the moratorium to stay, Le Matin d’Algérie reported.

Justice Minister Lotfi Boudjemaa said in Oran on 22 September that the death penalty “will be activated” against drug traffickers, APS reported. He said the procedures would follow only once all appeals were exhausted.

What It Means for US Readers

For travellers, the law applies to foreigners as much as to Algerians. Drugs that are legal in some US states, such as cannabis, remain illegal in Algeria.

A drug conviction can bring a permanent ban from the country on top of any sentence. Anyone who commits an offence under the influence of drugs now faces the maximum penalty for it.

Police may order drug tests for suspects thought to have acted under the influence, and refusing is itself punishable.

For policy readers, Algeria is widening capital punishment and its justice minister says it will be applied. Yet no execution has taken place in 33 years.

Background on Algeria’s politics is in the Algeria explainer.

What Is Not Known

APS did not name the nine or give their ages or nationalities. It is not known whether the three defendants who were present will appeal their death sentences.

The six fugitives remain at large. Algérie360 reported that searches continue in Algeria and abroad.

It is not known whether Algeria will carry out an execution once appeals in this case run out. It is also unclear when the upper house will vote on the arson and abduction bill.

More: Algeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Algeria executed anyone recently?

No. Algeria has carried out no execution since September 1993, according to its own 2017 report to the UN. Courts still pass death sentences, and Amnesty International recorded 11 in 2025, all for murder.

What is Algeria’s Law 25-03?

It is a law signed on 1 July 2025 and published on 13 July 2025 that toughened Algeria’s 2004 drug law. It added the death penalty for the gravest trafficking cases, such as those linked to transnational gangs, national security or deaths.

Are the nine death sentences final?

No. The verdict came from a first-instance criminal court, so it can still be appealed. Under Algerian law, the six people tried in absentia are entitled to a retrial if caught.

Does the drug law apply to foreigners?

Yes. A foreigner convicted of a drug felony must be permanently banned from Algeria. That ban comes on top of any prison or death sentence.

What is pregabalin?

Pregabalin is a prescription medicine for nerve pain and epilepsy. In Algeria it is often diverted and sold illegally, and this case involved 225,030 pills.

Sources: APS (Algérie Presse Service), 5 October 2026; TSA, 5 October 2026; Ennahar, 5 October 2026; APS (Justice Minister in Oran), 22 September 2026; Journal Officiel no. 43 (Law 25-03), 13 July 2025; Algeria, fourth periodic report to the UN Human Rights Committee (CCPR/C/DZA/4), 23 February 2017; UN Human Rights Committee, concluding observations on Algeria (CCPR/C/DZA/CO/4), 17 August 2018; Amnesty International, Death Sentences and Executions 2025, May 2026; TSA (September 2025 seizure), 22 September 2025; Algérie Eco (lower-house vote), 1 October 2026; TSA (lower-house vote), 1 October 2026; Algérie360, 5 October 2026; Le Matin d’Algérie, 5 October 2026.
