World.title: Germany's ex-spy chief arrested for espionage
World.content:
August Hanning served as the head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency from 1998 to 2005. According to German media, he is being investigated for allegedly passing on state secrets and working as an agent.

Police have arrested the former head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence agency, August Hanning, on suspicion of espionage, the federal prosecutor's office announced Tuesday.

Hanning served as the agency's chief from December 1998 to November 2005, before moving to the Federal Interior Ministry where he worked as state secretary until November 2009.

According to a statement from the prosecutor's office, he is facing charges including alleged espionage, disclosure of state secrets, attempted treason, and working as a secret service agent.

The statement added that a former high-ranking employee of the BND had also been arrested on suspicion of providing Hanning with hundreds of classified documents in exchange for payment.

DW's chief political editor Michaela Küfner, reporting from a government press briefing on the arrest, described the case as Germany's "biggest espionage scandal of the century unfolding in real time."

What else do we know about the investigation?

Police arrested Hanning early Tuesday at his home in Nordwalde near the western German city of Münster, according to information from WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung.

Hanning's alleged accomplice, who was identified only as Manfred D. in line with Germany's privacy laws, was taken into custody in Bavaria.

Authorities were conducting searches at both suspects' properties, as well as in Berlin, the prosecutor said.

During Hanning's tenure as spy head, D. served as his chief of staff. He also subsequently worked under Hanning at the Interior Ministry until 2009.

He is facing charges of "aiding and abetting attempted treason and espionage against the state."

The prosector's office said the two men are believed to have come up with their arrangement in 2010.

2,000 documents allegedly handed over to Hanning

From 2012 to March 2026, D. served as chief of staff to Hanning's successors at the BND spy agency, where he had access to a wealth of classified documents, according to the prosecutor's statement.

"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D. provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," the statement said.

It added that D. is alleged to have provided Hanning with information until at least mid-2022, and that Hanning used the information in his private consulting work.

Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D., for several years," the statement said.

The prosecutor's office did not say which foreign intelligence service was involved.

The two suspects are expected to appear before an investigating judge on Tuesday and Wednesday.

World.title: Canada: Quebec separatists return to power, promise new independence referendum
World.content:
Parti Quebecois has won the provincial election, but fallen short of a majority. Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says he will seek another referendum on independence, but not while US President Donald Trump is in office.

In Quebec's provincial election on Monday, the separatist Parti Quebecois (PQ) came in the lead after promising another referendum on independence from Canada but fell short of a outright majority.

The PQ, led by 49-year-old Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, was on track to win nearly 60 of the 127 seats in the National Assembly, just short of the 64 needed for a majority.

However, their return to power after more than a decade comes with a caveat as the minority government will need support from opposition parties to pass legislation and survive confidence votes.

"Quebecers elected the Parti Quebecois asking it to work with the other parties, and I heard that message," the PQ leader said.

St-Pierre Plamondon says dreams of independent Quebec

The PQ's return to power also brings to forefront the issue of identity of Quebec's French-speakers, who make up 80% of the population, and comes with a promise of an independence referendum.

St-Pierre Plamondon said he envisioned Quebec as a country on its own and that a referendum would allow Quebecers to decide their own future.

"I continue to dream and visualize that country," St-Pierre Plamondon said in his victory speech. "That dream will be realized one day."

The jubilant leader, however, made it clear that the referendum would not take place while US President Donald Trump remains in office. He said the decision would need "an informed and calm debate" and could not be allowed to be "hijacked by the theatrics of an unpredictable president."

Coalition Avenir Quebec leader Christine Frechette conceded defeat, saying voters had made their choice and that she took full responsibility for the 'difficult result' Image: Mathieu Belanger/REUTERS

Severing ties with British monarchy?

The PQ's victory does not necessarily signal majority support for independence.

While in the last referendum for independence in 1995, just 50.58% voted to stay in Canada, recent polls show support for sovereignty at around 30%.

"If Quebec becomes independent it would make us politically, economically and militarily vulnerable," 19-year-old Alexia Gomez, told news agency AFP.

The Liberals and Conservatives have also voiced their opposition to an independence referendum, further complicating the PQ's path.

On the other hand, in a move more likely to find resonance among Quebecers, St-Pierre Plamondon's party has also pledged to reduce Quebec's ties to the British monarchy.

Monday's result comes just two weeks before Alberta voters decide whether to support beginning the process toward a referendum on separating from Canada.

World.title: Germany news: Saxony-Anhalt parliament sits after AfD win
World.content:
Von der Leyen urges EU states to avoid deep budget cuts Image: Pascal Bastien/AP Photo/picture alliance

Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, warned on Tuesday against major cuts to the European Union's next long-term budget.

"I am aware that balancing all of these constraints is not easy. I am also aware of the difficult budgetary situation in the member states," von der Leyen told the European Parliament in the French city of Strasbourg.

"But I would like to caution against large cuts. They would risk undermining critical priorities that we have all agreed upon," she added.

Negotiations on the long-term budget for the 2028-2034 period are currently underway. The EU's long-term budget, also known as the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), is the European Union's seven-year spending plan that sets how much the bloc can spend and on which priorities, such as agriculture, regional development, research, defense, migration, and climate policy.

The European Commission has proposed a budget of around €1.76 trillion (about $1.98 trillion). The budget is financed mainly through contributions based on the size of member states' economies.

The current MFF for 2021-2027 amounts to around €1.2 trillion.

Traditionally, Germany has opposed increases to the proposed budget, while other countries favor maintaining subsidies for economically disadvantaged regions. This time has been no different, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz calling for major cuts.

Ireland, which currently holds the rotating EU presidency, is expected to present a new compromise proposal in the coming days.

European Council President Antonio Costa aims to secure an agreement on the new budget by the end of the year.

"This ​is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the ​rest of my life," Kaur said as she announced her decision on social media.

The senior batter's decision to quit comes after she recently led her team to win their second successive Asian Games gold medal.

37-year-old Kaur became the ​highest-capped player in ‌women's international cricket this year.

The skipper led India in five tests, 51 ⁠one-day ⁠internationals and 155 T20 internationals.

She also led India to their maiden women's global title at last year's ODI World Cup.

Kaur's announcement comes after a review meeting was held by the Board of Control for Cricket in India on Monday,

In her statement on Tuesday, Kaur indicated that she would continue to play cricket.

"Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will." she said.

World.title: Trump says taxpayers will no longer fund ads touting administration
World.content:
Trump faced criticism from across the political divide after at least $1.5 million in federal funds was spent on TV ads. He says his MAGA Inc. super PAC will pay for future ads.

US President Donald Trump said Monday that taxpayer funds will no longer be used for television ads featuring him, which he claimed were a "standard thing to do," and said the cost will instead be borne by his super PAC.

The campaign-style ads, which cost at least $1.5 million (€1.34 million) in federal funds, drew criticism from lawmakers and ethics experts across the political divide.

What did Trump say about the ads?

Labeling the ads a "positive promotion for our Great USA," the US president said he decided to bear the costs himself and through his MAGA Inc. political action committee.

"This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

A White House official confirmed that MAGA Inc. would fund the ads going forward.

The MAGA Inc. super PAC had a war chest of more than $400 million by the end of July.

Trump ads warn of 'final battle'

The ads, which began airing in late September, feature Trump promoting his policies and warning against communism and of a "final battle" against "globalists."

They end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government.

Critics, including lawmakers from both parties, have questioned whether the ads violate restrictions on government propaganda and partisan political activity.

Democrats have said the administration transferred $20 million from the Department of Homeland Security to fund the ads and have called for independent investigations.

Trump has not said whether taxpayers will be reimbursed for the ads already aired.

World.title: Measles cases are spreading in the US this year, with over 1,000 infections reported in Pennsylvania
World.content:
A measles outbreak in Pennsylvania has topped 1,000 cases, with neighboring New York declaring a disaster emergency and mobilizing measures to fight the spread.

Over 1,000 cases of measles have been recorded so far this year in Pennsylvania alone, health officials in the northeastern US state said on Monday, the largest outbreak in a US state since the early 1990s.

The US Center for Disease Control (CDC) has put the number of cases recorded nationwide so far this year at 3,869, in what is seen as the worst year for measles since 1991.

What do we know about the latest measles outbreak?

The current outbreak started west of Philadelphia in April, health officials said. Nearly 200 people have been hospitalized and five have died. Nearly all of the cases involved people who were not vaccinated, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

In neighboring New York on Monday, Governor Kathy Hochul declared a month-long state disaster emergency to "strengthen ongoing efforts to confront" measles.

Over 100 cases have been recorded this year in New York State outside of New York City, with 92 of those reported in "under-immunized" rural areas since July 15.

The executive order suspends regulations on administering vaccines, expanding permission to paramedics and midwives, while allowing nurses to order testing and lowering permission barriers.

"No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease," Hochul said.

US vaccine coverage dips

Since last year, measles has broken out in several US states, including Texas, Utah and South Carolina, which has reported just under 1,000 cases.

Measles includes symptoms like high fever, cough, and rash. It can cause serious complications, especially in young children. It is highly contagious but can be prevented with vaccines.

However, skepticism toward vaccines in the US has risen in recent years, with more parents waiving routine vaccinations amid disinformation about vaccine safety.

Is the US experiencing a vaccine crisis? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In 2000, the US had eliminated the domestic spread of measles with high vaccination rates, but coverage has recently dipped below the 95% necessary to prevent outbreaks.

US Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr, who has expressed views skeptical of vaccines that are not backed by science, has characterized vaccinations as a "personal choice."

Although Kennedy maintains that the measles vaccine is the best defense against the highly contagious and potentially fatal infection, he has also advocated unproven "alternative treatments" like taking vitamins.

World.title: ICC unseals Taliban leaders' warrants over persecuting women
World.content:
The court gave more details on the warrants for four Taliban leaders accused of the crime against humanity of gender persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community. The Islamist group rejected the warrants.

The International Criminal Court (ICC) disclosed on Monday more details about the arrest warrants against two Taliban leaders, while also issuing two more arrest warrants.

The four Taliban leaders are accused of crimes against humanity through the persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community in Afghanistan since taking power in 2021.

According to the court, warrants were issued in July and September of last year against Hibatullah Akhundzada , the Taliban's Supreme Leader, as well as against Abdul Hakim Haqqani, who heads the country's Supreme Court.

The other two warrants were issued against Education Minister Habibullah Agha and Minister of Higher Education Neda Mohammad Nadim.

The four are charged with persecution on grounds of gender of "girls, women and other persons nonconforming with the Taliban's policy on gender, gender identity or expression; and on political grounds against persons perceived as 'allies of girls and women,'" according to the court.

An arrest warrant was issued against Taliban Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada [FILE: Aug 14, 2023] Image: WAKIL KOHSAR/AFP

What does the ICC accuse the 4 Taliban leaders of?

The judges who issued the warrants said that the four implemented policies that saw "severe violations of fundamental rights and freedoms of the civilian population of Afghanistan, in connection with conducts of murder, imprisonment, torture, rape and enforced disappearance."

The Taliban "specifically targeted girls and women by reason of their gender," the judges added, also mentioning persecution against people due to "certain expressions of sexuality and/or gender identity."

The ICC has no jurisdiction to execute the warrants. Still, the move is considered a form of pressure on the Afghan ruling authority.

The Taliban have taken a wide range of measures to restrict women's access to jobs and education beyond sixth grade, as well as barring them from most public spaces.

Women are also obligated to cover their whole bodies apart from their eyes upon leaving home, with a male relative having to accompany them on long trips.

Taliban rejects ICC's warrants

Afghanistan's government spokesperson said the country does not recognize the court's authority.

"We are bound by the rulings of Islamic Sharia and its courts, not by intelligence entities or so-called courts." chief spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid said in a statement.

The Taliban has returned to rule over Afghanistan since August 2021 Image: Javid Ashna/Middle East Images/picture alliance

A request for warrants for Akhundzada and Haqqani made last year by former ICC chief prosecutor Karim Khan argued that "Afghan women and girls as well as the LGBTQI+ community are facing an unprecedented, unconscionable and ongoing persecution by the Taliban.”

The UN Human Rights Council has called on the Taliban to drop its "systematic oppression of all women and girls in Afghanistan."

Human rights groups have been calling for the international community to do more against the Taliban's gender-based policies in Afghanistan.

World.title: Así gestó Sánchez el adelanto electoral: “Este Congreso no nos vale, tenemos que ir a elecciones, podemos ganar”
World.content:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez (en el centro), asiste a la reunión de la Comisión Ejecutiva Federal celebrada este lunes en la sede federal del PSOE.

El presidente y su núcleo duro ya hablaban de elecciones el jueves por la tarde, cuando empezaron a conocer que Junts iba al ‘no’. Las dudas eran por cómo está la izquierda, pero nunca se vio otra opción más que convocar ya

Aún no había amanecido en Nueva York, donde dormía Pedro Sánchez, cuando en Madrid se estaba produciendo a la vista de todos el acontecimiento que precipitaría un adelanto electoral que el presidente había rechazado decenas de veces. Rodeada de activistas del Sindicato de Inquilinas, de caras conocidas y muy identificadas con el progresismo —como Ana Belén, Juan Diego Botto y Carlos Bardem—, Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, abandonaba su casa en camilla, desahuciada por el fondo que la compró, después de 70 años pagando su alquiler.

Sánchez vivía en ese momento angustiado por la crisis de Ceuta, el gran asunto de la política nacional durante dos meses, que según algunos analistas podía ser la puntilla para el Ejecutivo y ahora ha quedado relegada a un segundo plano. Su núcleo duro, sus ministros, su entorno más cercano insistía ante todas las consultas: “Las elecciones están más lejos que nunca, necesitamos tiempo para resolver Ceuta, intentaremos los Presupuestos y después veremos. Podría ser marzo, pero cada vez es más probable ir a julio”.

En esta mañana del miércoles 23 de septiembre, ninguna de las personas clave del entorno del presidente, y mucho menos él mismo, podía siquiera vislumbrar que la política española estaba a punto de sufrir un enésimo giro completo de guion que llevaría a una convocatoria electoral en 2026, justo lo único que Sánchez dijo que no haría en ningún caso. “Habrá Presupuestos en 2026 y elecciones en 2027, repetía como un mantra el presidente.

02:26 Sánchez anuncia elecciones el 29 de noviembre

Sánchez estaba intentando por todos los medios salir del agujero de Ceuta, en el que le metían una y otra vez los medios, incluso los internacionales —en Nueva York la CNN le preguntó de forma muy directa qué había hecho mal para que entraran 80.000 personas y él admitió que Marruecos había fallado— y para ello había organizado una cita clave con Zohran Mamdani, el alcalde de Nueva York, gran referente progresista que ganó las elecciones precisamente con propuestas radicales en vivienda. El español estaba pletórico con los aplausos de Mamdani en la residencia oficial del alcalde, un hermoso palacete pegado al East River: “España ha subido el SMI el 66%. Sánchez ha mandado el mensaje de que el trabajo y la dignidad importan”, clamaba el neoyorquino.

Pero en España las cosas iban por otro lado. La indignación crecía con el desahucio de Maricarmen Abascal, especialmente en el mundo progresista. Sánchez entendió rápido que ese era un asunto que iba a cambiar totalmente el eje de la política, aunque en ese momento no podía imaginar que 10 días después le iba a llevar a convocar elecciones. En la rueda de prensa en Nueva York, el presidente ya se lanzó con todo contra Ayuso: “Están más preocupados en comprar aticazos pero han hecho caso omiso a una tragedia social como la de Maricarmen, que debería ser resuelta”. Ceuta empezó a pasar a un segundo plano en las noticias.

Maricarmen es sacada en camilla por sanitarios tras su desahucio, el 23 de septiembre en Madrid. ÁLVARO GARCÍA

Sánchez ya había hablado con sus colaboradores en Madrid y le habían dicho que la conmoción era tan grande que esta vez sí había agua para aprobar un decreto sobre vivienda con el escudo antidesahucios que llevaba meses negociándose, pero nunca se llevaba al Consejo de Ministros porque Junts daba largas. En esos días, Junts empezó a hablar de otra manera con la ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez. Ella se convenció, y se lo dijo al presidente, de que había agua en la piscina. Así se lo hizo pensar Miriam Nogueras, portavoz de Junts.

A partir de ahí se abrió una negociación intensa con todos los grupos pero cuidando especialmente a Junts, el eslabón más frágil de la cadena, y a Podemos, que también amenazaba con romperla si el decreto no era contundente y sobre todo si metían en él la reforma de la ley del suelo que pedía el PNV. Se consiguió eso: el PNV renunció a meter ahí la ley del suelo. Podemos además tenía la presión del Sindicato de Inquilinas, que pedía el voto a favor. Se cerró con Sumar la prórroga de los alquileres.

Todo iba bien. Junts logró incluir el 90% de sus propuestas, según explicó la ministra. Sobre todo deducciones fiscales. Incluso ya a punto de entrar al Consejo de Ministros el martes 29, Junts colocó la última medida, la garantía definitiva: si se paraliza un desahucio, las comunidades están obligadas a pagar al propietario la deuda que tiene el inquilino si no encuentran una solución habitacional.

Junts hizo ver que eso le valía. Pero el miércoles, cuando leyó el decreto en el BOE, empezó a ponerle pegas. Aun así, a Sánchez le preguntaron con Macron en La Moncloa, incluso le hablaron de elecciones anticipadas si no salía el decreto, y se mostró confiado: “Soy razonablemente optimista”.

El jueves al mediodía llegaron las primeras alertas. “Ojo, que Junts se puede ir al no, ni siquiera a la abstención. Se lo puede cargar todo”, le transmitieron a Sánchez algunas personas que conocían el debate interno. Varios ministros consultados empezaban a dudar. “Tienen que elegir entre la gente, que quiere el decreto, también los que les votan, o las presiones de la patronal y los lobbies de los fondos. Ellos sabrán, pero han demostrado hasta ahora varias veces que están muy perdidos”, señalaba uno de los mejor informados.

Ahí es cuando la hipótesis electoral empieza a fraguarse. Junts convoca su ejecutiva a las 21.00, y muchos se temen ya lo peor. Sánchez habla con su núcleo duro: Félix Bolaños, Óscar Puente, Óscar López, Diego Rubio [su jefe de Gabinete], la secretaria de organización del PSOE, Rebeca Torró. También contacta varias veces con Salvador Illa, su persona de máxima confianza, que además conoce bien a Junts aunque se relaciona más con la parte más pactista, encabezada por Jordi Turull. El presidente también habla con la andaluza María Jesús Montero.

La portavoz de Junts en el Congreso, Miriam Nogueras, el 2 de octubre. Pablo Monge

Son los dirigentes clave. Y la mayoría empieza a ver muy claro que si Junts tumba los decretos hay que ir a elecciones. No hay mucho más margen. “Si el Congreso no aprueba algo tan básico como un decreto de emergencia para parar desahucios como el de Maricarmen, ¿con qué cara vamos a ir a intentar unos Presupuestos?“, le dicen varios dirigentes. Otros se entusiasman. ”Es una oportunidad, podemos girar el discurso, hablar de vivienda, de sanidad, de educación, de los temas que importan, hay que ir a por todas", le repiten varios.

Sánchez siempre prefiere escuchar para madurar su decisión y no dejar claro qué va a hacer, mantener el misterio. Pero esta vez varios de los consultados le vieron mucho más decidido que en otras ocasiones. Él les repite a todos una frase que acabaría siendo definitiva, y que está de alguna manera en la comparecencia en la que anunció las elecciones el lunes: “Si no podemos aprobar políticas en el tema más fundamental, tenemos que convocar y decirle a la gente que necesitamos más diputados para aprobarlas”.

Las dudas, en realidad, según explican varios, pasaban más por el lado del espacio de la izquierda del PSOE, al que esta convocatoria le pilla desarmado, sin estructura, con un nombre recién elegido —Frente Amplio— y aún sin candidato, aunque rápidamente el fin de semana se ha apuntado hacia Mónica García.

Llega el viernes, y Sánchez comprueba en el Congreso que no es un farol. Que va en serio y con Junts no hay nada que hacer. Han decidido cargarse la legislatura a pocos días de que Carles Puigdemont sea definitivamente amnistiado por el Tribunal Constitucional, que está a punto de concederle el amparo que ha pedido. La sensación de traición de Junts, y también de suicidio político, es enorme en todo el equipo de Sánchez.

El presidente lo tiene cada vez más claro. Por la zona de Gobierno del Congreso pasan todos los ministros en una larga mañana de debate de los decretos. Hay un ambiente de funeral en los bancos de la izquierda del hemiciclo. Todo el mundo es consciente de que se está acabando la legislatura. Algunos en Sumar tienen más dudas. Otros, como Gabriel Rufián, de ERC, también rechazan ir a elecciones. Tampoco está preparado su proyecto de unificar a la izquierda.

Pedro Sánchez, junto a Yolanda Díaz, el viernes en el Congreso. Juan Medina (REUTERS)

Sánchez habla con Yolanda Díaz, con la que ha trenzado una relación política intensa de confianza en estos años. Lo llevan haciendo desde el jueves. Para él es importante entender si ese espacio está preparado. Necesita que aguanten, no le basta con absorberlos, porque hay millones de personas que jamás votarán al PSOE. Habla con los demás ministros de Sumar, entre los que está la probable candidata. Algunos de ellos también creen que es el momento de ir a elecciones. “Lo único seguro es que si hay elecciones nos pillan con la bandera correcta en las manos”, señala uno de ellos.

Todo se va a precipitar y no parece que la izquierda esté lista. Pero Sánchez no ve manera de seguir y sus ministros socialistas creen que la situación es una oportunidad para movilizar a la izquierda como en 2023, cuando el presidente dio la campanada con un millón de votos más de los previstos y logró seguir en La Moncloa. Sánchez prepara su discurso en la tribuna, a la que va a subir de manera inesperada e inusual, con una frase que ya huele a elecciones: “Hagan lo correcto, porque creo que, si no, la historia les juzgará antes de lo que creen y con más contundencia de la que imaginan”, le dice a PP, Vox y Junts.

Sánchez se va por la tarde a La Moncloa. No hay reuniones de crisis, solo una interminable lista de llamadas interrumpida por alguna sesión de deporte durante el fin de semana. Uno tras otro, todos los dirigentes socialistas consultados le van diciendo lo mismo: “La gente está indignada. Hay que ir a elecciones. Es una oportunidad”. Sánchez empieza una ronda con todos los dirigentes provinciales. Esta vez no habla solo con su núcleo duro, como es habitual. Ahora amplía al partido. Además pide análisis de datos. Los expertos de La Moncloa los escrutan. Las encuestas son muy malas, todas dan que el PP y Vox suman cómodamente la mayoría absoluta. Sánchez no se fía de esos sondeos, que ya fallaron en 2023. Los suyos le animan a ir a elecciones, a jugársela, porque ninguna encuesta puede medir ya el efecto de la conmoción Maricarmen.

Lo va teniendo cada vez más claro. Pero aún quiere ver las manifestaciones del sábado, probar cómo está el ambiente en la calle. La convocatoria de “rodea el Congreso” el viernes ha sido pequeña. El sábado, sin embargo, las manifestaciones se llenan. Es un mensaje contundente, aunque no definitivo.

Pero Sánchez está cada vez más decidido. A sus interlocutores les deja claro que es inviable intentar seguir con un Congreso que tumba el “decreto Maricarmen”. Y además señala lo que le dicen muchos dirigentes socialistas: hay que aprovechar el momento, como en 2023, subirse a una ola de movilización de la izquierda por la vivienda, darle la vuelta a las encuestas como entonces.

—Este congreso no nos vale, tenemos que ir a elecciones. Además tenemos una oportunidad para que la campaña vaya sobre vivienda, sobre educación, sobre sanidad. Podemos ganar —les repite Sánchez a los suyos.

Las elecciones están decididas, aunque el remate llegará el domingo, ya cuando Sánchez empieza a trabajar en su discurso con su Gabinete. Además habla con Bolaños para organizar todo lo que va a venir después, con dos consejos de ministros, uno extraordinario para las elecciones y otro ordinario para aprobar el contenido del decreto Maricarmen y llevarlo a convalidar ya en la diputación permanente, donde el Gobierno tiene mayoría sin Junts. Por último llama al rey para informarle a media tarde en una larga conversación telefónica, según La Zarzuela, de sus planes de convocar elecciones al día siguiente, cuando Felipe VI viaja a Finlandia.

“La derecha siempre dibuja a Sánchez como alguien aferrado al poder. Por eso se han vuelto a equivocar pensando que no convocaría elecciones. Pero Sánchez ya es un dirigente maduro, es el segundo presidente más longevo, ya tiene un legado muy claro, está en la historia. Él ha entendido que no hay condiciones para seguir con este Congreso y hay una oportunidad para ganar. Y por eso convoca. No hay más”, resume alguien que conoce muy bien al presidente y ha hablado mucho con él estos días. “No había manera de seguir. ¿Con qué cara íbamos a intentar negociar ahora unos Presupuestos con Junts? No tenía sentido y por eso nos vamos a elecciones”, señala un ministro.

Atrás han quedado todas las teorías conspiranoicas de que Sánchez no convocaría elecciones o incluso intentaría un referéndum de monarquía o república que circularon en muchos sectores. Todo ha sido mucho más normal. Una convocatoria como otras.

09:12 La comparecencia íntegra de Sánchez para anunciar elecciones el 29 de noviembre El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, anuncia la disolución de las Cortes y el adelanto de las elecciones generales al domingo 29 de noviembre. Foto: FERNANDO CALVO (EFE)

Resuelta la decisión, Sánchez la comunica el lunes y convoca un Consejo de Ministros extraordinario. Y ahí se lanza con un tono mitinero muy distinto al que había usado en la comparecencia institucional, donde se le veía cansado. El presidente arranca casi gritando: “¡Salimos a ganar y vamos a ganar!“. Eso obliga a todos los ministros del PSOE a hablar y lanzar mensajes similares, hasta convertir el consejo en una especie de mitin. Los de Sumar son más contenidos, pero también hacen discursos sobre la importancia de las elecciones y confían en ganar.

Todos son conscientes de lo importante que es que ese espacio se reactive. Poco antes de empezar el Consejo de Ministros, Sánchez bromea con los ministros de Sumar. Pero en realidad habla en serio: ”¡Tenéis que sacar un mínimo del 10%!“. La clave de las elecciones de 2023 es que el PSOE y el PP quedaron empatados arriba, por encima del 30%, y Vox y Sumar abajo, rondando el 12%. Pero ahora la ultraderecha se va según las encuestas al 18% y la izquierda, que de momento va por separado, no llega al 9% entre todos. Del cambio en esos números iniciales puede depender todo. Y de la capacidad de Sánchez para crecer más allá del 30%. El punto de partida de 2019 era difícil, el de 2023 casi imposible y este de 2026 parece más imposible aún. Sánchez y los suyos tienen 54 días para convencer a millones de personas de que vale la pena volver a cuadrar la carambola irrepetible.

World.title: “Si un alumno no entrena la capacidad de frustración, entre lo bueno y lo fácil elegirá lo fácil”
World.content:
Horizontes laborales en un futuro dominado por la IA. Conversaciones sobre la educación que queremos | Pensemos el mañana (Episodio 5)

Miguel Antón, profesor del IESE Business School, y su alumna Ana Jara charlan sobre qué habilidades deben desarrollar las futuras generaciones tras la irrupción de la IA en el mundo laboral: dominar la comunicación oral y el trabajo en equipo, preservar la capacidad de concentración y desarrollar el pensamiento crítico

Miguel Antón PROFESOR DE FINANZAS Y DIRECTOR DEL MIM Y DEL MIF EN IESE BUSINESS SCHOOL Es licenciado y máster en Economía por la Universidad de Navarra y doctor en Finanzas por la London School of Economics. En el IESE Business School su misión es guiar y formar a aquellos jóvenes que quieren convertirse en los ejecutivos del mañana en grandes compañías Ana Jara ALUMNA DEL MÁSTER EN MANAGEMENT EN IESE BUSINESS SCHOOL Después de estudiar Humanidades se matriculó en una escuela de negocios para dar un giro a su carrera y buscar mejores salidas laborales. Su objetivo al finalizar esta formación es incursionar en el universo de las grandes consultoras

¿Qué vamos a hacer cuando las máquinas hagan nuestro trabajo? La pregunta que abre esta nueva entrega de Pensemos el mañana, un proyecto de Fundación Unicaja y EL PAÍS para responder a los desafíos que presenta la educación, es la que articula la conversación entre dos perfiles muy concernidos, cada uno a su manera, por el futuro del mundo del trabajo: por un lado, el profesor del IESE Miguel Antón, cuya misión es analizar en profundidad los cambios en el mercado para ofrecer a los futuros ejecutivos las herramientas con las que puedan hacerse un hueco en una gran compañía; y por otro Ana Jara, una de sus alumnas, que observa con cierta inquietud cómo la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial (IA) puede cambiar por completo la estructura de las empresas.

“¿Un consejo para los jóvenes que quieran ser exitosos en el trabajo? Que comuniquen bien”

En este entorno volátil, Antón ofrece una receta en la que destacan varios pilares: dominar a la perfección la comunicación oral y saber trabajar en equipo; preservar la capacidad de concentración en un mundo inundado de estímulos; desarrollar el pensamiento crítico para manejar y cuestionar grandes volúmenes de información; entrenar la capacidad de frustración y buscar conocerse a uno mismo: las fortalezas, los deseos y los sueños más profundos, pero también las debilidades.

“Los alumnos tenemos miedo porque todo está evolucionando tan rápido que no sabemos si en dos años vamos a tener trabajo”

Un consejo, este último, que lleva al profesor a vaticinar que las nuevas generaciones, representadas en alumnos como Ana, deberán volver a plantearse a aquellas preguntas esenciales que en la Antigua Grecia dieron origen a la Filosofía, no solo para encontrar su sitio no solo en el mercado de trabajo sino en el mundo: ¿Quiénes somos?, ¿de dónde venimos?, ¿hacia dónde vamos?

Pensemos la educación del futuro ‘Pensemos el mañana’, un proyecto de Fundación Unicaja, busca fomentar el conocimiento, los valores de la educación, un aprendizaje sostenible y responsable y dar respuestas a los grandes desafíos de la educación del futuro. El proyecto pivota sobre seis ejes: 1 Aprendizaje y sentido vital 2 Bienestar y salud mental 3 Futuro y empleabilidad 4 Sostenibilidad y sentido colectivo 5 Tecnología y ética 6 Carácter y ciudadanía ¿Qué está ocurriendo en estos tiempos de cambios profundos y transversales? ¿Cuáles son los grandes retos para afrontar la transformación que viene? ¿Qué educación necesitamos? Diferentes personalidades de todos los ámbitos nos ayudarán a responder a estas y otras preguntas destinadas a impulsar cambios, dinamizar ideas y apoyar propuestas con impacto pedagógico y social. ‘Pensemos el mañana’ es un proyecto inspirador para las futuras generaciones llamadas a conquistar nuevas cotas del saber en un mundo complejo y cambiante.

World.title: Cómo hacer realidad el sueño de un científico
World.content:
La investigadora Nùria Casacuberta, una de las beneficiarias del programa Retorno del Talento de la Fundación Ramón Areces, en su centro de trabajo de la Escuela Politécnica Federal de Zúrich (Suiza).

Conseguir un aparato único para avanzar en el estudio de una enfermedad singular, volver a España después de tres lustros investigando en el extranjero... La Fundación Ramón Areces cumple 50 años impulsando con programas y becas la labor de los cientos de profesionales de la ciencia

Habla

Núria Casacuberta (Malla, Barcelona, 1982)regresó a España el pasado mayo tras pasar los últimos 14 años trabajando como investigadora oceanográfica en la Escuela Politécnica Federal de Suiza. Licenciada y doctora en Ciencias Ambientales por la Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, volvió con una certeza: no basta únicamente con encontrar una plaza, sino que hay que disponer de las condiciones necesarias y óptimas para seguir ejerciendo la ciencia en la vuelta a casa. Hace falta, explica, “financiación, infraestructura, personal y tiempo para desarrollar los proyectos abiertos”. En su caso, encontró el apoyo del Programa de Retorno del Talento, una de las iniciativas promovidas por la Fundación Ramón Areces para respaldar la investigación científica en el panorama nacional. Casacuberta reconoce que esta iniciativa le ha brindado la financiación necesaria para poder mantener sus líneas de investigación en España y abrir nuevos proyectos, lo que le ha aportado la “flexibilidad y las facilidades” para hacer posible esa transición “sin tener que empezar de cero”.

La oceanógrafa Núria Casacuberta en una de sus expediciones en el océano Ártico. Cedida por Núria Casacuberta

La Fundación Ramón Areces trabaja, desde su creación en 1976, en el apoyo a la ciencia a través de programas de ayuda para proyectos de investigación, para tesis doctorales y formación de excelencia. Solo en 2025 contribuyó a impulsar 312 investigaciones en áreas como las ciencias de la vida y la materia, ciencias sociales y humanidades, además de proporcionar más de un centenar de becas fuera de España dirigidas a estudiantes recién graduados y doctorados.

María Jesús Morán (Madrid, 1972), investigadora del hospital 12 de Octubre (Madrid), cuyo trabajo se centra en el estudio de las enfermedades mitocondriales, es beneficiaria de otro de los proyectos de la fundación, el programa PINERA para la investigación de enfermedades raras. Morán cuenta que “solo puede estar agradecida” por el apoyo recibido. “Los investigadores siempre nos quejamos de la falta de fondos porque realmente llevamos muchas décadas pidiendo que se aumente el porcentaje del PIB dedicado a ciencia”.

Aunque reconoce que cuando solicitó las ayudas no creía que se las fueran a conceder, Morán, licenciada en Biología por la Universidad Autónoma de Madrid y doctora en Bioquímica por la Universidad Complutense, ha encontrado la financiación que necesitaba. Gracias a PINERA, puede sufragar tres equipos de profesionales “estupendos, complementarios y competentes” con los que continuar sus estudios acerca del funcionamiento de las mitocondrias. “Ese apoyo es muy importante para nuestro ámbito. Es un soplo de esperanza para nuestros pacientes que entidades tan fuertes se acuerden de ellos y tengamos la oportunidad de hacer mejores estudios, más robustos científicamente”.

Los casos de Casacuberta y Morán permiten entender la filosofía que ha guiado a la Fundación Ramón Areces desde sus orígenes. A finales de los 70, cuando apenas existían instituciones privadas que apostasen por la investigación, la institución ya había construido una red de ayudas y programas para formar a los científicos españoles y abrir oportunidades para que pudieran desarrollar su talento en España. Su labor fue creciendo hasta el punto de que todo un premio Nobel de Medicina como el profesor Severo Ochoa inauguró en 1978 una de las primeras grandes iniciativas de la Fundación, el Programa de Actividades Culturales y Divulgación del Conocimiento. Desde entonces, decenas de premios Nobel de todo el mundo han compartido sus conocimientos y avances científicos en las actividades que organiza la Fundación.

Con un “marcado ADN científico”, como definen en la institución, fueron una de las primeras entidades privadas en poner el foco en las enfermedades raras. Esa atención específica permitió sentar las bases para, más adelante, impulsar programas más ambiciosos como PINERA, puesto en marcha en 2024. Otro de los pilares del trabajo de la fundación fue entender las necesidades de los científicos dentro y fuera de España. Así nació el Programa de Retorno del Talento, para ofrecer a aquellos investigadores en el exterior que desean volver las condiciones adecuadas para que puedan desarrollar su trabajo en España.

Los investigadores detrás de los programas La Fundación Ramón Areces ha ampliado en los últimos años sus programas de ayudas a la investigación con dos ambiciosas iniciativas, como son el Programa de Retorno del Talento y el Programa PINERA de Investigación en Enfermedades Raras (en la imagen, María Jesús Morán y Pablo Lapunzina reciben los diplomas de los proyectos seleccionados en la convocatoria de 2024)



Fotos: Cedidas por la Fundación Ramón Areces El programa de Retorno del Talento lleva cuatro ediciones proporcionando ayudas económicas para que científicos españoles en el extranjero puedan seguir continuando su labor en España. En la imagen, Núria Casacuberta, beneficiaria de la II edición Las becas en el extranjero ofrecen la posibilidad de estudiar en las universidades y centros más prestigiosos del mundo. La Fundación Ramón Areces también mantiene acuerdos para el acceso de investigadores españoles a diferentes centros internacionales. En la imagen, Silvia Basanta y Santiago de Navascués, que se han incorporado este año al Centro de Estudios Europeos Minda de Gunzburg (Estados Unidos) para trabajar codo con codo con la Universidad de Harvard El español Carlos Casquero continuará su trabajo con la beca de la Fundación Ramón Areces en el Instituto Ragon de Massachussets (Estados Unidos). Allí se ha unido a una comunidad investigadora que, desde hace tiempo, ha convertido el estudio del VIH y del sistema inmunitario en una parte fundamental de su misión La divulgación científica y cultural es otro de los pilares de la Fundación. En 2025 organizaron 127 actividades con ponencias de más de 600 expertos nacionales e internacionales, entre ellas, la Nobel Prize Conversation (en la imagen) que organizan junto a los organizadores detrás del prestigioso premio Nobel

El apoyo que reclaman (y necesitan) los científicos

Para María Jesús Morán, acceder al programa PINERA le ha permitido mejorar sustancialmente las condiciones de trabajo. Llevaba años reclamando la compra de nuevos equipos con los que continuar sus estudios sobre las mitocondrias —“el componente de las células que produce energía”, explica—, una de las patas fundamentales de su investigación sobre enfermedades raras. Necesitaba equipos “potentes y punteros” para analizar el consumo de oxígeno, pero estos “costaban mucho dinero”. El freno económico se acabó cuando le concedieron las ayudas y pudo sufragar los costes.

La labor de Morán ahora es “sacar el máximo partido” a esos equipos con los que puede desarrollar mejores estudios sobre los efectos de los tratamientos en los pacientes. Las herramientas que ha conseguido son poco comunes en España. “Te diría que somos el único hospital que tiene estos equipos. Y gracias a iniciativas como esta, creo que la investigación científica va mejorando, aunque a nosotros los investigadores nos gustaría que todo fuera más rápido”.

Núria Casacuberta coincide. “Tengo la impresión de que en los últimos años se ha producido un esfuerzo importante por aumentar y diversificar las fuentes de financiación”. A ella, el Programa Retorno le ha permitido volver a uno de los centros más prestigiosos de España en su campo: el Institut de Ciències del Mar (ICM-CSIC) de Barcelona. Así, puede continuar sus estudios sobre los cambios de circulación de los océanos Ártico y Subártico con “uno de los ingredientes más importantes para hacer ciencia: tener al lado personas con talento, motivación y ganas de hacer cosas nuevas”.

Acostumbrada a expediciones en los océanos más fríos del planeta, que a veces exigen “un año de preparación” para recopilar unas simples muestras, Casacuberta reconoce que la vida de un científico, pese a la creencia popular, no es rutinaria, sino “algo caótica”. Conese bagaje y experiencia internacional acumuladas en sus años en Suiza,la oceanógrafa cree que haber vuelto a España con “tantas facilidades” para desempeñar su pasión le da otra perspectiva. “Te ayuda a identificar mejor cuáles son tus puntos fuertes y ver los aspectos que podrían funcionar mejor de otra manera”. La investigadora reconoce que, si no existiese el Programa Retorno, “probablemente” no se habría planteado nunca su regreso. “Volver a tu país tiene una ventaja importante: conoces el sistema, el entorno y la forma de trabajar, y eso permite concentrarse en lo que realmente importa: hacer ciencia”.

World.title: Cinemas pause Naza screenings ahead of October 7 anniversary
World.content:
Cinema screenings of the Israeli documentary Naza, which investigates the war on Gaza, is being suspended from most Dutch cinemas from Tuesday until the weekend so that they do not coincide with the commemoration of the October 7 Hamas attacks.

This is in line with the wishes of the film’s makers, two Israeli documentarians, who fear that their safety – and that of their families, who are still in Israel – will be further threatened if the film is shown around the date.

The Dutch film distributor Cherry Pickers, which is responsible for the film in the Netherlands, has said it will heed their wishes. The duo have not yet returned to Israel since the film’s release, but their families have been harassed and the government is moving to strip them of their nationality.

Naza is composed of interviews with 24 anonymous Israeli intelligence and military personnel involved in military campaign on Gaza since October 7, 2023. They describe how civilians were routinely killed, often hundreds at a time, to target single militants.

They also describe how surveillance was used to track suspects and wait until they were at home with their families before bombing them, as well as using special AI systems to select and kill targets. Israeli officials have disputed many of the claims.

A screening of the film in Delft last week on the opening day was interrupted by an Israeli group, one of whom took a microphone and began telling the audience how her family was murdered by Hamas. Another tried to project footage of the attacks onto the cinema screen.

World.title: Patients fear shortage of medicinal cannabis when rules change
World.content:
Patients who rely on medicinal cannabis are worried about supplies running out when the government ends its contract with the only Dutch licensed grower next year.

The health ministry is not renewing the contract between the Bureau for Medicinal Cannabis (BMC) and Bedrocan from 2027 as part of a plan to liberalise the supply chain by letting suppliers sell directly to pharmacies.

But the rule changes have been delayed, meaning that Bedrocan, based in Emmeloord, will be unable to sell its products at all from next year.

The government says it will import medicinal cannabis from abroad to ensure patients are not denied treatment. The BMC has ordered in extra stocks for the start of next year, but these medicines will go out of date in mid-2027.

Around 7,000 people in the Netherlands are prescribed cannabis for conditions such as MS and epilepsy, or as a form of palliative care.

The MS Vereniging, which represents people with multiple sclerosis, warned that using a different variant of the medicine would be less effective for some patients.

Specific variety

In a letter to health minister Sophie Hermans, the MS association said some patients who had been prescribed cannabis long-term were dependent on a “specific variety” of the drug and switching to an alternative version would affect the quality of their treatment.

The ministry disputed this in its reply, saying there was “no scientific evidence that different varieties have different therapeutic effects”.

But Renger Witkamp, professor of pharmacology at Wageningen University, said different varieties of cannabis were known to work differently. “Cannabis is different from synthetic medicines,” he told the Volkskrant. “The plant contains dozens of chemicals that collectively determine the effect.

“The relationship between those chemicals is determined by the plant variety, but also by the conditions in which it is grown, such as light, soil and fertiliser.”

World.title: Heinen struggling to hit deadline for capital gains tax reform
World.content:
Finance minister Eelco Heinen is in a race against time to introduce a new capital gains tax system by his promised deadline of 2028, financial institutions have warned.

Heinen is under pressure from right-wing opposition parties JA21 and SGP to replace the current income tax regime as quickly as possible as part of the deal to pass next year’s budget.

The minister also needs to plug a €7 billion hole in the finances after left-wing parties Pro and Volt forced the government to drop its planned cuts to social security as the price for their support. The minority government needs the votes of at least two opposition parties in parliament to pass legislation.

Heinen said 2028 could be achieved with “the maximum stretch from everyone”. But banks and the Council of State, which advises the cabinet on the legal implications of its bills, cast doubt on his timetable when asked by NOS.

The Council of State said it was “impossible” to have its analysis ready by next Monday, October 12, so that parliament can debate the bill next week. A spokesman said October 19 was the earliest realistic date.

The Dutch banking association NVB said its members need time to adapt their IT systems so they can pass the relevant details of their customers’ income to the tax office.

Risk of fraud

If customers have to provide the information themselves it increases the risk of delays, inaccuracies and fraud, the banks have warned.

The tax office is also under pressure to update its systems to deal with other reforms, such as the introduction of compulsory work incapacity insurance for people who are self-employed.

Changing the income tax method at the same time would be likely to delay the insurance plan by a year, civil servants told NOS.

Every year that the cabinet delays the overhaul of the income tax system is costing the government an estimated €3.5 billion in lost revenue.

Assumed gains

Heinen’s latest draft does not explain how he plans to compensate for the income lost during the transition to capital gains tax, which will only raise tax on assets and investments when they are sold.

The current “box 3” method charges taxpayers on their assumed gains from their assets every year, but the Supreme Court struck out this system in 2021 because it was unfair on savers whose wealth was held in low-interest accounts.

Heinen included a proposal to lower the thresholds for the “box 3” wealth tax as a stopgap measure in his submission to the Council of State, but parliament has already indicated it does not support this reform.

World.title: Unhealthy food outlets dominate Dutch cities, say researchers
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The food in 10 major Dutch cities has become less healthy over the past decade, according to new research by Amsterdam UMC.

Health executives from the 10 cities have written to health minister Sophie Hermans urging her to speed up a promised food law that would let councils limit unhealthy outlets, Het Parool reported on Tuesday.

The researchers scored 31 types of food outlet, from greengrocers to fast-food chains. The scores combined expert ratings with checks of more than 83,000 products against the “Wheel of Five” (Schijf van Vijf), the official Dutch healthy eating guidelines.

Each neighbourhood was then given a score from -500 (extremely unhealthy) to +500 (extremely healthy), based on the type, number and proximity of nearby outlets.

All 10 cities scored negative in both 2014 and 2024, ranging from -252 in Groningen to -327 in Leiden. Amsterdam fell from -287 to -301. Across the cities, 77% of neighbourhoods scored lower in 2024 than 10 years earlier.

In Amsterdam, 96% of food outlets fall into categories the researchers rate as unhealthy. Some 87 of the city’s 90 secondary schools and vocational colleges are in what the report calls a “very unhealthy” food environment.

The councils say they currently lack a clear legal basis to refuse outlets selling unhealthy food.

“That more than nine in 10 secondary schools and vocational colleges are in an unhealthy food environment means young people are surrounded every day by an offer that makes choosing healthily harder,” Amsterdam health executive Alexander Scholtes told Het Parool. “I am not willing to resign myself to that.”

World.title: Cabinet wants phones out of schools from January
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The cabinet is calling on all primary and secondary schools to ban mobile phone use starting from January.

In a new proposal from digital economy minister Willemijn Aerdts, children would not be allowed to use their phones on school grounds, rules about children appearing in family vlogs would be tightened and the time children spend scrolling would be limited.

“Online, on social media or in video games, children quickly become exposed and face unacceptable risks,” Aerdts said in the proposal, called ‘Strategy Letter on Children’s Rights’.

Since 2024, there have been national agreements prohibiting the use of phones in the classroom.

The government does not have the authority to order schools to implement the policy and the education ministry will work with schools to come up with an agreement.

Aerdts is also keen to limit how children are used in online content, like family-style YouTube.

The cabinet also intends on commissioning research into sites like Netflix, YouTube, Roblox, Fortnite, ChatGPT, Instagram, Snapchat, and TikTok and their impact on children.

Earlier this year, the government has backed an EU-wide minimum age for social media. D66, VVD and CDA agreed in their coalition agreement to push for an enforceable European minimum age of 15.

World.content:

Nine Dutch restaurants have won Michelin stars for the first time in the 2026 edition of the guide, and two of them went straight in with two stars.

Azurite in Delft, run by chef Mario Ridder, and Suis in Schin op Geul, near Valkenburg, both entered the guide at two-star level, broadcaster NOS reported.

Suis only opened at the end of April, after chef Ralf Berendsen left La Butte aux Bois to start his own restaurant.

The 7 new one-star restaurants are spread across the country: Nassau in Groningen, Le Epifaan in Veeningen in Drenthe, Wild Atelier at the De Echoput hotel in Hoog Soeren, Bij Sidney in Loenen aan de Vecht, De Cuijt in Mierlo near Eindhoven, Rozewied in Kortgene in Zeeland, and Ambrozijn in Valkenburg.

Le Epifaan is run by Jarno Eggen, who previously cooked at two-star De Groene Lantaarn in Staphorst before it closed. Rozewied’s chefs, Noëmie Haentjens and Ferdy van Rijswijk, also won Michelin’s Young Chef Award.

Matthijs Vrancken and Nouri Haj Romdhane of Brut172 in Reijmerstok won the sommelier award. Château Neercanne in Maastricht won the award for service.

De Librije in Zwolle remains the only three-star restaurant in the Netherlands, a rating it has held since 2004. Nelson Tanate now leads the kitchen following the death of co-owner and chef Jonnie Boer in April 2025.

No Amsterdam restaurant won a new star this year, and Daalder and De Juwelier lost theirs, AT5 reported.

In total, the Netherlands has 119 starred restaurants, the same number as last year.

World.title: Is it hard to make friends with the Dutch or is it you?
World.content:
Our regular columnist wants to know whether the Dutch are really so hard to make friends with – or is the problem you?

“It’s just so hard to make friends with the Dutch,” the woman seated next to me bemoans. I’m at a dinner party made up mostly, but not entirely, of internationals.

In fact, a Dutch woman seated across from us agreed. She’d recently moved to The Hague after living in Groningen for the past few years and was apparently also struggling to meet people.

It’s an oft-heard complaint in international circles.

Pretty much every organisation catering to internationals in the Netherlands has some advice for how to achieve this virtually impossible feat.

“Many locals have their own social groups that they have maintained since childhood,” the Leiden International Center patiently explains.

The city of Amsterdam sets the bar low. “A neighbour doesn’t have to become a friend (although they might!) – even just being on nodding terms with the people living around you can help you feel at home,” it advises.

There are dozens of threads on Reddit from the recently relocated who are struggling to find connections amongst the Dutch.

True to form, one Dutch poster replies: “We don’t know you, you might just be unlikable for all we know.”

While this may be harsh – sorry, direct – it’s also probably the truth.

You might not be unlikeable in an existential sense. You’re probably a nice person who has friends and loved ones that just happen to live elsewhere. But to the average Tina, Henk and Luca, you just don’t bring much to the table.

First, let’s start with the idea that Dutch people establish their social roster before evacuating the womb.

It is true, in my experience, that Dutch people maintain the friendships they made in childhood and university. This is also true of literally everyone. I concede that the country is small, which makes it easier to keep up with those friendships.

But really, most of us make our friends prior to our early 20s. You just choose to leave yours behind for clogs and tulips. Now your lineup is empty and you’re clawing for a position on a team with few openings.

Which leads me to my second point: there is a reason most of us make friends early in life. It is significantly easy to make friends prior to reaching adulthood. The foundations of primary school friendships are “The other child was randomly selected to sit next to me” and “Who wants to play the same game at recess.” You go to school all day, you see these people all the time and you haven’t yet been downtrodden by the stresses of life.

Now you need to find more of a connection than “I like playing in the sandbox with you” and you need to find the time to make that connection, somewhere between working, exercising, raising your children, spending time with your partner and remembering to order a shower curtain. (If my husband is reading this, I am sorry – I forgot again.)

Even the aforementioned Dutchie at my dinner party was struggling. It’s not simply because you’re a foreigner, it’s just hard to make friends post-graduation.

It is, however, also because you are a foreigner. Dutch people do speak English but that doesn’t mean they want to speak their second language all the time. The language barrier also makes it harder for you to mesh into a group. If you make a Dutch friend and they invite you to their birthday party, you’re now forcing everyone in the circle to switch to English.

Plus, you don’t share the same cultural references, the same jokes, the same base understanding of the world. None of this is insurmountable but it all makes it more difficult to form a bond.

If you came here looking for advice on how to make friendships with the Dutch, you’re in the wrong place. This isn’t an advice column. Making friends as an adult is challenging and you’re playing that game on hard mode by trying to do it across cultural and language differences.

In the meantime, you can try just nodding at people. Maybe eventually one of has them just moved from Groningen and is also desperately trying to convince others that they are likable.

World.title: International train connection from Groningen to Leer returns
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

After almost 11 years, people can again travel by train from Groningen to the German city of Leer.

Services were suspended in 2015 after a cargo ship crashed into the Friesenbrücke, the rail bridge over the Ems on the German side of the border.

At Groningen central station, travelers lined up at 5:30am to catch the first train in over a decade.

The rebuilt Friesenbrücke is 335 metres long and is Europe’s largest lift-swing rail bridge. Its 145-metre central section lifts and turns to let ships pass.

The new bridge was opened in 2024, but needed additional testing before rail service could resume.

Regional Director Gerrit de Groot of Arriva, which maintains the rail service, told RTV Noord he was “delighted” with the reopening. “It is fantastic that, as a regional carrier, we are making international transport possible in this way. It is a wonderful moment,” he said.

The journey takes around 90 minutes. Arriva expects that they will see peaks of travel during the holiday season when people want to visit the Christmas markets across the border.

World.title: Reports claim Trump tried to change Poland’s government. What do we know?
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. Media reports claim that US President Donald Trump, during a previously unreported meeting earlier this year with Poland’s defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, suggested that he leave Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s ruling coalition and form a new government with the right-wing opposition. Kosiniak-Kamysz has confirmed that the meeting took place, but has not commented on what was discussed. Meanwhile, Tusk himself has said that, while he wants to “maintain discretion”, the information he received from Kosiniak-Kamysz indicates that Trump was interested in discussing the “internal situation in Poland”. Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski has even more bluntly suggested that the meeting may have served as “an attempt to involve a foreign state in our internal politics”. Below, we outline how the controversy unfolded, what we know so far, and how senior political figures have commented on the issue. The context Poland’s government is a broad coalition that ranges from left to centre right. Although Tusk’s centrist Civic Platform (KO) dominates, it would not have the parliamentary majority necessary to rule if it lost any of its junior coalition partners. One of those partners is the Polish People’s Party (PSL), which is the most conservative element of the coalition. It has clashed with its partners over issues such as abortion and LGBT+ rights. PSL is led by Kosiniak-Kamysz, who serves as both deputy prime minister and defence minister. Some elements of the right-wing opposition have suggested that PSL could break with Tusk to form an alternative government, perhaps even with Kosiniak-Kamysz as prime minister. Last year, PSL controversially polled its members on whether they would want to do so. However, PSL and its leader have repeatedly insisted that they remain loyal to Tusk’s coalition. The Polish People's Party's parliamentary survival is on a knife edge, and could determine whether @donaldtusk's coalition remains in power after next year's elections.@AleksSzczerbiak looks at the challenges facing PSL and how it may respond to them https://t.co/MmswSLNWJE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 30, 2026 Meanwhile, the government is in constant conflict with President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition. Nawrocki is also a close ally of Trump, who endorsed him during last year’s presidential election. By contrast, Tusk and his government have clashed with the Trump administration, though they also seek to maintain close relations with the US as Poland’s most important security partner. The meeting The news that Kosiniak-Kamysz had met with Trump in March this year came to light in a rather roundabout way. On 21 September, Poland’s defence ministry announced that a planned meeting at the Pentagon between Kosiniak-Kamysz and his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth, planned for 23 September, had been cancelled “at the urgent request of the American side”. The official reason for the change of plans was Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US at the same time. However, some commentators in Poland claimed that Hegseth had actually cancelled the meeting at the behest of figures close to Nawrocki. In an effort to debunk those claims, Adam Bielan, a senior PiS figure from the opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, claimed that he and Nikodem Rachoń, a presidential advisor, had helped to arrange a meeting earlier this year between Kosiniak-Kamysz and a US figure “much more important than Hegseth”. Rachoń later confirmed this, but said that the meeting had been secret and he was unable to reveal the identity of the US official. He urged Kosiniak-Kamysz to do so. The defence minister obliged, confirming that the meeting had been with Trump himself and had taken place at the White House on 2 March, alongside a ceremony at which a US army officer, Michael Ollis, was posthumously awarded the Medal of Honour for giving his own life to save that of a Polish officer, Karol Cierpica, in Afghanistan. “I had the opportunity to talk to President Trump for a moment, for which I am very grateful,” said Kosiniak-Kamysz, who noted the role of Nawrocki’s office in arranging the conversation. What did Trump say to Kosiniak-Kamysz? Neither Rachoń nor Kosiniak-Kamysz indicated what had been discussed at the meeting. However, last Friday, Dominika Wielowieyska, a leading Polish journalist, claimed that her conversations with various sources, who she did not name, had indicated that Trump used the meeting to encourage Kosiniak-Kamysz to split with Trump and form a new government with the right-wing opposition. “Trump suggested to Kosiniak-Kamysz that it would be best if he formed a coalition with the right, and that then they would have 100% support from the United States and the presidential administration, and the door would essentially be open to achieving great success for many Poles,” said Wielowieyska, who writes for Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading liberal daily that is hostile towards Nawrocki and sympathetic towards Tusk. She added that Kosiniak-Kamysz had immediately shared information about the meeting with the government but that Rachoń had failed to submit a note about it to the foreign ministry, despite that being normal practice and despite a request for a note from foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. Today, Republika, a right-wing broadcaster with close ties to Nawrocki and the opposition, likewise reported, based on unnamed sources, that, “during the conversation with Kosiniak-Kamysz, there were indications that the Americans were interested in a change of prime minister in Poland”. What has Poland’s government said? On Friday, Sikorski took to social media to respond to a claim by Bielan that the Trump-Kosiniak-Kamysz meeting was intended to “unblock” negotiations regarding Poland’s desire to host a new permanent US military base. “In the case of such an important conversation, the organiser [Rachoń] had an obligation to prepare a note,” wrote Sikorski, adding that such a document never reached the foreign ministry. “Could that be because the meeting also served as an attempt to involve a foreign state in our internal politics?” Z tak ważnej rozmowy organizator miał obowiązek sporządzić notatkę. Do @MSZ_RP ona nie dotarła. Czyżby dlatego, że spotkanie służyło też próbie zaangażowania obcego państwa w naszą wewnętrzną politykę? https://t.co/0wL0QZBxPv — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) October 2, 2026 On Monday, Tusk himself told broadcaster TVN that Kosiniak-Kamysz had informed him about his meeting with Trump immediately after it took place. He added that the subject of the meeting “is too interesting to talk about publicly”, but that military “bases were not the topic of the conversation”. “The conversation was of a confidential nature, and therefore I feel obliged to maintain discretion. It was more about the internal situation in Poland, that’s how I would put it most delicately,” said Tusk. Kosiniak-Kamysz himself also confirmed on Monday that the question of a permanent US base in Poland had not been discussed at the meeting. He noted that, in March, that issue was not even seriously on the table, because it was only two months later that Trump announced he intended to send additional troops to Poland The defence minister did not give any further details about the content of the meeting, which he described as “informal”. Thousands of protesters blockaded a bishop inside a church in a Polish village on Sunday – and some even physically attacked him – amid anger over the dismissal of a popular long-serving local Catholic priest. As a result, police were called in and, after efforts by negotiators to calm the crowd failed, officers escorted the bishop away from the premises after midnight. „Kościół w Grojcu otoczyło kilka tysięcy osób, parafian i uczęszczających do grojeckiej świątyni. #Aktualnie Okrzyki „jesteśmy z Tobą” dla księdza Józefa Zborka." Materiał od @FaktyOswiecim pic.twitter.com/3zaqlBCDF6 — Sebastian Kościelnik (@S_Koscielnik) October 4, 2026 The incident took place in the village of Grojec, near the city of Oświęcim in southern Poland. The municipality has an official population of around 3,200, but local media – including the Gazeta Krakowska newspaper and Fakty Oświęcim website – report that around 3,000 people gathered on Sunday evening to protest. They were angered by the decision to remove local priest Józef Zborek, who has served in the parish for almost 30 years, from his position. The diocese of Bielsko-Żywiec says the priest was found in church proceedings to have been guilty of “serious and proven irregularities in the performance of his duties”. However, the actual nature of his offences has not been publicly revealed, with the church noting that, under canon law, only Zborek himself can do so. The case against him was initially reported in 2024. The priest repeatedly appealed against the decision, taking the case to the Vatican. However, the decision to remove him was upheld, with Zborek removed from his position on Saturday. On Sunday, Roman Pindel, the bishop of Bielsko-Żywiec, visited Grojec to meet with the parish council and discuss the situation. Afterwards, he proceeded to the local church to attend the Eucharist. However, before his arrival, thousands of people had gathered around the church, holding signs saying “Don’t take away our parish priest”. Some burst inside and disrupted the ceremony. Asked about the reasons for Zborek’s popularity, one woman told Gazeta Krakowska that he had accepted children who had been turned away by other priests for first communion and had “no problem baptising illegitimate children”. News website Onet reports that one local theory is that the priest was removed from his position because he had not charged parishioners for sacraments. Churches in Poland generally expect people to make payments in return for sacraments such as baptism, confirmation and marriage. 🔴Sceny pod kościołem. Biskup w eskorcie policji. Jest nagranie Nocna interwencja policji przed kościołem w Grojcu w Małopolsce. World.title: Poland updates nuclear strategy with delays to launch of first two plants
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government has updated Poland’s nuclear strategy for the first time in six years, with the new document acknowledging that the country’s first-ever nuclear plant will go online in 2036, three years later than previously planned, and the second in 2040, one year behind schedule. The delays were widely anticipated, as Poland is already behind the schedule set out in the previous nuclear programme, adopted under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government in 2020. However, the current administration says the country is still on track for nuclear to become a major part of a more diversified energy mix, providing around 15-16% of electricity generation by 2040. “This is not just a plan to develop new capacity, but also to build a strong Polish nuclear industry,” energy minister Miłosz Motyka wrote on social media. “We are building a nuclear sector that will drive the Polish economy and serve our security for decades to come.” Rząd przyjął aktualizację Programu polskiej energetyki jądrowej 🇵🇱 To nie tylko plan rozwoju nowych mocy, ale także budowy silnego polskiego przemysłu jądrowego ⚡️ ✅ W sumie do 9 GWe nowych mocy jądrowych; ✅ coraz większy udział polskich firm – docelowo nawet 70 proc. przy… pic.twitter.com/8DorRLUWUj — Miłosz Motyka (@motykamilosz) September 29, 2026 Under the updated Polish Nuclear Power Programme (PPEJ), Poland plans to develop two nuclear power plants with a combined capacity of around 6 GW to 9 GW, using large-scale Generation III+ reactors. The first plant, which will have a total capacity of about 3.75 GW, is being built in partnership with an American consortium made up of Westinghouse and Bechtel in the municipality of Choczewo on the Baltic coast. Preparatory work at the site is already underway. The European Commission last year approved Polish state aid for the project, which is set to receive 60.2 billion zloty (€13.8 billion) in public support between 2025 and 2030 In March 2026, the investor submitted an application to the president of the National Atomic Energy Agency for a permit to construct the plant, with the pouring of the first nuclear concrete scheduled for 2028. The first reactor is now expected to enter commercial operation in 2036, three years later than previously planned. Construction of Poland’s first nuclear power plant is now set to begin after the @EU_Commission approved Warsaw’s request to allocate 60 billion zloty (€14.2 billion) in state aid for the project https://t.co/Z7BJpRRKnq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 9, 2025 Plans are already underway for a second nuclear power plant, with construction scheduled to begin in 2032 and the first unit expected to come online around 2040, one year later than previously planned. Bełchatów and Konin in central Poland remain the preferred locations for that plant, with both areas offering existing energy infrastructure and extensive experience in electricity generation. Companies from the United States, France and Canada are currently competing to supply the technology and build it, with Poland to choose its partner next year. Alongside expanding nuclear capacity, the programme aims to increase the role of Polish companies in the sector. Domestic firms are expected to account for about 40% of the value of the first reactor project, according to the government. That share could rise to as much as 70% for subsequent units as Polish companies build up expertise, experience and the necessary certifications. The government also plans to develop the broader skills base needed to support the nuclear industry, involving universities, research institutes, technical schools and businesses. A group of prominent Polish businesspeople – including @RBrzoska of @InPostPL and @mati Staniszewski of @ElevenLabs – are investing in a project to develop small modular nuclear reactors being led by Poland's richest man, Michał Sołowow https://t.co/NFoCh9JmYz — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 1, 2026 The expansion of nuclear power is part of a broader effort to reduce Poland’s traditional reliance on coal, which currently generates around half of the country’s electricity. That is by far the highest figure in the EU. Poland has already been diversifying its energy mix. Coal has declined from supplying 87% of power a decade ago. Meanwhile, the share of renewables has risen from 9% to 29% over the same period. Under a national energy and climate plan approved in June, Poland aims by 2040 for coal to account for only 0-5% of the energy mix. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%). Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 As well as traditional large-scale nuclear power plants, Poland is also pursuing small modular reactor (SMR) projects. SMRs, which are prefabricated in factories before being installed onsite, are much smaller than traditional reactors, and proponents say they provide a faster and more cost-effective way of adding nuclear capacity.
