World.title: From Streets to Polling Stations: Serbia’s Student Movement Takes Electoral Test
World.content:
When Serbia’s students began blockading their universities after the fatal collapse of the canopy at the railway station in Novi Sad in November 2024, entering parliament was not part of the plan.

Their demands were directed at Serbia’s institutions: publication of documentation relating to the station reconstruction, prosecution of those accused of attacking students commemorating the victims, the dropping of charges against arrested students, and increased funding for higher education.

“At that point, we did not even know what the electoral process involved. We simply wanted justice,” said Milica Najdanovic, a student at the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering.

Five months of university blockades and mass protests changed the calculation. Concluding that their original demands would not be met, the students added another: early parliamentary elections.

World.title: One Click, Money Gone: Albania Battles Spike in Cyber Fraud
World.content:
It all started with a text message in May. Gentjana Driza was waiting for a delivery from e-commerce marketplace Temu when she received a message apparently from Albania Post, telling her to pay a small customs fee.

The message contained a link. Driza clicked on it and was taken to a series of forms. According to her complaint to the police, she believed the request genuinely came from Albania Post, so she followed the instructions and entered her personal and banking details.

She soon realised she had been scammed. Notifications began appearing on her banking app showing substantial transfers from her account. The transactions continued even after she contacted her bank and blocked her card.

Over the next three days, around 100,000 lek (1,085 euros) was taken from Driza’s account. The exact amount remained unclear, as transactions continued to be processed.

World.title: Nationalist Parties Celebrate Wins in Bosnia Election, But Many Voters Stay Home
World.content:
“It was not a surprise because we as citizens cannot free ourselves from the ethno-national frameworks,” political analyst Tanja Topic told BIRN after Bosnia’s dominant nationalist parties claimed victory on October 4 in the general election.

The [Bosniak] Party of Democratic Action, SDA, the Croatian Democratic Union, HDZ BiH, and the [Serb] Alliance of Independent Social Democrats, SNSD, each remained the strongest force in their respective ethnic camps, while many voters stayed at home – and a new challenger shook up the Bosniak field.

Topic said most voters clearly looked past the corruption, crime, nepotism and clientelism on which power rests, as each wave of national homogenisation follows another, leaving the country stuck in a vicious circle.

World.title: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



The first reading of the special court law amendment at the Kosovo parliament, October 5, 2026. Photo: Antigone Isufi/BIRN.

Kosovo MPs on Monday voted to amend the law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers so the Hague-based court, part of Kosovo’s justice system, may not impose a sentence of imprisonment exceeding 15 years. The amendment has not been adopted yet, as it must undergo a parliamentary committee review and return for a second reading.

Outside parliament, protesters who had staged an all-night vigil in front of the legislature chanted: “Vote [for] the law.”

The vote comes amid anger in Kosovo after the court sentenced former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci and three other former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, Jakup Krasniqi, Kadri Veseli and Rexhep Selimi, to 25, 25 18 and 13 years in prison respectively for war crimes on September 16.

The four were found guilty of arbitrary detention, cruel treatment, torture and murder from April 1998 to June 20, 1999, in Kosovo and several locations in Albania.

Critics have, among others, claimed that the court did not apply the “lex mitior” principle, which allows defendants to be sentenced under the most favourable law of the time that the crime was committed. According to the applicable law of former Yugoslavia, the maximum prison sentence is 15 years.

The amendments include for the sentences to be served in Kosovo. Based on the current law, “the Specialist Chambers may order the transfer of a convicted person to a third country for service of his or her sentence of imprisonment”.

The amendments also grant Kosovo’s President power to grant pardons, the work of the court to be subjected to monitoring by international organisations, and for a constitutional review of the law to be conducted by the Constitutional Court of Kosovo.

It is not certain whether a second reading will take place on Monday.

Bedri Hamza, chair of the opposition Democratic Party of Kosovo, PDK, which Thaci founded, and which proposed the amendments, said before the vote that the law does not belong to his party, even if it “is a PDK initiative”.

The verdict, which is to be appealed, caused outrage in Kosovo and people have been protesting daily ever since.

It also led to the initiative to change the law on the court. The court is a hybrid tribunal – although it is part of Kosovo’s judiciary, it is staffed with internationals and located in The Hague.

It was established in 2015 under pressure from Kosovo’s Western allies because of concern of potential witness intimidation if the processes were to be held domestically in Kosovo.

The court has a mandate to try crimes committed from January 1, 1998, to December 31, 2000, based on a Council of Europe report by Swiss Senator Dick Marty, which made allegations of war crimes and organ trafficking by KLA fighters.

An EU Special Investigative Task Force, led by former US prosecutor Clint Williamson, concluded that there was enough evidence to indict suspects for war crimes and crimes against humanity, but not enough to bring charges for organ trafficking.

The amendments of the law aim to change the mandate of the court to only cover crimes allegedly committed after the Kosovo war, from July 1, 1999 until December 31, 2000. The draft amendment says that the court will not have jurisdiction over acts that were not committed in relation to the allegations of organ-trafficking in the Dick Marty report – for which it has already been established that there is not enough evidence for trials.

On Monday, before the law was put to a vote, Prime Minister Albin Kurti reminded MPs that the country faces another crisis, over the election of a President.

“A law regarding the Hague court is necessary, but so is a President of Kosovo. Proceeding with one without the other could be highly detrimental. We cannot claim to be defending Kosovo’s interests in The Hague while allowing an institutional vacuum to develop within Kosovo,” he said.

Tuesday is the constitutional deadline for Kosovo to elect a President and finalise the formation of institutions deriving from the June 7 elections. If a President is not elected, the country faces its fourth parliamentary elections in less than two years.

Even if the law amendments pass the second reading, they will be enforced only after the appeals panel at the Kosovo Specialist Chambers issues a verdict for Thaci and the three others.

World.title: Serbs Abroad May Have to Vote Overnight Under New Election Rule
World.content:
Serbs voting abroad in upcoming elections will have to follow polling hours based on Central European Time under a new decision adopted in the early hours of Monday morning by the Republic Electoral Commission, RIK, which has set standardised voting hours of 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The decision means that while some polling stations abroad will operate simultaneously with those in Serbia if they are in the same time zone, voters in some countries, including the United States, Australia and Indonesia, may have to cast ballots during local nighttime hours.

The proposal was passed by 20 RIK members in favour, while seven voted against. Several RIK members criticised the move, arguing it could make it harder for Serbian citizens abroad to exercise their right to vote. They also questioned why the Foreign Ministry, which initiated the proposal, had become involved in determining polling hours.

RIK member Ivan Sebek said such an arrangement had never been introduced since Serbia began organising voting abroad, and no previously reported problem justified it. “You are further restricting voters’ rights and effectively cutting the time available to exercise their right to vote in half,” Sebek said.

Other RIK members raised concerns about voters’ safety when voting at night. Vladimir Dragas called it “completely illegal” and warned it could anger some diaspora voters, forced to cast their ballots in the middle of the night.

The decision comes as the governing Serbian Progressive Party faces its strongest challenge since it came to power in 2012, from the recently-established opposition Student List, which grew out of the student-led protest movement. Some commentators have suggested there is strong support for the students’ cause among diaspora Serbians.

The change in voting times has worried some Serbian voters around the world.

Marija, who lives in China, speaking to BIRN on condition of anonymity, said the opening hours of the Serbian embassy on election day would be inconvenient, lasting from 2 p.m. until 3 a.m. Another issue is that, for the whole of China, only one polling station has been approved, in Beijing.

“Considering that China is a huge territory, the travelling distance we are talking about is huge … Don’t forget families who need to add two hours per flight, book accommodation, eat in Beijing, and come back home the same day. Also, local laws are very strict when it comes to people gathering, especially around the San Li Tun area [where most of the embassies are],” she explained.

Marija said diaspora voters had already faced various difficulties since the elections were announced.

“When we initially contacted the authorities about our request to vote abroad, we did not receive timely responses to our emails. In some cases, we had to wait a day or two for an answer. There were also significant delays concerning the documents we were supposed to receive from our local authorities in Serbia confirming we were eligible to vote outside the country, particularly here in China,” she said.

She said they had been expecting polling stations to be opened wherever at least 100 citizens had registered. However, only one polling station, in Beijing, was ultimately approved.

The same issue has emerged in Australia, where polling stations were approved only in Melbourne and Sydney, even though more than 100 Serbian voters have registered also in Perth and Brisbane.

Nemanja Djurovic told BIRN that voters from Brisbane have been directed to vote in Melbourne, even though Sydney is closer.

He added that the decision to open polling stations in only these two cities would result in many people not voting, as travel is a financial burden, and some citizens, like pregnant women, will not be able to take the flights that are necessary.

“The state is effectively slapping Serbian citizens living in Brisbane and Perth in the face. We are deeply disappointed and feel like second-class citizens because our rights are being openly ignored. The state is sending us a clear message that it does not want the diaspora to vote,” Nemanja said.

He added that the voting hours could significantly affect turnout in Australia, as polling there would take place from 5 p.m. on Sunday until 6 a.m. on Monday, when many people would already be preparing for work.

“Public transport stops running around midnight, while some bus services stop even earlier. This will significantly reduce turnout,” he predicted.

“The authorities want to prevent the first results coming from diaspora polling stations in the east from being negative for them,” he added.

World.title: In Montenegro, Whistleblower Reports Rise, But Convictions Remain Rare
World.content:
A growing number of Montenegrins are blowing the whistle on irregularities, abuse or corruption in their workplaces, but rarely do those behind the wrongdoing end up in court.

According to data from the Agency for Prevention of Corruption, ASK, the rate of whistleblowing has shot up since 2020, when the Democratic Party of Socialists, DPS, left office after three decades of uninterrupted rule.

Between 2016 and 2025, a total of 1,259 whistleblower reports were filed, according to the ASK. Seventy-two per-cent of those reports came after 2020.

Yet since 2016, indictments have been raised by prosecutors in only four cases based on whistleblower reports. Two of those resulted in convictions, though the ASK said it did not know whether those verdicts were final.

The rise in reports is evident in the ASK data, which 110 were submitted in 2019 compared to 142 in 2021, 188 in 2022 and 190 in 2023.

World.title: Bosnian Election Sees Record Low Turnout, Dodik Triumphant, Presidency Reshaped
World.content:
Republika Srpska Prime Minister Savo Minic (L) and Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD) President, Milorad Dodik (R) celebrate after the announcement of the early results in Banja Luka, 04 October 2026. Photo: EPA/NIDAL SALJIC.

With more than 90 per cent of votes counted in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s general elections, preliminary results on Monday morning indicated a new composition for the country’s three-member presidency – amid a turnout that plummeted 9.5 per cent compared to the previous nationwide elections in 2022.

The presidency looks set to comprise Denis Becirovic of the United for Bosnia and Herzegovina coalition as the Bosniak member, Darijana Filipovic of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, HDZ BiH as the Croat member, and Zeljka Cvijanovic of the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats, SNSD as the Serb member.

Becirovic won a second term as the Bosniak member of the presidency with 38.12 per cent, ahead of Party of Democratic Action, SDA leader Bakir Izetbegovic on 33.98 per cent and Semir Efendic of the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina on 25.75 per cent.

HDZ BiH candidate Filipovic won the race for the Croat seat with 46.55 per cent, ahead of Democratic Front candidate Slaven Kovacevic on 30.57 per cent and independent candidate Zdenko Lucic on 22.88 per cent.

The SNSD’s Cvijanovic won the Serb seat with 55.37 per cent, securing a second term. Serb Democratic Party, SDS candidate Marinko Bozovic received 26.54 per cent, while Nebojsa Vukanovic won 18.08 per cent.

Turnout nationwide was just 42 per cent. The Central Election Commission has stressed that the results remain preliminary as counting continues.

Voters on Sunday cast ballots for the members of the state presidency, the state parliament, the president of Republika Srpska, entity parliaments and cantonal assemblies in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The results secure the continued political influence of Bosnian Serb nationalist leader Milorad Dodik, the head of the SNSD, even though he has been barred from standing for public office due to a conviction.

“I declare victory at all levels. Thank you to everyone,” Dodik said after the vote.

In the Republika Srpska entity, the SNSD was leading the race for the entity’s National Assembly with 38.93 per cent of the vote, based on almost 87 per cent of counted ballots. The SNSD’s Savo Minic, Dodik’s close all who is currently the entity’s prime minister, also looks set to position of the president of Republika Srpska.

Dodik attributed part of the party’s success to what he described as a changed political environment in the United States. Amid intensive lobbying by the Bosnian Serbs, US sanctions against Dodik and SNSD allies imposed for corruption and secessionist activities have been dropped by the Trump administration.

“If there had not been Trump’s magnificent victory, we would probably be politically dead today, but thanks to the new environment, we are now political winners,” Dodik said. He also thanked Vladimir Putin, who had declared his support.

The SDA was leading the race for the House of Representatives of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, according to results from 93.48 per cent of polling stations. The SDA was on 30.58 per cent, the Social Democratic Party, SDP second on 15.39 per cent, with the coalition led by the HDZ BiH third with 13.61 per cent.

SDP leader Nermin Niksic said the party was satisfied with its performance, highlighting Becirovic’s win in the presidency race and Ivan Begic’s expected victory as vice-president of Republika Srpska, coming second behind Minic.

“It is not usual for governments to perform well in elections, but the SDP has received confirmation that it has a better electoral result, more votes and two individual positions – the candidate for the presidency and, as things stand now, the vice-president of Republika Srpska,” Niksic said.

He said the SDP expects to gain two or three additional seats in the Federation parliament compared with the 2022 elections. He also expects the party to retain its five seats in the state-level House of Representatives.

The CEC is expected to continue publishing updated preliminary results as ballots are processed.

Besides expected smaller issues with new election technologies, including biometric voter identification and ballot scanners, which were introduced for these polls, the voting process went off without major issues.

According to BIRN’s contacts at the Central Election Commission, over 80 per cent of the polling stations in the country filed election results in the first 15 minutes after polls closed.

World.title: Support for Young People in Croatia to Buy First Property Approved
World.content:
October the 6th, 2026 – 39 million euros in support measures have been approved for young people in Croatia to purchase their first property.

The Ministry of Physical Planning, Construction and State Property has announced that the Agency for Legal Transactions and Real Estate Brokerage (APN) received a total of 7,925 applications for tax refund on the purchase or construction of a first residential property by the 2nd of October 2026.

Poslovni reports that of the applications received, 6,561 have already been processed, 5,122 have been approved, 274 have been sent for additional documentation, while 1,165 applications have been rejected. Accordingly, a total payment of almost 39 million euros has been approved, while the average support per family amounts to 7,581 euros, the statement says.

This is a support measure intended for young citizens and families aimed at facilitating the resolution of the housing issue. The largest number of approved applications comes from the City of Zagreb (2,068), followed by Zagreb County (490), Split-Dalmatia County (487)… Among cities, Zagreb leads (2,068), followed by Split (282), Rijeka (214), Velika Gorica (167), Zadar (138), Osijek (131), Karlovac (101), Zaprešić (89), Solin (64), Varaždin (63), Slavonski Brod (61), Vinkovci (59), Pula (55), Samobor (54), Dugo Selo and Koprivnica (45), and Dubrovnik (42).

The average age of applicants is 32 years of age; the youngest are 18 and the oldest are 44 years of age. Regarding the size of the property, the average area is 72 square metres. The smallest property for which support was approved is located in Primorje-Gorski Kotar County and has 14 square metres, while the largest property by area, measuring 259 square metres, was recorded in Istria County. The average property price is 2,168 euros per square metre. The highest recorded price of 5,263 euros per square metre relates to a property in Dubrovnik-Neretva County, while the property with the lowest price, 83 euros per square metre, was purchased in Brod-Posavina County.

World.title: Incident at Split Airport: Air Serbia Plane Evacuated, Man Arrested
World.content:
October the 6th, 2026 – An unusual incident at Split Airport saw an Air Serbia plane bound for Belgrade evacuated and a man arrested.

Index reports that an incident occurred on an otherwise entirely normally scheduled Air Serbia aircraft that was due to take off for Belgrade yesterday afternoon. All passengers had to be evacuated on Monday afternoon at Split Airport due to a bomb threat. The police quickly arrived following the statement made by a man who then detained the passenger. The flight was scheduled for 15:20 but left only hours later.

Vinko Paić, one of the passengers on board the flight, described the bizarre situation on the aircraft. He said that several police officers entered the plane on the tarmac, some in uniform and some in civilian clothes. “Through the window I saw a police vehicle pull up next to the plane. They took out a grey-haired gentleman who was sitting in the 3rd or 4th row,” Paić explained. Since the passengers initially had absolutely no idea what was going on, Paić asked a flight attendant what it was about. She briefly replied: “He mentioned the word bomb.”

Paić added that several passengers left the aircraft of their own accord out of fear. Shortly afterwards, around 15:40, the pilot announced over the intercom that everyone had to leave for a security check of the aircraft. The police then thoroughly checked all of the passengers, all of their luggage and the entire aircraft. After no explosives were found, the aircraft was cleared for its flight from Split to Belgrade.

World.title: The 5 Things Croatian Island Residents Say Are Urgently Required
World.content:
October the 6th, 2026 – There are 5 things Croatian island residents say are urgently required in order for any real life to be consistently maintained on the country’s many islands.

High property prices, losing their maritime connection with their hometown during study periods, and having to travel to the mainland for every specialist examination are just some of the everyday challenges faced by young people on Croatian islands. Morski reports that more was revealed during a recently held online workshop called “Stay or leave? – young people and the future of the islands.” The workshop was held as part of the “Island Youth for Global Change” (IYGC) project, young islanders offered concrete solutions and agreed on five key measures that would enable them to live long-term on the islands.

The project was implemented by the Island Movement and LAG 5 within the GEAR UP! call, and the workshop participants focused on five key areas: housing, working conditions, higher education, healthcare, and social life outside the tourist season.

life outside of the summer season is needed

Outside of the boiling, tourism-fuelled summer months, social, sports and cultural activities on many islands almost completely die down. Young people emphasise that they are ready to organise activities themselves, but they lack basic infrastructure.

Solution: It is proposed that cities and municipalities issue public calls through which they would provide young people with premises, basic materials and initial support for establishing sports clubs or organising events, after which the young people would take over the running of the activities themselves.

co-financing the purchase of first properties

Property prices on Croatia’s many islands are largely unaffordable for the local population, which has been highlighted as one of the biggest obstacles to starting a family on the island.

Solution: Introduction of a model in which the local self-government co-finances the purchase of an apartment or house. In return, the buyer commits to long-term residence on the island. In the event of limited budget funds, priority would be given to shortage occupations.

equal treatment for both seasonal and domestic employees

Finding affordable accommodation for workers who stay on the island all year round is a major problem, and inequality in working conditions has also been pointed out. While foreign workers often receive free accommodation, food and utilities in addition to their salary, domestic workers are left without these benefits.

Solution: Construction or conversion of year-round staff accommodation facilities (staff houses) available to domestic workers. Alternatively, it is proposed that domestic workers be granted the right to equal benefits or to a cash allowance in the amount that the employer would otherwise allocate for their accommodation (e.g. around 200 euros per month).

making sure students can always reach home via ferry whatever the season

During four- or five-year studies on the mainland, young people’s connection with the island gradually weakens, which often results in permanent departure.

Solution: Co-financing of at least one trip home per month by the municipalities, as well as the establishment and financial support of island student associations in university cities (following the successful example of the Lošinj student association in Zagreb).

the need for specialist doctors on the islands

Travelling to the mainland for routine or specialist examinations entails a large financial and time cost for island families.

Solution: Organisation of visits by specialist doctors to the island once or twice a month, according to a pre-determined schedule, which would raise primary healthcare to a significantly higher level.

World.title: Hotel Atrium in Split Undergoes Impressive Transformation
World.content:
October the 6th, 2026 – Hotel Atrium in Split has undergone an impressive transformation with a team of experienced experts at the helm.

The five-star Hotel Atrium in Split has been given a new face after the first major investment in interior design and furnishing since its opening. Poslovni reports that the hotel’s newly refreshed spaces, carefully selected materials and new equipment are part of a strategic investment with which the hotel is raising the quality of the stay and further developing its offer for business guests and wellness lovers.

Behind the investment stands Plavi Safir d.o.o., the parent company within which, in addition to Atrium, Amphora and Amphora’s Garden also operate. The three hotels operate under the common brand Safir Hotels, the largest hotel group in Split with its own management at all levels. The investment in Atrium continues the development of the group, whose properties play an important role in the city’s hotel offer.

The new design was a collaboration between designer Maja Buljan from the studio LUMAR design and Cult, a Split-based group with experience in furnishing numerous Croatian hotels. Cult took over the complete furnishing of the bathrooms, the supply and installation of cladding, and the cladding of the fireplace in the lobby. Its team was involved in the project development, proposing materials and seeking implementation solutions together with the designer.

“In the Atrium hotel renovation project I was responsible for the interior design of all 129 rooms with their associated bathrooms, as well as common areas such as the lobby, reception, bar, pastry shop, restaurant and wellness. My goal was for the interior to have character and recognisability, but at the same time not to impose itself on the guest, rather to calm them and provide a sense of luxury that is primarily felt and only then seen,” designer Buljan emphasised.

“By investing in the furnishing of Hotel Atrium we are raising the quality of the offer and strengthening its competitiveness. Our goal is to achieve the special ‘Meetings’ and ‘Health and Fitness’ standards and to further develop congress and wellness facilities. In this way we will better respond to the needs of business guests, event organisers and guests seeking rest and recreation. We want to attract a wider circle of guests and offer them more reasons to come to Split throughout the year,” says Bruno Nizić, executive director of the Safir Hotels group.

How extensive the project was is also shown by the quantities of materials installed. Approximately 4,550 square metres of Laminam cladding were used for Atrium, of which around 3,800 square metres were large-format slabs and an additional 750 square metres of smaller dimensions. Berry Alloc floor coverings were installed in the rooms, while special attention was paid to the bathrooms, where the guest comes into contact with almost every selected element on a daily basis.

Approximately 230 Laufen washbasins were installed along with Hansgrohe showers and mixers, Quare shower trays, Relax shower cabins and Etrusca bathroom mirrors. The selection was accompanied by the demanding work of coordinating delivery, installation and finishing details.

It is precisely here, they explain at Cult, that the experience of working on hotel projects comes to the fore. In addition to the appearance of the space, it is necessary to think in good time about its functionality, maintenance and intensive everyday use.

“Our work begins with understanding what the investor and the designer want to achieve. In a hotel one must think in advance about functionality, maintenance, durability and the method of installation of every element. Experience from previous projects enables us to anticipate possible difficulties and propose solutions while it is still easy to adapt them. At Atrium we were constantly by the designer’s side, jointly developing the details and monitoring their implementation. It is precisely in this collaboration that our knowledge and experience gain concrete value,” says Željko Tukić, head of the Cult group, who also took this opportunity to thank Ivana Šuto, member of the management board of Safir Hotels, for the trust placed in them for one of the most significant projects in Split’s hospitality industry.

Cult, in addition to supplying premium materials, specialises in design, supervision and installation. Its offer includes more than a hundred European brands, including a number that it represents exclusively. The selection covers bathroom equipment, floor and wall coverings, pools, wellness zones, radiators, doors and designer furniture, and investors have access to expert support in aligning them with the project, budget and implementation requirements.

Atrium thus joins Cult’s portfolio, which includes AC Hotel Split by Marriott, Hotel Ambasador, The Isolano Autograph Collection by Marriott, Molum Hotel & Residences and Hotel Sumratin. Among its references are also Mövenpick Hotel & Residences Kvarner Bay, the Amfora and Sirena hotels on Hvar, and properties from the Valamar and Bluesun groups, along with a number of luxury villas and tourism investments. Working on different hotel concepts has enabled Cult to develop the knowledge needed for demanding projects, from the initial selection of materials to their final application.

World.title: Bilić and Modrić Face the Press Ahead of Croatia-Spain at Poljud
World.content:
Croatia close out a bruising run of four Nations League matches in 11 days on Tuesday night, when world champions Spain visit Poljud for a 20:45 kick-off. Head coach Slaven Bilić and captain Luka Modrić faced the media in Split on Monday.

The campaign began well. Croatia won 2-1 away to the Czech Republic on September 26th, but what followed has shaken the national team. Spain won 4-1 in Seville three days later, and on Saturday England won 7-0 in Rijeka, a historic defeat for which Bilić apologized to the nation. Croatia have now conceded 12 goals in three matches, the second-worst defensive record in the competition, and sit on three points in League A Group 3.

Two group matches remain in November, but Tuesday carries a weight of its own. Speculation has grown in the Croatian media that Bilić, only four competitive matches into his second spell in charge, could step down if his side fails to beat Spain.

Spain held their final training session at Las Rozas, outside Madrid, on Monday before flying to Split with a 24-man squad. Luis de la Fuente will be without three players at Poljud: midfielder Fabián Ruiz, who is in Paris for the birth of his son, and injured forwards Nico Williams and Ferran Torres.

The absences have done little to dent the mood. Spain lead Group A3 with a maximum nine points after beating England 3-2, Croatia 4-1 and Czechia 3-1, and the Spanish federation said the team wants to close this opening stretch of the season with a 100 percent record.

Those wins extended Spain’s unbeaten run to 41 matches over 90 minutes or extra time. Their only setback in that period came in the 2025 Nations League final, which Portugal won on penalties.

De la Fuente and Dani Olmo, the Barcelona attacking midfielder and former Dinamo Zagreb player, will address the media in Split on Monday evening. In Spain, the debate is whether 19-year-old winger Lamine Yamal will start. He scored in the second minute against both England and Croatia, and in the fifth against the Czech Republic.

Captain Luka Modrić was first to take questions, and was asked whether the squad had talked through Saturday’s defeat to England.

“We spoke, of course. We couldn’t pretend that nothing had happened,” Modrić said. “When something like this happens, you have to talk about it and look at what went wrong. Whatever was said will stay between us.

Of course we have more in us, and tomorrow we will show a very different Croatia for the fans, who deserve it. Tomorrow we will be completely different in every aspect of the game.”

“In football, as in life, you don’t have time to dwell. You have to move forward,” he said. “We have been in this position before. We lost 6-0 to Spain right after finishing second in the world. And what happened after that? We came out of it and figured things out. We will again.”

That defeat came in Elche in September 2018, two months after Croatia reached the World Cup final. They beat Spain 3-2 in Zagreb in the return fixture that November.

Modrić was then asked what the Split crowd can expect on Tuesday.

“Losing is not the problem. The problem is the way we lose. The way we lost against England was nothing to be proud of. We expect a positive reaction from the crowd and their support, as always. After the game, they can judge us. But we need the fans tomorrow.

We always talk about how much their support means to us. Of course we upset everyone, but nobody is hurting more than we are over what happened the other day. We are hoping for a positive crowd, and I believe we will be completely different tomorrow.”

Asked where he sees the room for improvement, Modrić pointed to the basics.

“In our togetherness, in the fight. That is where we need to fix the most as a team. Against the best team in the world, all of that has to change: the aggression and everything else. If we give Spain too much space, it is very tough to play that way. All of those things need to change, and I believe they will.”

Modrić, 41, was also asked about his own future with the national team.

“There is no greater pride than playing for Croatia and being with these boys. I still don’t know when I will retire. We will see. I am still enjoying it, which is the most important thing. It could be a month, three months, and so on. Right now, I am not thinking about that.”

Bilić spoke next and began with Saturday’s defeat.

“Nothing has changed in my mind about what happened two days ago. It was the worst defeat in our history, and that will stay written forever,” he said. “These are not games you forget. You have to remember them always, so that they don’t repeat themselves.

The one good thing is that when things get this bad, you have to react. There is no room to play around. There has to be a reaction.

On one hand, this is the toughest game imaginable for us. On the other, it is the best possible situation: the stadium, the atmosphere, the chance for the players to turn all of this around. I hope we will win; I believe we will win, but we need to show everything we did not have against England.

I am disappointed and upset that we came out the way we did against England, a team we knew could walk all over us. That is why I am angry,” Bilić said. “We always have to give our maximum in focus, concentration and quality. We have to play and give everything tomorrow. We know the opponent. But we know who we are.”

Asked about possible changes to the line-up, Bilić said nothing had been decided.

“We started the Nations League with a goal. We want to secure at least third place, and of course get a result against these teams,” he said. “Some players are not getting as many minutes at their clubs, and we have to be careful with that.

For tomorrow, the last game of this little cycle, we will see. We will see how training goes today and then think about the starting eleven. Everyone is available. We will do a light session today, and then see.”

Bilić, a Split native who played for and later coached Hajduk, was asked how it feels to be back at Poljud.

“It is my home. Of course I am happy to be here. It means everything. I am five minutes from home, at the club that gave me everything. There is nothing better. How could there be?

I had a plan ahead of the Nations League. The result is key, the most important thing,” Bilić said. “But the goal is the Euros, a good qualifying campaign, and seeing how we can become the best national team in the world. I can only find that out by us playing games. That was my plan. We are still third in the group. We have another game tomorrow, and at the end of all this we could still finish second.”

Croatia and Spain meet tomorrow at 20:45. Poljud is sold out.

World.title: Croatia Ranks 3rd in EU for Renewable Energy
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Croatia has ranked an impressive 3rd in the EU for its renewable energy, with solar energy being the most important source in 2026’s second quarter.

Renewable energy sources produced more than half of the electricity in the European Union in the second quarter of 2026. Marin Penavic reports for Poslovni that according to Eurostat data, their share in total production reached 54.1 percent, which is still slightly less than in the same period last year, when it stood at 54.3 percent.

Differences among EU Member States are very pronounced, at the top is Latvia, where as much as 97.7 percent of the electricity produced came from renewable sources. Denmark follows with a share of 94.3 percent, while Croatia ranks third with 92.2 percent. In Latvia the largest contribution comes from hydro power and solar, in Denmark wind energy dominates, while Croatia’s result relies primarily on hydro power plants.

Infographic shows the ten European Union Member States with the highest share of electricity produced from renewable sources in total electricity produced. At the top are Latvia with 97.7 percent of electricity, Denmark with 94.3 percent and Croatia with 92.2 percent. At the bottom of the list is Germany with 63.8 percent.

Among the countries with the highest shares of renewable electricity are also Austria, Estonia, Portugal and Lithuania, which means that countries with large hydro power potential, but also those that have strongly developed wind farms and solar energy, particularly stand out at the top of the European ranking. At the level of the entire EU, solar energy was the most important renewable source in the second quarter, with 41.6 percent of total renewable production. It was followed by wind with 27.7 percent and hydro power with 22.6 percent, while other renewable sources had a significantly smaller share.

At the same time, the data show that the transition towards renewable sources is not equally fast in all parts of the Union. While in Latvia their share almost reached 100 percent, at the bottom are Slovakia with 19.8 percent, Czechia with 20.9 percent and Malta with 24.5 percent. Eurostat notes that this indicator refers to the share of renewable sources in net electricity production and should not be equated with the share of renewable energy in gross final consumption, which is calculated according to a different methodology.

World.title: Dubrovnik Nominated for the Title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Dubrovnik, once known as the unfortunate poster child of mass tourism, has now been nominated for the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination.

After being named the world’s best sustainable destination back in 2025, Dubrovnik has once again been nominated this year for the prestigious title of “World’s Leading Sustainable Destination 2026” as part of the World Sustainable Travel & Hospitality Awards. Morski reports that voting is open until the 21st of October, and Dubrovnik is competing for the title against four other world destinations.

The new nomination represents a continuation of the international recognition of the City of Dubrovnik’s long-standing activities aimed at responsible and sustainable tourism management, the preservation of cultural and historical heritage, the protection of the natural environment, and the quality of life of the local population.

In 2025, Dubrovnik won the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination, with particular emphasis in the justification on the Respect the City initiative, launched back in 2017 as a strategic and multidisciplinary model of destination management.

Among the measures recognised at the time were the application of new technologies in visitor management, an artificial intelligence-based system for predicting visitor numbers, the Dubrovnik Pass, coordination of cruise ship arrivals and a reservation system for tourist buses, as well as other projects that align tourism development with the needs of the local community and the protection of valuable heritage. The results of this approach are also visible through the assessment according to the criteria of the Global Sustainable Tourism Council (GSTC), according to which Dubrovnik increased its score from 70 percent in 2019 to 86.04 percent in 2023.

Competing with Dubrovnik for the title of World’s Leading Sustainable Destination 2026 are Diriyah – The City of Earth, Dubai, the Maldives, and Serengeti National Park. Voting has been open from the 25th of September and will remain open until the 21st of October 2026. Representatives of the tourism and hospitality sector, the media, and the general public can participate. Votes from verified professionals in the tourism and hospitality industry carry double the value of public votes.

You can support Dubrovnik here.

The World Sustainable Travel & Hospitality Awards (WSTHA) is otherwise a global awards programme launched at COP28 in Dubai with the aim of recognising and showcasing individuals, organisations, destinations and initiatives that make a significant contribution to the sustainable development of tourism and hospitality. WSTHA is a sister programme of the World Travel Awards, an international tourism awards programme established in 1993, and 2026 marks its third annual edition.

The categories and criteria of the programme are guided by an international Advisory Board composed of experts, representatives of the academic community and leading institutions in the field of sustainable tourism. The programme is based on the principles of the UN Sustainable Development Goals and an approach that encompasses people, planet, place, prosperity and partnerships, with the aim of recognising concrete solutions, innovations and measurable progress towards more sustainable tourism.

World.title: Croatia Has a New Football Stadium That is Unique in the World
World.content:
October the 5th, 2026 – Croatia now has a brand new football stadium that is entirely unique in the world and boasts a million dollar view.

While spears are currently being broken over the issues with the new stadium at Maksimir, plans are being forged for the new so-called Poljud beauty and Kranjčevićeva is almost finished. Zvonimir Varga reports for Poslovni that Croatia is however home to a non-controversial new football stadium getting much less attention. It has sprung up on the sunny Kvarner coastline and will certainly attract plenty of attention with its appearance, particularly with its impressive view.

On Friday evening, along the main road that runs through Rijeka and Opatija, the new stadium of NK Opatija was officially opened with a match against the first-division side from Rujevica. Built on the site of the old one, it has become a modern complex constructed according to the infrastructural criteria of the Croatian Football Federation (HNS) for the second Croatian football league in which NK Opatija competes.

The new stadium has 802 seated places, separate stands for home and away fans, auxiliary facilities and a completely new artificial surface with the highest FIFA certificate. In addition to the main pitch there is also a smaller auxiliary pitch and a warm-up area. The main building houses new changing rooms, rooms for coaches and referees, a first-aid and doping-control room, an indoor training hall, storage rooms, a VIP area, catering facilities and a fan shop.

But what captures attention at first glance is the location of the stadium — more precisely the view that opens from the central stand onto the open sea, with the city of Rijeka on the left. Although this is a smaller stadium, there are not many stadiums in Europe, or even in the world, that offer such a view of the sea.

In Croatia the only comparable ones are Poljud, from which the sea is only partially visible, and Kantrida, where professional matches have not been played for a long time. In Europe there is the legendary Estadio Riazor of Spanish Deportivo, Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo in Venice, Stade Louis II in Monaco, and Henningsvær Idrettslag Stadion in Norway (without stands but surrounded by sea and mountains). Around the world, there are similar stadiums in Japan, Australia and South Africa. There are certainly more, but we are not sure whether any can match the ‘million-dollar view’ from the new Opatija stadium.

It should be emphasised that works on the renovation of the Opatija stadium began at the end of 2024, after the contract was signed with the contractor GP Krk. The total value of the project stands at a whopping 6.5 million euros. The project was realised through the city company Opatija 21, and financing was secured with credit funds from HBOR and Zagrebačka banka, with financial support from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport.

We all well remember the bronze medal from Russia and the silver from Qatar 2022, when it was said that the time was right for building new stadiums. We also remember the photo opportunities of the then football officials back in 2014 at Zagreb’s Svetice with shovels that were never put into the ground. Fortunately for all sports lovers, Croatian football today has some new people and initiatives, so we can be proud of Opus Arena in Osijek, the upcoming stadiums at Kranjčevićeva and Maksimir, the announced renovation of Poljud, and now also this small but distinctive new stadium in Opatija.

World.title: Iraq welcomed record 10 million tourists in 2025
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq welcomed approximately 10 million international tourists throughout 2025, marking an unprecedented modern benchmark for the country’s travel sector, according to official figures disclosed on Monday, October 5, 2026, by Fadhil Al-Badrani, Undersecretary of the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities.

The influx, which encompasses both religious pilgrims and cultural heritage travelers, underscores the country’s growing appeal as regional connectivity expands. Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Badrani detailed the institutional mechanisms governing inbound traveler verification.

He explained that entry data is tracked through an integrated federal reporting apparatus linking the National Data Center, the Ministry of Interior, the Border Ports Commission, and international civil airports across Baghdad, Najaf, Basra, and Erbil.

These inter-agency registries are channeled directly to the Tourism Commission and the Ministry of Culture to compile precise statutory records.

Al-Badrani acknowledged that international tourism flows during 2026 experienced an unavoidable slowdown, driven by regional security volatility and logistical strains that dampened cross-border leisure travel across the Middle East.

However, he contrasted current headwinds with the record-setting performance of 2025, where sustained domestic stability and streamlined entry visas facilitated massive arrivals.

The 10-million visitor total was primarily anchored by Iraq’s religious tourism corridors—chiefly major annual pilgrimages to holy shrines in Karbala, Najaf, Kadhimiya, and Samarra—supplemented by an expanding cohort of international visitors touring Mesopotamian archaeological landmarks, including Babylon, Ur, Hatra, and the UNESCO-listed Iraqi Marshlands.

Al-Badrani emphasized that surpassing 10 million arrivals represents a milestone compared to previous decades, demonstrating the tourism industry’s capacity to serve as a vital pillar for economic diversification and sovereign non-oil revenue generation.

World.title: Iraq considers raising official dollar rate to 1,500 IQD and dropping currency zeros
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Safaa Al-Jabri, member of parliament for the Al-Sadiqoun bloc and member of the Parliamentary Economic Committee, revealed that the federal government is reviewing a proposal to adjust Iraq’s official exchange rate from 1,310 dinars to 1,500 dinars per U.S. dollar, while advancing high-level deliberations to redenominate the national currency and potentially remove zeros.

Speaking in a televised interview, Al-Jabri projected that sovereign state revenues for the 2027 federal budget will surpass $110 billion, declaring that Iraq has successfully weathered the acute economic fallout triggered by past disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz and Basra export halts.

According to Al-Jabri, fiscal parameters for the upcoming national budget are being restructured on the back of rising non-oil customs and tax receipts, an unprecedented $8 billion to $10 billion generated from domestic petroleum sales, and projected crude oil export earnings exceeding $85 billion.

He noted that Iraqi crude sales currently benchmark around $80 to $82 per barrel, generating approximately $5 billion in monthly export revenues, providing budgetary headroom as trade bottlenecks and logistics gradually normalize.

Regarding currency and fiscal policy, Al-Jabri highlighted key government plans:

Official Exchange Rate Revision: Leaked preliminary drafts of the federal budget proposal—which carries a planned deficit between 25 and 30 trillion dinars—contain a formal submission from the Minister of Finance proposing to adjust the official statutory exchange rate to 150,000 dinars per $100 (1,500 IQD per USD). Al-Jabri noted that no binding cabinet decision has been finalized to date.

Currency Redenomination: Serious technical discussions are underway between the Prime Minister’s Office and the Central Bank of Iraq regarding currency redesign and the removal of three zeros. The measure is currently stalled only by legal jurisdictional reviews to identify the specific governing authority legally empowered to greenlight and execute the structural transition.

Critique of Past Budget Frameworks: Al-Jabri criticized previous administrations for populist fiscal practices, claiming that state budgets were prepared through rote copy-paste mechanisms for nearly twenty years under former Finance Minister Taif Sami, who had risen through the ministry ranks from director general of budget to minister.

Public Liabilities & Contract Terminations: The lawmaker highlighted structural financial arrears inherited by the treasury, including outstanding wheat procurement payouts owed to local farmers, unpaid rationing supply dues claimed by Al-Owais Company across 2025 and 2026, and 33 billion dinars in overdue liabilities tied to road and bridge construction. In response, Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi has canceled legacy public work contracts where execution progress remained below 20 percent.

The potential devaluation of the official dinar to 1,500 IQD per dollar represents an effort to narrow the spread with the parallel currency market—which recently traded above 160,000 dinars per $100—while curbing the planned fiscal deficit for the 2027 fiscal cycle.

World.title: Asian stocks mixed despite tech-led Wall St record
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks were mixed Tuesday as a tech-led record on Wall Street was tempered by ongoing worries about a spike in government borrowing costs.

Oil held most of the losses seen in response to a G7 release of stockpiles, Saudi Arabia’s price cut and a pick-up in Gulf exports to pre-war levels, though supply fears are keeping global benchmark Brent above $100 a barrel.

The US Nasdaq closed at a fresh peak thanks to rallies in tech giants including Nvidia, SpaceX and Meta, though observers pointed out that the market gains were increasingly concentrated on a few stocks.

Asia struggled to match the positive energy on Wall Street, where the Dow and S&P 500 also ended higher.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Jakarta and Wellington rose, but Seoul, Singapore, Taipei and Manila edged down. Shanghai was closed for a holiday.

The tepid performance comes amid long-running uncertainty among traders over the Middle East crisis, which has fanned energy costs and in turn pushed inflation higher — putting pressure on central banks to hike interest rates.

This has pushed government bond yields up to levels not seen for decades.

Analysts have pointed out that the race to build out AI data centres, servers and chips has compounded that problem, with tech titans no longer able to rely on their vast piles of cash.

Borrowing by firms including Google, Amazon and Microsoft hit around $500 billion in the nine months since January, and Goldman Sachs expects a further ramp-up in 2027, to $1.2 trillion.

“This is not something that we’ve seen before,” said Chris Della Fave, senior vice president at fundraising advisory firm Post Oak Group, who estimates that AI now accounts for 25 percent of all corporate bond issuance — up from 4 percent two years ago.

Oil prices inched up following Monday’s drop of almost two percent, though Saudi Aramco’s chief executive Amin Nasser, speaking after the G7 release, warned over global stockpiles.

“The system is already straining,” he told the Energy Intelligence Forum in London.

“And with precious little else the world can turn to, the supply resilience cushion is scarily thin.”

Middle East oil exports, excluding Iran, surpassed their pre-war levels last week despite attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, according to data from the maritime tracking firm Kpler.

But Nasser warned Monday against looking at headline figures for reserves, noting that “less than 10 percent” were available.

And FOREX.com’s Fiona Cincotta said: “Tensions in the Middle East remain elevated, with several vessels coming under attack around the coast of Oman and Yemen.

“This could limit the downside in oil prices, particularly if disruptions to shipping or regional supply intensify.

“The key question is whether improving crude supply can outweigh the geopolitical risk premium and keep oil prices under control. A sustained decline in energy prices would ease some of the inflation pressure currently complicating the outlook for central banks.”

World.title: AI borrowing binge rattles US markets
World.content:
New York – The world’s richest companies can no longer rely on their massive cash piles alone to stay in the artificial intelligence race and have suddenly started borrowing massively in a shift that is sending repercussions across the world.

Rising US interest rates, including on the Treasury bonds that anchor the global economy, are sending tremors through the financial world, and some analysts point to the AI borrowing bonanza as one of the culprits.

From next to nothing in 2024, tech sector borrowing has reached around $500 billion in the nine months since January, as Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and others raise debt hand over fist to finance the chips, servers and data centers that power AI.

Goldman Sachs expects a further ramp-up in 2027, to $1.2 trillion.

“This is not something that we’ve seen before,” said Chris Della Fave, senior vice president at fundraising advisory firm Post Oak Group, who estimates that AI now accounts for 25 percent of all corporate bond issuance, up from 4 percent two years ago.

In inflation-adjusted terms, the AI sector is expected to borrow more this year than US cable operators did to build out the entire internet, or than railroad companies did during the 19th-century US rail boom.

So far, investors have eagerly snapped up the chance to lend to the tech giants, but they have demanded returns that would have been unthinkable for such blue-chip companies not long ago.

Even Meta has had to offer more than 7 percent a year, while riskier cloud data center specialists have gone above 9 percent.

The impact reaches well beyond the companies building AI — their debt is even starting to crowd out demand for the US government bonds that anchor the financial system.

An investor who might otherwise buy a US Treasury bond “might decide to buy Microsoft” instead, said Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial, referring to the tech giant’s bonds.

That shift pushes up the rates Washington pays to borrow, he explained.

This adds to the other force driving up US borrowing costs: inflation, fueled by the war against Iran and high energy prices.

The interest rate on 10-year US government bonds — Wall Street’s benchmark and widely seen as the most important number in global finance, setting the tone for everything from mortgages to car loans — is now above 5.30 percent, its highest level since 2002.

– ‘Sharper correction’ –

Adding to the volatility, hedge funds had piled into US government bonds like never before, holding 7 percent of all those in circulation at the end of 2025, though that share has since fallen.

Hedge funds, which place big bets on markets, move their money far faster than more cautious investors such as insurers and pension funds.

Even if the war and the oil situation stabilized, Della Fave said, “I wouldn’t expect the yields to dramatically reduce, to be honest, because of this influence of the AI debt situation.”

Beyond the rising cost of borrowing, some are questioning the risks of betting on an AI boom that could hit a wall, as the dot-com bubble did in 2000.

Even a moderate slowdown in the frenzied pace of construction, delays on certain projects or weaker-than-expected revenue growth could trigger a shock in financial markets, Malek warned.

In late September, the Bank of England’s Financial Policy Committee warned that “the risk of a sharper correction persists,” particularly if concerns about the pace of AI development or adoption hit earnings expectations.

In July, amid some second-guessing about the AI boom, the tech-heavy Nasdaq index fell nearly 7 percent.

Against this backdrop, cloud specialist Oracle is sometimes seen as a bellwether.

With massive debt ($125 billion), cash reserves that shrink every quarter and a possible delay on a huge data center project in New Mexico, several warning lights are flashing for Larry Ellison’s group.

“Let’s say Oracle has a problem… They can’t pay for something,” Malek said. Trouble with its debt “could trigger contagion” across AI finance as a whole, he added.

World.title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send-off
World.content:
Buenos Aires – Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions.

After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain’s armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina’s emerging generation.

The friendly marks a symbolic passing of the torch for a player whose international legacy includes a World Cup title, two Copa America crowns and the Finalissima.

Messi also bows out as Argentina’s record appearance-maker and leading scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.

His farewell comes two and a half months after Argentina’s ill-tempered World Cup final defeat to Spain in New Jersey, where Messi exited in tears after making little impression.

“I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance,” Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

– Friends reunited –

Members of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad — the players who delivered the country’s third star — and their families will join Messi for Tuesday’s farewell against Benin, ranked 93rd in the world.

Veterans of that Doha triumph such as Angel Di María, who retired from international football in 2024, will be there to witness the passing of the torch to a new generation charged with extending the Albiceleste’s golden era.

Several of the newcomers, including Franco Mastantuono and Leonel Flores, were not even born when “La Pulga” (“The Flea”) made his Argentina debut in 2005 for a team whose history had for so long been dominated by Diego Maradona.

“It’s going to be an unforgettable day for everyone. Everyone wants to be at this match, and now it’s just about enjoying it,” Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said.

Argentina’s new generation has already shown what it can do without its captain, although nobody is pretending replacing a man regarded by many as the greatest footballer in history will be straightforward.

“Collectively, we will try to fill the void left by Leo,” said Scaloni, who is negotiating a contract extension after leaving his future unresolved following the World Cup defeat in July.

Scaloni, who mastered the art of building the right supporting cast around Messi, will also say goodbye on Tuesday to 38-year-old vice-captain Nicolas Otamendi.

Like Messi and Otamendi, midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Giovani Lo Celso were called up solely for the Benin game, raising the possibility that neither will represent Argentina again.

– New generation –

Those certain to be involved, at least from the bench, include other veterans of the 2022 World Cup who will be the standard-bearers for Argentina after Messi: defender Cristian Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez, and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.

Tenacious centre-back Romero is set to inherit the captain’s armband, first worn by Messi at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez and Lautaro Martinez are next in the captaincy hierarchy.

They have already begun to rally around Messi’s heirs, who showed their appetite for success in Argentina’s first game since the World Cup final, against Bolivia in Cordoba on Wednesday.

Argentina swept the Bolivians aside 4-0, with young talents Nico Paz and Jose Manuel Lopez among the scorers.

They followed that victory with a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso at the Monumental on Saturday, with Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni scoring their first international goals.

While Argentina’s future is beginning to take shape, one small but symbolically significant question remains: who inherits Messi’s number 10 shirt?

“We won’t give the number 10 to anyone until Leo’s match takes place,” Scaloni said. “After that, we’ll see.”

World.title: Russia downplays plague reports as Trump offers US help
World.content:
Moscow – Russia on Monday sought to downplay reports that a laboratory technician had died of plague, even as President Donald Trump said Washington was closely monitoring the situation and offered US help.

Reports on Friday that pneumonic plague had killed a 28-year-old woman named Darya Shipilova, who had been working for the anti-plague institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, sparked alarm.

“We’re looking at it very strongly, we just heard about it,” Trump told reporters at the White House when asked what Washington was going to do about the risk of plague coming from Russia.

“We’ll help them, we’ll help them as much as we can.”

The Russian news outlet People of Baikal, citing unnamed sources close to the regional security services, said the dead woman may have contracted pneumonic plague from a broken test tube.

Other media reported a possible link between her death and a lab accident at the facility.

As many as 200 people with whom she may have had contact were under quarantine, the People of Baikal outlet added, without elaborating.

But Russian officials stressed that postmortem tests had not detected the disease.

Irkutsk Regional Governor Igor Kobzev said Monday that a special expert commission inspection in the region had found that “the cause of death was pneumonia of undetermined aetiology”.

He said on Telegram that Russia’s consumer and health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor had determined, following tests, that “no microorganisms linked to the young woman’s professional work were found in her biological samples”.

He added that there had been “no new cases of staff from the anti-plague institute seeking medical attention” since the woman’s death.

Kobzev said the sanitary-epidemiological situation in Irkutsk was “stable”.

“The situation remains under our control and that of the experts.”

– ‘Rumours and speculations’ –

Asked about the situation on Monday, Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters to “rely on Rospotrebnadzor’s official statements rather than… rumours and speculations”.

Plague is a bacterial disease that can occur in several forms, including pneumonic plague, which is the most contagious type and can be transmitted by respiratory means. Bubonic plague is transmitted by infected fleas.

Pneumonic plague can be fatal if not treated early, according to the World Health Organization.

The reports will be closely watched in Washington, where memories of the Covid-19 pandemic that started in Trump’s first term are still fresh.

Trump has strongly backed the theory that the disease was due to a leak from a laboratory in Wuhan, China.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said his country was monitoring the Russia situation but saw no “cause for alarm”.

“There’s very limited travel between the US and Russia, obviously, but like anything else, something like that gets out, it could quickly spread,” Rubio told reporters before taking off for a visit to Iceland.

“So we’re watching and monitoring it closely. I don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause to just keep an eye on it. And we’re doing that.”

Experts said the reported response in Russia appeared “proportionate”.

“It appears that measures are being implemented to quarantine any potential contacts and prevent any onward transmission,” Malick Gibani, clinical associate professor in bacterial vaccinology, Imperial College London, said in a commentary.

World.title: Brazilian stocks surge to record after Bolsonaro election lead
World.content:
Brasília – Brazilian stocks surged to record highs Monday, with Sao Paulo’s main index up almost nine percent by midday, after a surprise first-round election result saw right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro edge past incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

The Ibovespa index hit a record high of almost 210,000 points after Sunday’s presidential election, which heads to a run-off in three weeks.

Flavio Bolsonaro secured 47 percent of the vote, ahead of leftist Lula’s 45 percent. Lula now faces a tough path to a fourth term in office in the October 25 run-off election.

The son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro has promised fiscal austerity in the face of rising public debt and a smaller state.

Investors see Bolsonaro as “more aligned with Brazil’s economic and fiscal needs,” Jerson Zanlorenzi, head of the equities and derivatives desk at BTG Pactual, told AFP.

Stocks “have been heavily discounted in Brazil over the past four or five years, mainly because of the dynamics of high interest rates here, as well as the prospect of low foreign investment,” he said.

“Brazilian equities were already very cheap and almost nobody had a position,” Zanlorenzi said.

Investors also reacted to Bolsonaro’s party making sweeping gains in Congress, indicating that a victory in the run-off would give him “the necessary quorum to pass the major reforms Brazil needs.”

Some stocks surged 20 percent, with further room for gains as share prices have lagged behind corporate earnings, he said.

Brazil’s currency, the real, also strengthened against the dollar.

During Lula’s third term in office, inflation has come under control and unemployment fell to historic lows.

However, Brazilians complain about a loss of purchasing power and authorities are concerned about rising household debt.

At 13.75 percent, Brazil has some of the highest interest rates in the world, which has been a frequent complaint by Lula.

Inflation eased to 4.44 percent year-on-year in July, according to Brazil’s IBGE statistics agency, within the government’s target range.

World.title: ‘Reckless’ AI firms can’t control models, says whistleblower
World.content:
New York – Leading artificial intelligence companies do not know how to keep AI systems from pursuing objectives their developers did not assign, whistleblower Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI and Anthropic employee, warned Monday.

“Companies are being extremely reckless given the stakes,” Coxon told local lawmakers at a hearing before the New York City Council.

In early September, the British researcher published a statement on X explaining his decision to resign from Anthropic, saying AI developers sincerely believed the technology could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”

His testimony made headlines around the world, and several current and former employees of AI’s major players have since voiced similar concerns.

While AI could bring “tremendous benefits” to society, “on the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control of these AIs and could end in human extinction,” he said Monday.

“We don’t know how to prevent them from developing goals of their own,” beyond their creators’ control, Coxon explained, “and we don’t have the safeguards to prevent them from acting on these goals.”

The Cambridge University graduate took aim at tech industry culture, saying companies “run on a startup mindset: move fast, break things, fix them later.”

“That works for a photo sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever,” Coxon said.

“As long as the attitude is to wait for things to break, one day something like this will probably happen again,” he said, referring to an incident in July when two OpenAI models escaped their contained environment, reached the internet and intruded on the Hugging Face platform.

“Except the AIs will be much more capable,” he added.

“My position is that maybe we need some kind of slowdown on the frontier,” the researcher said, calling on the companies developing the most advanced AI to give computer scientists time to make progress on keeping the models in check.

Addressing a press conference, additional deputy commissioner of Police (New Delhi) Manjeet said Nadeem admitted during questioning that he used AI tools to create such videos.

It is being portrayed that an individual in Police uniform is misbehaving with a woman. Through social media, the identity of the officer is being revealed. When we examined it, we found that one Nadeem Ahmed, a r/o Palwal, Haryana was running that channel. We arrested him. In the initial questioning, he told us that he is an independent journalist.

He told us that he had studied till class 10 in Madrasa of Saket, Delhi,â police said.





âHe also told us that he is a 10th-fail. Upon further questioning, he told us that he has AI tools, with the help of which he keeps making such videos. When we asked him why he made such videos, he told us that he wanted to tarnish the image of Police so that the protesters coming there would start harbouring hatred for the Police and start attacking them. We took immediate cognisance of this and arrested him. We will take him into police remand and further question him.

His source of funding and accomplices are matters of investigation. We have seized his phone for further analysis. He became more active during CJP protest. So, we will analyse if this is part of any bigger conspiracy...â police added.

Police are also investigating whether others were involved in the alleged conspiracy and are working to identify them.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar has called the United Nations âlargely irrelevantâ to decision-making on major global crises, blaming a âgridlockedâ Security Council and its outdated composition for the organisationâs ineffectiveness.Speaking at the fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Monday, Jaishankar said the UN had struggled to play a meaningful role in addressing major international issues, including conflicts in the Gulf and Ukraine, crises in Africa and the Covid-19 pandemic.âWhere the UN is concerned, I think it's obvious to everybody by now that the UN is gridlocked,â Jaishankar said.âIf you look at the big issues of the day... actually, the United Nations has been largely irrelevant to the decision-making,â he added.Jaishankar said much of the problem stemmed from the Security Councilâs inability to reach decisions. He also questioned whether its current composition reflected the wider international community.The UN was founded with 51 members and now has almost four times that number, he noted.âSo, if you have grown four times, and you want to keep the old board of management, it's not going to work. I mean, it's common sense,â he said.Jaishankar also criticised countries that he said were resisting UN reform while citing Africaâs interests as a reason.He said Africa had already presented a clear position during intergovernmental negotiations on what it wanted from reform of the world body.Despite his criticism, Jaishankar said the answer was not to bypass the UN.âWe need the UN. The UN has done a big service to the international community,â he said.âOur job must be to âfix the UN, not to work around the UNâ,â he added, saying the UN itself needed to contribute to the reform process.India has been pushing for comprehensive UN reforms, including expansion of the Security Council. It has worked with the G4 grouping of India, Japan, Brazil and Germany, as well as the L.69 group of developing countries, to build support for reform.Jaishankar has previously criticised the UNâs structure, saying the organisation had failed to keep pace with a world that had become more interconnected and multipolar.

World.title: ‘Unacceptable’: India reacts after Russian strike injures Indian sailor on Black Sea ship

India has strongly condemned the attack on the MV ROYAD MAMMADOV in the Black Sea, which tragically resulted in the deaths of two foreign nationals

India on Monday condemned the attack on a civilian commercial vessel in the Black Sea as âcompletely unacceptableâ after a Russian drone strike reportedly killed two foreign nationals and injured crew members, including an Indian sailor.The vessel, MV ROYAD MAMMADOV, was attacked outside Romania's territorial waters, according to reports. Three Indian nationals were among the crew, with the Indian Embassy in Romania confirming that all three were safe and receiving medical care.One of the three Indians was injured in the attack and was being treated at ConstanÈa County Hospital. We have spoken to them. One of them has been injured and is receiving medical attention. We are in close touch with the hospital authorities. We are extending all possible support for the welfare and wellbeing of the Indian crew members,â the embassy said.External affairs minister S Jaishankar, speaking at the United Nations General Assembly, condemned attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers across major maritime routes.âNew challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. There have been attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea. Indian seafarers have lost their lives, as have others from other nations.
